description:
Head of Air and Space Media & Communications (RAF)

Ministry of Defence

Apply before 11:55 pm on Sunday 25th October 2026

 
Return to search results
Details
Reference number
478753
Salary
£95,000
Existing Civil Servants on level transfer will retain their existing base salary. Candidates on promotion will have their substantive base salary increased by 10% or start on the minimum of the SCS PB1 scale of £86,000 per annum; whichever is higher.​
A Civil Service Pension with an employer contribution of 28.97%
Job grade
SCS Pay Band 1
Contract type
Permanent
Business area
MOD - Military Strategic Headquarters
Type of role
Communications / Marketing
Senior leadership
Working pattern
Flexible working, Full-time
Number of jobs available

Contents
Location
About the job
Benefits
Things you need to know
Apply and further information
Location
This role is based at RAF High Wycombe, but regular attendance at MOD Main Building, London is required. There is an expectation that a minimum of 60% of working time will be spent in the office.
About the job
Job summary

In Air and Space Media and Communications, we have the privilege of telling impactful, engaging stories about the RAF that have an international reach, with the goal of increasing understanding of the role the RAF plays in protecting the nation, now and in the future. From the counter-drone operations in the Middle East to the defence of Space, we get to work on high profile and interesting campaigns that you don’t find elsewhere.

Our people are our most valued asset, and our internal communications are as important as those global media moments, As leader of this brilliant Whole Force team of Regulars, Reservists and Civilians, you will be their biggest champion and a passionate advocate for the Royal Air Force. It’s a challenging role that can be hugely demanding at times, but it’s also rewarding, exciting and fulfilling, crucial to positioning the RAF as part of a Joint global UK Defence narrative that deters our adversaries and celebrates our alliances. ​

Job description
Leadership of Air M&C, and professional leadership of the Communications function across the Air Command. ​
Represent Air M&C in senior relationships within RAF and externally with suppliers, MOD, Government Communications Service and professional bodies. Engagement with senior stakeholders on challenging topics is a critical part of this role, and you will need to build trust and credibility quickly. ​
Directing and delivering the RAF Communications Strategy, tracking the impact of our outputs against objectives on a quarterly basis and agreeing changes to our strategic direction as part of the RAF senior leadership team.​
Provide communications advice to the Air and Space Executive Committee.​
Full oversight of a complex operating model including internal and external communications, high profile content production and RAF ceremonial activities.  ​
Business management, including financial and resourcing modelling and forecasting, management of c£4m budget overall. ​
As required, deputise for Assistant Chief of Air Staff where required and provide cover for your colleagues, both as a senior member of the RAF, a senior Civilian in Air and a member of the MOD communications community. ​
Person specification
Strategic Communications Leadership
Extensive experience of developing and delivering impactful communications strategies within complex organisations, ensuring communications activity supports organisational objectives and adapts to changing priorities.
Senior Stakeholder Influence and Counsel
Proven ability to advise and influence senior stakeholders, building trusted relationships and providing strategic counsel on high-profile, complex and sensitive issues to achieve organisational objectives.
Leadership of High-Performing Teams
Demonstrable experience of leading and developing high-performing multidisciplinary teams, driving continuous improvement, building capability and fostering a collaborative and inclusive culture.
Strategic Judgement and Organisational Impact
Strong strategic thinking and communications judgement, with the ability to align communications activity to organisational priorities, balance competing demands and deliver measurable outcomes.
Leading Through Change and Ambiguity
Demonstrable resilience and adaptability, with experience of leading teams and communications activity through change, uncertainty and evolving priorities whilst maintaining focus, momentum and delivery.
Benefits
Alongside your salary of £95,000, Ministry of Defence contributes £27,521 towards you being a member of the Civil Service Defined Benefit Pension scheme. Find out what benefits a Civil Service Pension provides (opens in a new window).
Learning and development tailored to your role
An environment with flexible working options
A culture encouraging inclusion and diversity
A Civil Service pension with an employer contribution of 28.97%
Things you need to know
Artificial intelligence
Artificial intelligence can be a useful tool to support your application, however, all examples and statements provided must be truthful, factually accurate and taken directly from your own experience. Where plagiarism has been identified (presenting the ideas and experiences of others, or generated by artificial intelligence, as your own) applications may be withdrawn and internal candidates may be subject to disciplinary action. Please see our candidate guidance (opens in a new window) for more information on appropriate and inappropriate use.
Selection process details

To apply for this post, you will need to complete the online application process accessed via the Civil Service Jobs portal. This should be completed no later than 23:55 on 25th October 2026 and will involve providing the two documents which are weighted equally:

- A CV (no more than 2 pages) setting out your career history, with key responsibilities and achievements. Please ensure you have provided reasons for any gaps within the last two years.
- A Personal Statement (no more than 2 pages) providing tangible examples that clearly evidence how you meet the essential criteria for the role.

Air Vice-Marshal Cab Townsend is delighted to be hosting an informal online Q&A session on 20 October 2026, 15:00-15:30 to share more about the Head of Media & Communications (SCS1) role, the team, and the opportunities and challenges that come with it. There will also be plenty of time for your questions.​

You can join the session at this link. Attendance is completely optional and plays no part in the formal assessment process. If you experience any issues accessing the session, please contact Nicola.mcnamee100@mod.gov.uk.

External candidates who join the MOD and are new to the Civil Service will be subject to a six-month probation period.

For further information about the role and full application process, please refer to the candidate pack attached below. If you wish to receive any material in a different format for accessibility, then please contact People-CivHR-SCSCandidateSupport@mod.gov.uk.



Feedback will only be provided if you attend an interview or assessment.
This role has a minimum assignment duration of 3 years. An assignment duration is the period of time a Senior Civil Servant is expected to remain in the same post to enable them to deliver on the agreed key business outcomes. The assignment duration also supports your career through building your depth of expertise.

As part of accepting this role you will be agreeing to the expected assignment duration set out above. This will not result in a contractual change to your terms and conditions. Please note this is an expectation only, it is not something which is written into your terms and conditions or indeed which the employing organisation or you are bound by. It will depend on your personal circumstances at a particular time and business needs, for example, would not preclude any absence like family friendly leave. It is nonetheless an important expectation, which is why we ask you to confirm you agree to the assignment duration set out above.
Security
Successful candidates must meet the security requirements before they can be appointed. The level of security needed is security check (opens in a new window).

See our vetting charter (opens in a new window).
People working with government assets must complete baseline personnel security standard (opens in new window) checks.
Nationality requirements

This job is broadly open to the following groups:

UK nationals
nationals of the Republic of Ireland
nationals of Commonwealth countries who have the right to work in the UK
nationals of the EU, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland or Liechtenstein and family members of those nationalities with settled or pre-settled status under the European Union Settlement Scheme (EUSS) (opens in a new window)
nationals of the EU, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland or Liechtenstein and family members of those nationalities who have made a valid application for settled or pre-settled status under the European Union Settlement Scheme (EUSS)
individuals with limited leave to remain or indefinite leave to remain who were eligible to apply for EUSS on or before 31 December 2020
Turkish nationals, and certain family members of Turkish nationals, who have accrued the right to work in the Civil Service
Further information on nationality requirements (opens in a new window)
Working for the Civil Service
The Civil Service Code (opens in a new window) sets out the standards of behaviour expected of civil servants.

We recruit by merit on the basis of fair and open competition, as outlined in the Civil Service Commission's recruitment principles (opens in a new window).
The Civil Service embraces diversity and promotes equal opportunities. As such, we run a Disability Confident Scheme (DCS) for candidates with disabilities who meet the minimum selection criteria.
The Civil Service also offers a Redeployment Interview Scheme to civil servants who are at risk of redundancy, and who meet the minimum requirements for the advertised vacancy.
Diversity and Inclusion
The Civil Service is committed to attract, retain and invest in talent wherever it is found. To learn more please see the Civil Service People Plan (opens in a new window) and the Civil Service Diversity and Inclusion Strategy (opens in a new window).

About the job
Job summary

Can you demonstrate experience delivering regulatory or investigative services within a safety-critical, compliance, licensing, enforcement, transport, or public safety environment?

Have you successfully led complex incident investigations, managed casework, and produced high-quality evidence to support regulatory reporting or legal proceedings?

Are you confident using data, metrics, and analytical tools to identify trends, inform operational decisions, and improve regulatory outcomes?

If so, we’d love to hear from you!

This is an exciting opportunity to join a growing team at the forefront of improving safety, compliance, and public confidence. As part of a newly established role, you'll help shape the future direction of the function, working alongside skilled professionals on high-profile and impactful work. The team values innovation, collaboration, and continuous improvement, offering a supportive environment where you can influence outcomes, develop your expertise, and make a meaningful contribution from day one.

Joining our department comes with many benefits, including:

Employer pension contribution of 28.97% of your salary. Read more about Civil Service Pensions here
25 days annual leave, increasing by 1 day each year of service (up to a maximum of 30 days annual leave), plus 8 bank holidays a privilege day for the King’s birthday
Flexible working options where we encourage a great work-life balance.

Read more in the Benefits section below!

Find out more about what it's like working at DVSA.

Job description

Shape the future of transport in the UK. Join DVSA’s Connected and Automated Mobility Services (CAMS) team and play a key role in regulating the safe use of self-driving vehicles on Britain’s roads. As an In-Use Regulation Service (IURS) Investigation Specialist, you’ll lead complex investigations, influence the development of a pioneering regulatory framework, and work with government, industry, and enforcement partners. This is a unique opportunity to help deliver the future of road safety in a dynamic and high-profile environment

Your responsibilities will include, but aren’t limited to:

Support the development and implement the In-Use Regulation scheme for automated vehicles.
Support the delivery of the operational model and standard operating procedures (SOPs) for the IURS, including incident triage, case management, escalations, and closure.
Support in‑use reporting activities from Authorised Self Driving Entities (ASDEs) and No-User-in-Charge Operators (NUiCOs), working with DVSA Digital partners to maintain secure, compliant data flows and analytics.
Act as Senior Investigation Officer on multi‑disciplinary incident investigations (from traffic infractions to serious collisions), liaising with the Vehicle Certification Agency (CVA), law enforcement, local authorities, and statutory investigators.
Undertake and lead on investigations where the business dictates. This will include scoping the investigation/audit, conducting full and thorough investigations in-line with legislation and internal procedures, carrying out testing, and production of quality investigation reports.
Act as DVSA’s the IURS subject matter expert with the Department for Transport (DfT)/Centre for Connected and Autonomous Vehicles Senior Investigation Manager (Post Collison lead) IURS Investigation Specialist; 2025 01 19 v1 (CCAV), VCA, local authorities, operators, and other government bodies on IURS service matters and joint delivery.
Manage relationships with all internal and external stakeholders in order to meet the expectations and values of DVSA and the Civil Service.
Liaise with other Government Departments and Police Forces where their involvement in investigations is required and to facilitate the effective flow of intelligence within the law enforcement community.

For further information on the role, please read the role profile. Please note that the role profile is for information purposes only - whilst all elements are relevant to the role, they may not all be assessed during the recruitment process. This job advert will detail exactly what will be assessed during the recruitment process.

You can be based at any of the above locations, however if your chosen location is Yeading/Uxbridge please note:

This role is being advertised in Uxbridge, however the contractual base will be Yeading.

While estates work is being carried out in Yeading all posts are being temporarily based at Uxbridge. Successful applicants will start with us at our Uxbridge location.  

Please be aware that all employees will be required to work from the Yeading site once it reopens in 2028.

Employees based at Uxbridge will receive a London Weighting allowance of £4,000. This allowance will continue when the location moves to Yeading.

Person specification

You will be required to provide evidence that you hold any essential qualifications/licenses at some point during the recruitment process. If you cannot provide evidence, your application will be withdrawn.

Required experience:

To be successful in this role you will need to have the following experience:

Experience leading regulatory, criminal, or compliance investigations in safety-critical environments, managing casework and producing high-quality evidence-based reports.
Strong analytical skills, including using data, metrics, diagnostic tools, and sensitive evidential information to support robust regulatory decisions and investigations.
Excellent stakeholder management and communication skills, with experience working across government, industry, and enforcement partners, alongside developing capability in yourself and others.

Qualification/ Professional Memberships

Hold or be prepared to work towards Advanced Professional Certificate in Investigative Practice (or equivalent) covering evidence handling, interviewing, and case management.
A vocational related qualification in Motor Vehicle: Maintenance & Repair at level 3 or IMI ATA registration at diagnostic technician level or IRTEC registration at advanced technician level or Engtech registration.

Additional Information

Operational Delivery Profession (ODP) is the largest and most diverse professional community across the Civil Service. Many of us will have an association with several professional communities or specialisms, ODP applies to all public facing roles / or a role that is primarily aligned to supporting the work of those with public facing roles. All critical to the delivery of UK public services. 

Working hours, office attendance and travel requirements

Full time roles consist of 37 hours per week.

Whilst we welcome applications from those looking to work with us on a part time basis, there is a business requirement for the successful candidate to be able to work at least 30 hours per week.

This role is suitable for hybrid working, which is a non-contractual arrangement where a combination of workplace and home-based working can be accommodated subject to business requirements.

The expectation at present is a minimum of 60% of your working time a month will be spent at either your designated workplace (one of the locations cited in the advert) or, when required for business reasons, in another office/work location/visiting stakeholders. Your designated workplace will be your contractual place of work. There may be occasions where you are required to attend above the minimum expectation. 

Other Requirements:

About the job
Job summary

This is an exciting opportunity to be part of a new and dynamic team which will introduce a Verification Assurance Officer (VAO) job role within selected Jobcentre and Service Centres.

The role will enable the VAO and Jobcentre colleagues to work together to identify and tackle fraud on the frontline, responding to potential fraud quickly and effectively at the outset. The aim is to prevent fraud entering the welfare system, reduce customer debt and to meet Fraud, Error and Debt strategy and strategic objectives.  

As a VAO you will help improve the verification processes by strengthening our fraud controls on the front line. You will support the prevention of intentional fraud entering the welfare system, while actively increasing customer engagement and knowledge, educating them on their responsibilities.  

 As a great communicator you will also be responsible for raising Jobcentre colleagues' awareness of fraud and by providing practical support, making it clear that everyone has a responsibility to tackle fraud when they suspect it. 

Due to the nature of the work, you will be required to be carry out this role fully from a Jobcentre location, the critical part of the role will be interviewing claimants and collaborating with Jobcentre colleagues face to face, so hybrid and home working cannot be considered.

Job description

As a Verification Assurance Officer, your key tasks will be:

Work closely with Jobcentre and Service Centre colleagues conducting initial evidence interviews, further evidence interviews and verification activities by integrating within those teams in the sites. 
Conduct robust interviews where a colleague has a suspicion on the validity of documents produced for verification of Identification, housing costs, children and childcare costs elements of Universal Credit. 
Conduct review meetings with customers in scenarios where the Enhanced Review Team (ERT) and the customer have agreed to bring in evidence relating to their claim to a Jobcentre. 
Provide regular feedback at office meetings on trends, patterns of fraud, and how to detect them. Feed information into specialist risk and intelligence teams within DWP.
Lead customer education sessions jointly with Jobcentre colleagues to provide clarity on customer responsibilities and the consequences of non-compliance. 
Collate and maintain accurate Management Information (MI) as directed by analysts and performance teams. 

 Frequent travel between sites may be required depending on business needs. 

Person specification

The successful candidates will need to demonstrate: 

They are highly skilled in customer engagement and conducting effective face to face interviews, able to build rapport and gather relevant information. (First Lead criteria)
They work at pace, often to tight deadlines, whilst maintaining a focus on continuous improvement and identifying new ways of working. (Second lead criteria)
Proven people engagement skills, including collaborative working relationships with colleagues and stakeholders across wider teams and organisations.
Excellent verbal, written communication and organisation skills.

Selection process details
This vacancy is using Success Profiles (opens in a new window), and will assess your Behaviours, Strengths, Ability and Experience.

**Ensure that you read the full information about the selection process thoroughly before starting your application**. Please note the closing date for your full application (Application Form, Tests and Written Statements) is 23:55 on 27th October 2026**

Stage 1 – Application Form 

Please complete the application form with your basic information, which includes your personal details, eligibility to apply and any reasonable adjustments required.

Stage 2 – Online Test

Following submission of your Application Form, you will be invited to complete Work Strengths Tests.

Please complete the online tests as soon as possible (within 24 - 48 hours is recommended). You will need to allow at least one hour to complete the test plus time to complete your written application (see below for details). Guidance and a practice test will be available when you are invited to take the test. The tests are administered online and accessed via the Civil Service Jobs website.

You will be directed to the Talogy - True Talent – Scheduled Maintenance Window Webpage for online tests during an outage.

Our online test supplier will be performing scheduled maintenance between 12pm and 1pm on 25th October 2026. You will be unable to access tests during this period.

If you are in the middle of a test when the maintenance begins, your progress will be paused. You will be able to resume your test from where you left off via your application centre once the downtime has ended. Please note that you will not be able to launch any new tests while the system is offline.

Stage 3 - Curriculum Vitae (CV) 

You will be asked to complete a CV with details of your job history, full qualification details, previous skills and experience. You are not required to upload your personal CV. 

In the previous skills/experience section you should detail your employment and/or education history relevant to this vacancy (we recommend a maximum of 500 words). 

The CV will also cover your work history (we recommend you include up to the last 3 roles of employment history, plus any others that you feel are relevant) and your qualifications. 

Your CV will not be formally assessed, so please put the main evidence of your skills into your Personal Statement. Your CV will be used to add context to your personal statement. 

Stage 4 – Personal Statement and Sift

If you pass the test with the required scores, you will also be asked to complete a personal statement in no more than 750 words detailing the relevant skills and experience you can bring to the role, based on the Person Specification listed.

Please read and understand the Person Specification thoroughly, as this is what your written evidence will be assessed against. Pay particular attention to the lead criteria and second lead criteria as if you do not demonstrate this on your application, you will not progress to the interview stage.

Your layout is entirely your preference; you may choose narrative, bullets, etc. You may choose to address each criterion separately; however, one narrative example may cover and evidence several key criteria. You may not be able to meet all the key criteria, but please ensure you evidence the key personal requirements, what have you done that’s relatable to the requirements. You don’t have to explain the whole process, just what you have done and the skills and experience you have used. 

If you do not have work-based examples then please give examples from school/college, clubs, volunteering or other activities you have been involved in. 

Should a large number of applications be received, an initial sift may be conducted using the first lead criteria or both the first lead and second criteria. If so, we will sift on: 

They are highly skilled in customer engagement and conducting effective face to face interviews, able to build rapport and gather relevant information. (First Lead criteria)
They work at pace, often to tight deadlines, whilst maintaining a focus on continuous improvement and identifying new ways of working. (Second Lead criteria)

Candidates who pass the initial sift may be progressed to a full sift or progressed straight to an interview.

In the event we don’t receive a high number of applications we may not undertake a sift and progress all candidates to interview. For these reasons, the timeline is subject to change depending on the approach we take.  

**The closing date for all stages of your application is 23:55 on 27/10/2026. If you fail to complete all stages before the deadline, your application will be withdrawn**

The sift is scheduled to be held from 02/11/2026 to 13/11/2026. These dates may be subject to change.

Following completion of the sifting period above, results will be collated, and candidates will receive confirmation of the outcome. Those candidates who have met the agreed pass mark will be invited to interview. No feedback will be provided at this stage.

Stage 5 - Interview 

If you pass the written application sift with the required score, you will be invited to a blended interview and will receive an electronic notification to your Civil Service Jobs account. 

If high application volumes are received, the benchmark / score for candidates to proceed to the interview stage may be raised.

The interviews will be conducted face to face. Where possible the interviews will take place in Exeter, Guildford and Swindon, however candidates may be expected to travel to an alternative location as required.

If you require any reasonable adjustments to attend a face-to-face interview, please ensure you state those on your application form when asked to do so.

Interviews are scheduled to take place from 07/12/2026 to 18/12/2026. Please note that these dates are only indicative at this stage and could be subject to change.

Communications will be electronic and/or by SMS/telephone; therefore, it is important that you check your Civil Service Jobs account regularly, as well as your spam/junk email folder. Telephone calls may show as a withheld number, it is important that you answer so that your interview can be confirmed. If you wish to opt out of SMS messages, please email this address, including the vacancy reference and your candidate ID CFCD.RECRUITMENTINBOX@DWP.GOV.UK. As part of our commitment to improving the candidate experience, you may be contacted during the recruitment process to provide feedback.

Preparing for the Interview 

The interview will take approximately 30 to 40 minutes and will consist of behaviour and strength-based questions. A blended interview aims to be more of a conversation offering a more inclusive approach. The questions explore what you, the candidate, can and have done, but also your potential.   

Behaviours

You will be assessed against the Civil Service Behaviours listed at Executive Officer – Level 2. An example of a behavioural question would be “Tell me about a time when you have had to deal with a difficult customer.”

It may help to use one or more examples of a piece of work you have completed, or a situation you have been in, and use the WHO or STAR model to explain:

WHO - What it was, How you approached the work/situation and what the Outcomes were, what did you achieve? or  
STAR - What was the Situation? What were the Tasks? What Action did you take?  What were the Results of your actions? 

Strengths

It is difficult to prepare for strength type questions. However, you can think through your answers, focus on your achievements and aspects you enjoy and decide how these can be applied in the organisation and role. While strengths questions are shorter and we do not expect a full STAR response, the panel is interested in your first reaction to the question and information or reasoning to support this.

If you do not have work-based examples then please give examples from school/college, clubs, volunteering or other activities you have been involved in.   

If you withdraw your application at any stage, it will not progress further.  

Stage 5 – Offer

Once all interviews have been completed, you will be notified of the outcome by email. Our current plan is that this will be week commencing 11/01/2027, but this may be subject to change. Offers will be made in strict merit order to the highest scoring candidate first based on your location preferences and the geographical requirements of the business. Dependent on your position on the merit list, if none of your location preferences remain at the point we make a job offer, we may offer you a role at an alternative advertised location. Integrity, Plagiarism and Civil Service Principles 

The Civil Service values honesty and integrity and expects all candidates to abide by these principles. Please ensure that all examples provided in your application are taken directly from your own experience and that you describe the examples in your own words. Examples of plagiarism can include:

Presenting the work, ideas and experiences of others as your own.

 Disclosure and Barring Service and Internal Fraud Database Checks

To process applications without delay, we will be sending a Criminal Record Check to Disclosure and Barring Service on your behalf. 

However, we recognise in exceptional circumstances some candidates will want to send their completed forms direct. If you will be doing this, please advise Government Recruitment Service of your intention by emailing Pre-EmploymentChecks.grs@cabinetoffice.gov.uk stating the job reference number in the subject heading.  

If successful and transferring from another Government Department a criminal record check will be carried out.

This check also applies to employees who resign or otherwise leave before being dismissed for fraud or dishonesty had their employment continued. Any candidate’s details held on the IFD will be refused employment. Political Impartiality​

Due to the nature of our role, DWP is required to ensure that the political impartiality of its employees cannot be brought into question. The role you are applying for is classed by DWP as a ‘sensitive’ role because it involves contact with the public, so permission cannot be given to anyone in such a role to engage or remain politically active in any kind of local councillor role. There may also be restrictions applied to other political activities which are set out in the Department’s Standards of Behaviour Policy which is underpinned by the Civil Service Management Code. You may therefore wish to decide at application stage whether, if your job application was successful, there would be a conflict of interest with any political activity role you have and whether, knowing the restrictions we necessarily apply as an employer, you wish to pursue your application with DWP. Job description

This role will involve regular travel across South Central and the East of England, with occasional trips into London. Some overnight stays may also be required.

Overview of the job       

The National Security Division (NSD) is formed of 5 regional units across England and Wales. Each National Security Unit (NSU) is responsible for the management of national security and national interest probation cases outside of the Probation Service (PS) regional structures. The units are: 

•            North of England

•            Midlands

•            Wales and the South West 

•            East and South Central 

•            London, Kent, Surrey and Sussex 

Each unit has operational satellite locations and consists of a combination of office and remote based working. 

The operational function comprises of a team who deliver enhanced sentence management to Terrorist Convicted/Connected cases (TACT), Terrorist Risk (TR), Critical Public Protection Cases (CPPC) and Serious Organised Crime cases (SOC) assessed as posing the highest threat/highest harm throughout England and Wales, and who require a national response to sentence management. 

The NSD Senior Operational Lead supports the Head of National Security Division working to the Director for the National Security Division, accountable to the Chief Probation Officer, to provide operational leadership within a regional National Security Unit. 

The NSD Senior Operational Lead is responsible for operational management and oversight of critical cases under the supervision of the Probation Service, ensuring that an enhanced level of sentence management is delivered. 

The job holder will have direct line management responsibility for both operational and administrative staff within the unit.

Summary           

Delivery of risk management within this team presents challenges and complexities outside of the usual experience of Team Managers/Senior Probation Practitioners. The job holder will require a high level of resilience and an understanding of national priorities to oversee the significant levels of ministerial and media scrutiny this cohort of cases attract. They will need to be confident presenting to senior HMPPS staff as well as senior officers in partnership agencies. 

The job holder is responsible for the day-to-day delivery of all operational aspects of their function within National Security Division. This requires a high level of operational knowledge of probation work and national priorities to be able to effectively line manage Probation Practitioners who are working to enhanced national standards. 

The job holder will be expected to manage and lead a geographically dispersed team of staff within a specialised team to deliver enhanced management of terrorist offenders, serious organised criminals and other critical public protection cases who present a national threat. This includes maintaining the delivery of function across a national landscape. 

The job holder will need to acquire and maintain an understanding of all relevant departments across HMPPS and Department of Security including: Probation Regions, Joint Extremism Unit, Serious Organised Crime Unit and other relevant departments.

They will need to demonstrate an ability to broker and maintain operational relationships with HMPPS colleagues and law enforcement partners at senior operational grades.      

The job holder must at all times demonstrate a commitment to equality and inclusion and an understanding of their relevance to the work they do, in line with wider Probation Service (PS) policies and procedures and in accordance with a specific understanding of the NSD cohorts of offenders.

If relevant to the role, some out of hours working may be required.

Responsibilities, Activities & Duties 

The job holder will be required to carry out the following responsibilities, activities and duties:

•            Provide direct Line Management to a geographically dispersed specialist team of practitioners to deliver enhanced national standards to national security and critical public protection cases, which include TACT convicted, TACT concern, terrorist risk, high threat and high harm Serious Organised Crime nominals and most critical, highest profile CPPC cases. 

•            The job holder is required to demonstrate an awareness of operational and reputational risk and be accountable for the quality delivery of good practice and team performance. They will be required to identify areas for improvement within policy and enhanced national standards in line with gold standard practice through quality assuring all assessments completed with the National Security Division.

•            Be alert to fast changing political climate and responsive to both National and International Security information to effectively manage risk posed by cases held in the National Security Division.  

•            To access, interpret, analyse and apply performance data pro-actively in order to maximise National Security Division/team performance, evaluate practice and deliver organisational aims and provide operational assurance to Head of National Security Unit and Head of Performance and Quality.  Support the division by ensuring accurate performance data is reported, and cases of concern are identified and escalated as required.

•            Represent the Unit/Division in national and regional multi-agency and cross government department meetings which may involve undertaking specific areas of responsibility as delegated by the Head of National Security Unit to support national portfolio projects. 

•            To proactively manage staff development, issues of underperformance, attendance, health and safety, employee relations and diversity matters. Adopt a consistent, fair and objective standpoint when making decisions in relation to individual staff issues.

•            Develop and maintain relationships with operational counterparts in Probation regions and national/regional HMPPS departments such as JExU, SOCU, PPG.  This may include developing and delivering training and continuous professional development activity with internal and external stakeholders.  

•            Carry out safeguarding children and adults duties in accordance with the PS statutory responsibilities and agency policies and robustly demonstrate the need for safeguarding in the national security landscape.

•            Promote, chair and develop a core group approach to support MAPPA, incorporating a range of specialist operational functions including psychologists, polygraph leads and relevant external stakeholders. 

•            Represent the National Security Division by engaging with internal and external partners and attending regional partnership forums such as MARSOC, Pathfinder and Prevent Boards for a multi-agency delivery of service.

•            Ensure the appropriate handling of highly sensitive information/intelligence.

•            Provide input into regional and national conferences, showcasing the work of the National Security Division, identifying opportunities for operational innovation and delivery whilst providing consultation for sentence/risk management where appropriate.   

The duties/responsibilities listed above describe the post as it is at present and is not intended to be exhaustive. The job holder is expected to accept reasonable alterations and additional tasks of a similar level that may be necessary. Significant adjustments may require re-examination under the Job Evaluation Scheme and shall be discussed in the first instance with the job holder. This is particularly pertinent given the relatively new formation of the national security division and the evolving nature of the work. 

An ability to fulfil all spoken aspects of the role with confidence through the medium of English or (where specified in Wales) Welsh.

Summary

The post holder will be part of the Divisional Performance and Quality team.
 
They will work in partnership with divisional /local managers, practice tutor assessors and operational staff to promote high quality work through delivery of quality assurance and improvement activities including: audit and analysis, practice workshops, coaching and providing support to colleagues.
 
In line with NPS policies and procedures, the post holder must at all times demonstrate a commitment to equality and inclusion and an understanding of their relevance to the work they do.

• Deliver practice improvement workshops and briefings to POs and PSOs, and review the impact of these on practice
• Support the re-launch and deployment of Skills for Effective Engagement Development and Supervision (SEEDS)

• As agreed with local managers, provide coaching and support to groups of staff whose roles are changing

• Carry out safeguarding children and safeguarding adult duties in accordance with the NPS statutory responsibilities and agency policies
• Demonstrate and promote pro-social modelling skills by consistently reinforcing pro-social behaviour and attitudes and challenging anti-social behaviour and attitudes

About the job
Job summary
Please refer to Job Description
Job description

Proud to serve. Proud to keep justice going

The role of the legal adviser is vital to the smooth running of HM Courts and Tribunals Service (HMCTS) and is a highly rewarding position within our organisation. You’ll be surrounded by learning opportunities every day, so if you have a passion for law, this could be the right role for you.

About us

Our work at HMCTS is vitally important to the smooth running of a fair, accessible and efficient justice system, as we are responsible for the administration of criminal, civil and family courts and tribunals in England and Wales. Right now, we’re looking for trainee legal advisers to join our exceptional legal team and develop the skills to provide magistrates with advice on points of law, practice and procedure, and assist with the formulation and drafting of the reasons behind their judgments

Important: 

It is essential in understanding the unique nature of this role that prospective applicants visit a Magistrates’ Court to observe court proceedings before the interview stage of the process- if successful in reaching that stage.  Candidates are encouraged to plan ahead because the time period between confirmation and date of interview may be limited and interviews may not proceed if an observation has not been made. The observation provides valuable insight into the duties of a Trainee Legal Adviser and offers a practical understanding of the courtroom environment, as well as the various roles and responsibilities involved. Those who have undertaken this experience often report increased confidence and motivation to excel in the role.

About You

To be eligible to apply for this post, you must have passed the academic stage of qualification to become a solicitor or Barrister of the Senior Courts of England and Wales or a Fellow of the Chartered Institute of Legal Executives (CILEX) or CILEX Lawyer. Please refer to the entry requirement section for more information.

You’re an excellent communicator with the ability to inspire confidence in everyone you work with and the self-assurance to speak in court.  You’re enthusiastic about the responsibility that comes with being on the front line of the justice system. And now you're ready to take your career to the next level and make a positive difference to society and the communities we live in.

Learn new legal skills as you develop your career

When you join us as a trainee legal adviser, you’ll quickly discover that this isn’t your normal 9 to 5 role, as no two days are the same. You’ll learn new skills every day as you work at pace in a fast-moving, fluid environment, and help to keep the courts running smoothly and efficiently. Working on everything from minor motoring offences to serious crimes, you’ll be supported and mentored throughout your two-year training period. Once you’ve completed this, you’ll then have the opportunity to further develop your legal career within HMCTS. 

Work as the qualified, professional face of the courts

 

Rather than acting for a client you’ll be offering impartial and objective legal advice, so you’ll need to be passionate about the law and the issues that must be considered when magistrates are delivering judgments and sentences.

Helping to conduct case management hearings will be another key part of your role, as will liaising with outside agencies who are involved in specialist court work. Once you’re qualified, you’ll act as the professional face of the court, so we’ll expect you to work with integrity, empathy and understanding, and ensure that everyone who attends is treated with humanity and respect at all times.

Apply all your skills as you increase your knowledge of the law

In addition to your academic qualifications and excellent communication skills, you’ll be committed to increasing and maintaining your knowledge of the law. Open, approachable, professional and supportive, we’ll expect you to have excellent problem-solving skills and the ability to think on your feet in a busy court. Important decisions will be made, and these can have a profound effect on the people who come to court, so you’ll be confident, impartial and capable of considering a wide range of risks and implications. Flexible and adaptable, and with a high degree of personal responsibility, there are times when you’ll be faced with challenging situations. With this in mind you’ll be resilient and remain calm under pressure and have a diplomatic and tactful approach to everyone you work with.

This is an office based/court based frontline role. You’ll be allocated to your work base location that has been agreed between yourself and line manager as part of the recruitment process.

You’ll be expected to spend the duration of your training at your agreed base location to fulfil the demands of the training and the business needs in that location.

All our employees have to be security cleared before being appointed so you’ll undergo a vetting process if your application is successful.

Enjoy a healthy work/life balance with our range of benefits

When you join us, you’ll be making an important contribution to HM Courts and Tribunals Service – but how will we help you in return?

In addition to a competitive salary, generous holiday entitlement and a Civil Service pension, we’ll support your development with training opportunities to help you advance your career with us. We also understand the importance of a healthy work/life balance and with this in mind we offer flexible working schemes, paid maternity and paternity leave and excellent childcare benefits.

The vital work we do takes an incredible community of colleagues with different skills, backgrounds, cultures and identities. We support every individual, so you’ll always know you’re welcome and valued. We have strong and proactive staff networks, reasonable adjustments for those who need them and diversity talent programmes to help everyone, irrespective of their background, to achieve their potential.

Your benefits with us 

As part of our training we support qualifying work experience for the SRA and CILEX enabling legal professional qualification as a solicitor or CILEX.

This role is being offered on a Permanent basis. This role has a minimum assignment duration of 3 years – in line with the deliverables outlined within the advert.  Please note this is an expectation only, it is not something that is written into your terms and conditions or indeed which the employing organisation or you are bound by.

Upon successful completion of the full training and submission of your training portfolio (usually completed within two years), a Trainee legal adviser will then progress to a SEO Tier 1 Legal adviser role (with the associated increase in pay, in line with the HMCTS Legal adviser Tier Progression Framework). You’ll have access to a variety of legal careers in HMCTS and beyond.  As part of the Ministry of Justice, you’ll be entitled to a range of benefits including a civil service pension, flexible working arrangements, generous annual leave, childcare and travel allowances and numerous staff networks and clubs. For further information on our benefits please select here Why join us - HM Courts & Tribunals service

Entry Requirements

To be eligible to apply for this post, you must have passed the academic stage of qualification to become a solicitor or Barrister of the Senior Courts of England and Wales or a Fellow of the Chartered Institute of Legal Executives (CILEX) or CILEX Lawyer by virtue of —

(i)            having passed the necessary examinations; (example of which are listed below)

(ii)          having been granted an exemption in relation to the necessary examinations (example of which are listed below) by the appropriate examining body; or

(iii)         any combination of the two.

By way of example, the following list reflects the currently approved academic qualification routes.

·         The Legal Practice Course (LPC) for Solicitors, or BOTH the SQE1 and SQE2 stages of the Solicitors Qualifying Exam; or 

·         The Bar Training Course; or equivalent for Barristers; or 

·         The CILEx Level 3 Professional Diploma in Law and Practice and the CILEx Level 6 Diploma in Law and Practice; or

·         The CILEx Graduate Fast Track Diploma; or equivalent for Graduate Membership of CILEx.

Important Information for Bar-Qualified Candidates

HMCTS welcomes applications from candidates who have completed the Bar Training Course (BTC) or an equivalent qualification.

Please note that this recruitment campaign is separate from HMCTS's future pupillage provision.

Candidates whose primary objective is to obtain pupillage should note that HMCTS expects to advertise pupillage opportunities through a separate recruitment campaign from 2027, that will be promoted through the Pupillage Gateway, and Civil Service Jobs, with applications submitted through Civil Service Jobs. Details of that campaign will be published separately.

Successful appointment through this campaign will not lead to, guarantee, or provide access to pupillage within HMCTS.

 

You can apply for this role whilst you are completing the final academic stage of qualification but must be able to evidence your final certification at the point of an offer being made, to be able to proceed to appointment.

If you are unable to evidence the correct certification at the point of offer, you will be removed from the process. Training HMCTS delivers a bespoke training programme for trainee legal advisers to develop the skills, and knowledge for the legal adviser role. The training is delivered through a variety of methods, and you will be supported by an allocated mentor to guide them throughout the Induction and Training Programme. You will be required to attend a two-day Induction Programme run by the Judicial College which is followed by supplementary training in the workplace and the completion of modules contained in the Judicial College’s legal adviser Manual. This learning will be enhanced by relevant court observations and additional local and regional training events with peers.

About the job
Job summary

Would you like to join a close-knit and encouraging team of in-house designers creating work for the Royal Air Force?  

We are Air Media Centre, the in-house design studio and print department for HQ Air Command. Our work includes design consultancy across branding, design, multimedia, and print; video, animation, and motion graphics production; digital and print-based design; and the production of printed material that ranges from operational documents to communication and engagement material.  

You will work on a wide range of creative briefs, from small campaigns to one-off projects, all within the framework of our brand guidelines. These could include video, animation/motion graphics, infographics and digital, including short-form content for social media, as well as print. Our work focuses on telling engaging stories, to both our internal and external audiences.  

You will lead your own projects (with line management support), coordinating timeframes and working closely with both civilian and military staff. Within our established design studio, we will give you the opportunity and support to develop your technical skills. In addition to the exciting and rewarding design work you’ll encounter, we provide first class Learning and Development opportunities for your personal and professional development.  

If you have lots of exciting, fresh ideas, and would like to join us as a Video Producer and Multimedia Designer, do apply!

This position is advertised at 37 hours per week. 

Job description

Main requirements of the post: 

Work as part of a team with designers, digital printers, and our wider RAF Media and Communications colleagues, to deliver creative solutions that meet the needs of our clients from across the Royal Air Force. 
Apply design thinking, collaborating closely with RAF Media and Communications colleagues, videographers, clients and stakeholders to discuss and understand the business objectives and requirements of the project. 
Interpret and analyse the client’s business needs, understanding the audience, considering practical and innovative solutions and developing creative ideas/concepts to deliver the message.  
Create work to the agreed timeframes, adhering to copyright law, Defence brand rules, design standards and accessibility guidelines. 
Evaluate client feedback and apply lessons learnt.  
Deliver excellent customer service, demonstrating an understanding of client’s priorities and constraints.  
Occasional ad-hoc travel to RAF sites for filming. 
Person specification

Essential criteria: 

Minimum of a QCF Level 5 qualification in a design or media-related subject (DipHE, foundation degree, HND or equivalent). 
In-depth knowledge of industry-standard software (i.e. Adobe CC, including After Effects and Premiere Pro). 
Excellent video, animation, and motion graphics skills.  
Excellent typographic and layout skills.  
Good written and verbal communication skills. 
Experience of clarifying client objectives and planning a design approach. 
Experience of communicating clearly, with confidence, to present and explain ideas to clients.  
Good team working skills.  
Desire to constantly develop and improve yourself.

About the job
Job summary

We are delighted to advertise this role within RAF Digital. RAF Digital supports the delivery of enhanced freedom of action in the Air and Space domains through data exploitation and digital agility, supporting today’s RAF and driving the journey to the Next Generation RAF.

This is an exciting opportunity for a motivated and organised individual to join RAF Digital at the centre of the RAF’s digital transformation activity. The role sits within the RAF Digital Portfolio Office and supports delivery of the Air & Space Digital Plan (ASDP), helping to maintain portfolio control, strengthen governance, improve management information and support senior decision-making.

We are delighted to advertise this role within RAF Digital. The role will help maintain accurate portfolio information, support governance and reporting, improve data quality and provide reliable day-to-day support to portfolio management activity.

This position is advertised at 37 hours per week. 

Job description

You will play a key role in supporting the successful delivery of the Air & Space Digital Plan (ASDP), helping RAF Digital maintain oversight, control and assurance across a diverse portfolio of digital activity. Working at the heart of the RAF Digital Portfolio Office, you will provide critical support to governance, reporting, portfolio management and decision-making processes, ensuring senior leaders have the insight they need to deliver digital transformation effectively.

You will support the successful delivery of the ASDP, helping RAF Digital maintain accurate, timely and decision-ready portfolio information. Working within the RAF Digital Portfolio Office and under the direction of the Senior Programme Support Officer, you will support governance, reporting, portfolio controls and continuous improvement, ensuring teams and senior leaders receive reliable information to support delivery and decision-making.

This role offers the opportunity to work across a wide range of programmes, projects and stakeholders. You will develop practical experience in portfolio management, governance, digital tooling and management information while helping RAF Digital improve its ways of working.

Support the Senior Programme Support Officer in maintaining a coherent, decision-ready portfolio view across ASDP Lines of Effort, ensuring plans, priorities, milestones and delivery pressures are accurately reflected in portfolio products.
Maintain and quality assure portfolio data across risk management tool, the ASDP workbook, portfolio management tooling, dashboards and associated reporting products, ensuring information is accurate, current and suitable for decision-making.
Collate and validate management information covering delivery confidence, performance, cost, schedule, risks, issues, assumptions, dependencies, decisions and benefits.
Provide secretariat and coordination support to RAF Digital governance forums, including preparing agendas and packs, recording actions and decisions, tracking follow-up activity and maintaining appropriate records.
Produce routine and ad hoc reports, dashboards and analysis using Microsoft 365, Excel, Power BI and other approved tools to support portfolio insight, governance and prioritisation.
Engage with Lines of Effort, project and programme teams to improve data quality, PMCF maturity and consistency of portfolio reporting, escalating gaps or blockers through the Senior Programme Support Officer where required.
Support portfolio processes including risk, issue and dependency tracking, benefits and outcomes reporting, demand management, prioritisation and maintenance of the ASDP delivery pipeline.
Support RAF Digital-led Microsoft Copilot portfolio activity, including licence administration, demand tracking, onboarding coordination, usage reporting, adoption monitoring, communications and benefits evidence, under the direction of the Senior Programme Support Officer.
Support continuous improvement across Portfolio Office processes, reporting, automation, guidance and digital tooling, capturing lessons and helping implement agreed improvements.

Essential

Experience of supporting administrative, project, programme, portfolio, governance or business management activity, or the ability to develop quickly in these areas.

Good communication and stakeholder engagement skills, with the ability to build positive working relationships across teams.
Confident use of Microsoft 365 applications, including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Teams and SharePoint.
Good analytical and organisational skills, including the ability to maintain accurate information, identify gaps and produce clear reports or management information.
An understanding of risk, issue, dependency, benefits or performance reporting, or a willingness and ability to learn.
Ability to work collaboratively, support colleagues and contribute to continuous improvement in a busy delivery environment.
Equality & Diversity training, or willingness to complete all required mandatory training.

Experience of a risk management tool or a similar project, programme or portfolio management information system.
Experience of supporting governance meetings, maintaining action logs, preparing briefings, dashboards or reports.
Awareness of benefits management, risk management, change management or management information reporting.
Experience of Microsoft Copilot adoption, digital productivity, licence administration, user engagement or change activity.

About the job
Job summary

Would you like to make a difference to UK Defence by applying your Occupational Psychology skills and experience?  Would you like to work flexibly, have a generous holiday entitlement and contributory pension, and support for at least five days of professional and personal development each year? If so, this could be the role for you.

This is an exciting opportunity to join the Occupational Psychology Team at Air & Space Command. The role of the Air & Space HQ Occupational Psychology Team is to apply professional skills and knowledge to deliver outputs relevant to stakeholders in order that they can make evidence-based policy decisions. Whilst the RAF purpose is to deliver Air and Space Power for the UK this cannot be achieved without a focus on people and harnessing their potential.

Our work focuses on designing and delivering RAF specific aptitude testing, understanding the attitudes of RAF People and how these might shape their behaviours and decision making, and providing consultancy-based services for bespoke people requirements. Our work encompasses the Whole Force (Regulars, Reserves and Civil Servants) as well as families of serving personnel.

You will join the MOD Occupational Psychology profession which is part of the wider Government Occupational Psychology Profession (a recognised government specialist profession). The profession comprises over 250 members across all the major government departments and many agencies and arms-length bodies – which makes us the largest Occupational Psychology community in the U.K. We are a vibrant community with a long history in government going as far back as, at least, World War II, as shown in the Fifty Years of Occupational Psychology in Britain.

This position is advertised at 37 hours per week.

Job description

Responsibilities

The post holder will support the Principal Occupational Psychologist in the design, delivery and validation of computer Based Aptitude Testing for RAF specific critical roles. Act as technical Lead for the Continuous Attitude Surveys within the RAF.  Deliver bespoke research as commissioned by RAF stakeholders and wider Defence.

Key Duties

Support Computer Based Aptitude Testing

Support the Principal Psychologist with needs analysis to inform Computer Based Aptitude tests and wider psychological assessment practice.

Conduct research, statistical analysis and development to support the design, development, implementation and evaluation of the aptitude tests for RAF led personnel selection.

Technical Lead for RAF Continuous Attitude Surveys

Oversee the delivery and quality of the RAF Continuous Attitude Surveys acting as Technical Lead to ensure the robustness, utility and dissemination of results.

Research and development

Conduct research as directed by the research agenda and act as Technical Lead for research conducted by trainee occupational psychologists.
Apply the occupational psychology consultancy cycle to address people issues as prioritised.
Design and deliver interventions applying an evidence-based approach and evaluating interventions to assess their utility.
Collaborate with other psychologists and SMEs from other disciplines to develop solutions to People issues.
Collaborate with other psychologists and SMEs from other disciplines to develop solutions to People issues.

Drawing together different evidence sources to support evidence-based decision making and draw out the psychological implications of findings.
Providing technical advice and review of relevant evidence and research.
Collaborating with colleagues in other teams and being willing to learn from these experiences.

Job summary

Do you have a passion for training delivery and developing people? We are looking for a motivated and enthusiastic individual to join the Specialist Training School (STS) as a Specialist Trainer in Environmental Protection (EP).

This is an exciting opportunity to deliver engaging Environmental Protection training that directly supports Defence capability, assurance, and continuous improvement. Working alongside military personnel and a wide range of Defence stakeholders, you will help shape learner success, influence professional standards, and make a tangible difference across Defence.

Based at RAF Halton under the RAF Safety Centre, STS delivers high-quality Health and Safety, Environmental Protection, and Quality Management training across the UK and overseas. While experience in training delivery is desirable, we welcome applications from individuals who can demonstrate the skills, knowledge, and potential to succeed in the role. Full support will be provided to develop the required training and professional qualifications.

This role offers the opportunity to build expertise in EP while broadening your experience across other specialist training disciplines. If you are looking for a rewarding career where you can develop others, contribute to operational excellence, and be part of a professional and supportive team, we would love to hear from you.

This position is advertised at 37 hours per week. 

Job description

As a Specialist Trainer (Environmental Protection) within the Specialist Training School (STS), you will be responsible for delivering high-quality training that supports Defence capability, assurance, and continuous improvement. Reporting to the Training Delivery Manager, you will deliver training in accordance with JSP 822, DSAT principles, and approved training specifications, ensuring learners achieve the required knowledge, skills, and competencies.

You will deliver EP training across Defence, both at RAF Halton and at locations throughout the UK and overseas, maintaining the highest standards of professionalism, learner engagement, and training excellence.

Key Responsibilities:

Deliver EP and associated specialist training in accordance with approved Training Objectives, Learning Specifications (LSpecs), Assessment Strategies (AStrat), and Assessment Specifications (ASpec).
Plan, prepare, and facilitate training activities using approved course materials and contemporary delivery methods to maximise learner engagement and achievement.
Assess learners through formative and summative assessment activities, maintaining accurate records and ensuring results are processed within required timescales.
Act as a Subject Matter Expert, contributing to the review, maintenance, and continuous improvement of training content to ensure compliance with current legislation, Defence policy, and organisational requirements.
Work collaboratively with Training Managers, the Training Design Office, and Training Support staff to maintain the quality, accuracy, and currency of training documentation.
Prepare and maintain training facilities, equipment, and learning resources, ensuring safe and effective delivery both on-site and at remote locations.
Maintain professional competence through continuous professional development, remaining current in Environmental requirements, Defence policy, and training best practice.
Support the delivery of training assurance activities, including participation in trainer observations, quality reviews, and continuous improvement initiatives.
Deliver training at Defence establishments across the UK and overseas, including regular off-site travel where required.
Support wider Specialist Training School activities, projects, and business requirements as directed by the Training Manager or Officer Commanding STS.

Additional Responsibilities:

Maintain compliance with all STS Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), Defence policies, and mandatory training requirements.
Manage travel, accommodation, and administrative requirements associated with training delivery in accordance with MOD policy.
Contribute to the development and sharing of best practice across the Specialist Training School and wider Defence training community.
Support the delivery of other specialist training disciplines, including Health and Safety and Quality Management, where appropriately qualified and trained.

This role offers a unique opportunity to influence Defence capability through the delivery of high-quality training while developing expertise across multiple specialist disciplines within the RAF Safety Centre.

Level 3 Award in Education and Training (formally PTTLS).

Knowledge and understanding of technology enhanced learning (TEL)
Proficient in Microsoft Office 365 Suite including Word, Excel, Forms and PowerPoint.
Military background or knowledge

Job description

HMPPS Band 4

The National Crime in Prison (CiP) team is dedicated to improving justice outcomes for crimes committed within the prison estate. The Area Crime in Prison Coordinator (ACiPCo) position provides an opportunity to support prisons through an area-specific, mobile, peripatetic model- delivering targeted support across the estate.

These roles are specifically designed to strengthen capability and build resilience within establishments by providing temporary, needs-led support to either single prisons and/or clusters of prisons. Unlike permanent establishment-based CiPCo roles, post holders will be deployed to specific establishments or clusters for defined periods, supporting the development of sustainable processes, improving adherence to the Crime in Prison Referral Agreement (CiPRA), and embedding effective crime management practices.

Deployment will be informed by ongoing area needs analysis, with a clear expectation that post holders will move between locations in line with changing priorities.

This approach forms part of a developing area support model, designed to enhance consistency and effectiveness across the estate. Through targeted deployment, the roles will support establishments to implement and embed effective crime management processes, demonstrating sustainable models of resilience and enabling informed consideration of long-term resource and capability requirements.

The post holder will be line managed by the Area Crime Manager (Band 5) to provide specialist support to establishments, strengthening crime management processes, improving evidence handling, and promoting effective partnership working with criminal justice agencies.

The CiPCo role plays a key role in coordinating crime-related activity within prisons, ensuring consistent application of policy, supporting the Crime in Prison Referral Agreement (CiPRA), and improving outcomes for victims and witnesses of crime.
