If you’re customer focussed, intent on delivering excellent service, enthusiastic about leading and motivating a team, then this role gives you the opportunity to play a pivotal role within HM Courts & Tribunals Service (HMCTS).

About us

HMCTS is an agency of the Ministry of Justice responsible for the administration of criminal, civil and family Courts and Tribunals in England and Wales. Our roles support our service users and colleagues within HMCTS, where people and businesses access potentially life-changing justice.

National Services is a directorate within HMCTS Operations, comprised of Criminal Fines, Collection and Enforcement, National Business Centres and Courts & Tribunals Service Centres.

PLEASE NOTE: Office Location – Heathland House, Heather Farm, Woking, Surrey GU21 4XY. You must be able to travel to the Thames Basin Heaths SPA daily, with the role requiring occasional weekend/early morning and evening work. The TBH SPA and local partners fall within parts of Berkshire, Hampshire and Surrey.

The team provides an on-the-ground wardening service on the Thames Basin Heaths Special Protection Area (TBH SPA). Working closely with the Special Protection Area (SPA) landowners and managers and other key partners (including local authorities, Wildlife Trusts, the RSPB, Ministry of Defence, Forestry Commission, and The Crown Estate), the team engages directly with the public through engagement and education to raise awareness amongst visitors of the importance and sensitivity of this internationally important heathland site.    

The Thames Basin Heaths Partnership (TBHP), hosted by Natural England’s Thames Solent Area Team, is fully funded from developer contributions, and is overseen by the Thames Basin Heaths (TBH) Joint Strategic Partnership Board (JSPB), a body comprising eleven local authorities, and Hampshire and Surrey County Councils.   

Responsibilities for this Warden role will be engaging with the public on the SPA and at events, to raise awareness about the SPA's importance, spreading wildfire awareness and promoting Suitable Accessible Natural Greenspace (SANG) sites as alternatives.   

Additionally, this role will provide support to the team’s communications and monitoring functions, through providing social media content, writing articles, and collecting data through surveys.   

The role requires some involvement with the Heathland Hounds project – a sub team of the TBH SAMM project, focused on interacting with dog walkers – who are a key audience to which the projects key message ‘paws on paths’ is aimed, to encourage behaviour change and ultimately protect the SPA and reduce disturbance to its protected species. 

Job description  

Key Tasks / Principal Accountabilities

Warden the SPA and engage and educate the general public about ground-nesting birds, wildfire awareness and the use of SANGs.
Provide a consistent SPA/SANG message, including the use of promotional and educational materials.
Organise and deliver onsite events and pop-ups, and support the delivery of a wider engagement programme, including facilitating activities during Heath Week.
Assist with educational activities both on and off the SPA, including events, workshops and guided walks as required.
Develop and maintain relationships with stakeholders, partners and landowners to support the delivery of events, pit stops and pop-ups.
Contribute to social media content, website blogs and newsletter articles.
Be willing to learn and adopt new ways of working and new technologies.
Undertake administrative tasks as required.
Participate in monitoring activities, including visitor surveys, warden engagement logs and people-counter data collection, ensuring data is entered promptly and accurately.
Undertake other duties and activities as required.

Knowledge, Skills & Experience

Essential

A relevant qualification or experience in education, countryside or animal management, nature conservation, environmental science, on-the-ground wardening, or a related discipline.

Experience of, and confidence in, engaging with the public, particularly gained through working outdoors in a nature conservation or countryside access-related role.
Knowledge of Natural England's purpose and how this work contributes to its aims and objectives.
Good written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to engage effectively with a range of internal and external partners.
Ability to use Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Teams, Outlook and other technology as required.

Desirable

Experience of, and confidence in, engaging with children in an educational setting.
Experience of, and confidence in, engaging with dogs and dog walkers.
Knowledge of countryside access, rights of way and nature conservation issues.

Job description

Join us in shaping a future where nature and people thrive. Whether you're drawn to hands-on conservation or playing a vital part behind the scenes, your work at Natural England will support lasting benefits for the environment and society.  

Our Role 

Natural England is the Government’s adviser for the natural environment and the Nature regulator with a wide range of statutory duties and powers. We provide the evidence, expertise and advice to recover Nature and shape better places for people to live. We do this working through and with others.  

Strategic Outcomes for Nature 

Our strategy is framed through four strategic outcomes. Each of these outcomes reinforces and amplifies the others, and together they address environmental, social and economic actions critical to thriving nature.  

Recovering Nature – Increased scale and quality of places where nature thrives.  
Building Better Places – Greener homes and infrastructure create healthier, more investable places, recognising we live better where nature thrives around us.  
Improving Health and Wellbeing – Build nature into everyday life so people can support, access and benefit from nature, wherever they live.  
Delivering Security through Nature – Nature helps us adapt to the threats of a changing climate and improves our national security, supporting more resilient food production, healthy soils, clean and plentiful water and clean air.  

Find out more about the work of Natural England at:  

Natural England’s Strategy: Recovering Nature for Growth, Health and Security - GOV.UK

The Role

This role is based at Heather Farm, Woking, GU21 4XY and requires regular attendance at the site office and on the heathland sites in the Thames Basin Heath’s area.

 Based in the Thames Solent Area Team, you will be working as the Senior Manager for the Thames Basin Heaths Partnership (TBHP) project.

 The team provides an on-the-ground warden service on the Thames Basin Heaths Special Protection Area (TBH SPA). Working closely with the Special Protection Area (SPA) landowners and managers and other key partners (including local authorities, Wildlife Trusts, the RSPB, Ministry of Defence, Forestry Commission, and The Crown Estate), the team engages directly with the public to raise awareness amongst visitors of the importance and sensitivity of this internationally important heathland site.  

The Thames Basin Heaths Partnership (TBHP), hosted by Natural England’s Thames Solent Team, is fully funded from developer contributions, and is overseen by the Thames Basin Heaths (TBH) Joint Strategic Partnership Board (JSPB), a body comprising eleven local authorities, and Hampshire and Surrey County Councils.

 Working in partnership with Natural England (NE) colleagues, the TBH local authorities, SPA landowners and managers, and other stakeholders, you will line manage the warden team, consisting of both permanent and seasonal wardens and enable the project to achieve its objective of helping to protect the SPA from recreational pressures arising from new housing development

Job description  

Key Tasks/Principal Accountabilities

Work closely with the Senior Project Officer and the Senior warden as a key member of the TBH SAMM leadership team, championing the project through engaging with stakeholders/partners/councillors at regular meetings and site visits.
Provide effective line management for a team of wardening staff, including leading the annual recruitment of seasonal wardens.
Support the team by regularly meeting them on site, organising team face to face meetings (monthly) and support the team on their delivery of key public engagement events such as Heath Week.
Take charge of Health & Safety (H&S) for the SAMM team, participating as the SAMM team’s H&S committee representative, reviewing risk assessments, keeping hostile sites excel spreadsheet and hostile sites on the rota up to date. Have regular catchups with H&S Business Partner and ensure compliance with regular schedule of testing for the People Safe system.
Manage staff performance and the quality of the service delivery, to meet engagement and wardening hours targets – reported to the JSPB on a 6 monthly basis.
Lead procurement activity and online portal management of the People Safe system, and other services that the TBH SAMM team procure for their operations – such as vehicle leasing and cleaning services for the site office base.

Knowledge, Skills & Experience

Experience of leading and managing groups of people to help them understand and deliver against priorities to ensure targets and outcomes are met. (Essential)
The ability to lead people and teams through periods of change and an understanding that individuals adapt and react to change differently. (Essential)
Experience of managing the performance of individuals, ensuring that delivery standards are met. (Essential)
Understanding and experience of using coaching and mentoring skills to develop and support individuals within a team. (Essential)
Demonstrate leadership by sharing skills to help others achieve their capability and career goals. (Essential) 
Ability to manage several complex areas of work at the same time, to prioritise and communicate decisions that are taken. (Essential)
Demonstration of good communication skills, both written and verbal, as well as the ability to actively listen and relate to people from different backgrounds or with different levels of understanding. (Essential)
Good understanding of heathland management and ecology and the development pressures and issues affecting this habitat. (Desirable) 
Good understanding of access management and monitoring techniques and their use in managing recreational pressures. (Desirable)

Benefits  

At Natural England, we support a healthy work-life balance by offering full-time, part-time, and flexible working arrangements.  

We provide excellent opportunities for career progression, training, and development tailored to your role. This includes ten days annually for personal learning and development, plus three additional days for volunteering.  

You’ll receive a generous leave allowance of 25 days per year (pro rata), increasing by one day for each year of service up to 30 days (pro-rata), access to the Civil Service Pension scheme with a 28.97% employer contribution, and a range of benefits such as shopping discounts and a cycle-to-work scheme. Staff can also join the Civil Service Sport club for discounts on sports, leisure activities, and social events.  

We are committed to fairness, equality, and inclusivity. Our employee-led diversity networks help foster a welcoming environment where everyone feels valued and supported.  

Locations  

Natural England has adopted hybrid working – which means our staff work from a flexible range of locations, encompassing home, offices (ours and our partners) and relevant sites. All new staff will be formally linked to one of our 25 offices across England, and the expectation is that all new staff will be able to access their local office to be part of the community of staff in their geographical area. Staff are expected to attend their associated office for 20% of their contractual hours.  
  
Staff members are required to carry out all their duties working in this way and cannot do so from an overseas location at any time. Travel expenses will be paid if work-related travel is required but does not apply to travel between home and your associated office.   

National team roles can be linked with any Natural England office while Area Team roles will be linked with an office in the relevant geographic area.   

View a map of our office locations here: online map of Natural England office locations 

Pay   

It is Natural England policy to employ at the entry point of the salary range.  

You will become an active member of the relevant local leadership community, the group of senior Natural England staff in each of the localities across England who we ask to provide support and co-ordination for the local group of staff. 

Please note: Licensed visa sponsoring organisations are employers authorised by the government to recruit and sponsor overseas workers, enabling them to obtain the appropriate visa to work legally in the country. Natural England is NOT a licensed sponsorship employer. 

As part of the Natural England’s application process, candidates are asked to confirm their right to work and remain in the UK. If a candidate says that they meet these requirements, ID is checked, a provisional offer of permanent employment is made and pre-employment eligibility checks commence. Only after these checks are candidates given firm offers of employment. 

Natural England is unable to employ individuals who cannot provide the required evidence of their right to work. 

How to Apply 

We welcome and encourage applications from all communities. Natural England is accredited to the Disability Confident Scheme, which denotes organisations which have a positive attitude towards disabled people. Disabled applicants who meet the minimum requirements for the role at the shortlisting stage are guaranteed an invitation to interview.  

If you require a reasonable adjustment at interview, or there is anything else you would like the panel to take into consideration, you should notify us of this at application stage where possible, or well in advance of your interview. We now provide primary interview questions in advance for all formal recruitments.  

This vacancy uses competency-based assessment. We'll assess you against the competencies below during the selection process. Please be aware that we reserve the right for roles that receive a high volume of applications to initially sift applications for one competence only. 

Leading and Managing People
Work Delivery
Personal Effectiveness
Putting People at the Heart of the Environment

When completing the application form you should present relevant examples using the STAR format. Give us an example of how you have demonstrated the competency (which can be work related or from another area of your life) and tell us about the Situation, the specific Task you had to undertake, the specific Actions you took, and the Result (both immediate and in a wider context) of your Action.  

Please note that STAR format is not required when answering the Technical Skills & Knowledge competency.  

Examples should be given in no more than 250 words for each competency.  

If you are successful at the shortlisting stage, you will be invited to attend an interview via MS Teams or a suitable alternative, where you will be asked to give examples for all competencies as set out in the Job Description.  

As with all roles in NE, these roles require office attendance of a minimum of 20% of the working time – one day per week for those who work full time, subject to any reasonable adjustments and/or existing contractual homeworking.

About the job
Job summary

This post is open to applicants who can meet the College’s nationality, UK residency and vetting requirements.  

About us:

PoliceAI is a nationally significant technology and transformation programme in UK policing. Backed by central government investment and positioned at the heart of the police reform agenda, PoliceAI is the new National Centre for AI in Policing, helping to shape how policing uses data, technology and artificial intelligence to tackle crime, protect the public and modernise frontline operations. 

We bring together operational policing, technical expertise, product delivery, assurance and the responsible use of AI to develop and scale capabilities that improve public safety outcomes. Our work helps forces respond more effectively to demand, strengthen investigations, identify risk and harm earlier, and free up frontline time for the activities that matter most to communities. 

This is an opportunity to contribute to a programme with national reach and meaningful public service impact, helping to define how AI is developed, governed and adopted across one of the UK’s most important public services. The work is varied and complex, moves at pace, and has the potential to deliver better tools for policing, better outcomes for the public, and stronger foundations for the responsible use of AI. 

PoliceAI is hosted within the College of Policing. 

About the College of Policing: 

Our mission is: Leadership, Standards, Performance. This guides our work with individuals, forces, and policing partners towards our vision. We exist to support police officers, police staff and volunteers to deliver the best service to the public. Only through high quality leadership, consistent standards and continual performance improvement can everyone in policing reach their full potential. Our mission guides our work with individual, forces and partners towards our vision.

We offer a supportive and inclusive environment for people to thrive through our extensive flexible-working policy, employee wellbeing support, family friendly policies, and status as a disability confident leader. 

For further information visit our ‘Work for us’ page.

Location 

Remote working (anywhere in the UK). Please note, some travel may be required. 

Job description

We are looking for people who are motivated by public service, interested in responsible innovation, and comfortable working collaboratively across organisational, operational and technical boundaries. Joining PoliceAI means contributing to a supportive, multidisciplinary team that is helping to shape the future of policing and ensure AI is used in ways that are effective, responsible, operationally useful and worthy of public trust.  

As a Senior AI Engineer at PoliceAI, you will lead hands-on engineering across both AI product development and support for testing, evaluation, verification and validation (TEVV). Working with end-users, product owners and subject matter experts, you will translate policing needs into technical solutions and the engineering capability needed to assess AI products.  

You will build secure, maintainable and scalable services, while working with Data Science & Evaluation to develop reusable test harnesses, integrations and tooling for TEVV of internally developed and third-party AI products. Collaborating with platform engineers, software engineers, user-centred designers and governance colleagues, you will support repeatable assessment of system performance, limitations and suitability for intended policing use.  

Reporting to the Head of Engineering, success means owning complex engineering delivery across product development and TEVV support, remaining hands-on in code and raising quality through design review, reusable patterns and coaching AI Engineers to support trusted AI adoption across England & Wales policing.  

Additional Information: 

We recruit by merit on the basis of fair and open competition, as outlined in the Civil Service Commission's recruitment principles. 

Due to our status as Public Servants, we are not eligible to participate in the Civil Service transfer process. Therefore, while successful candidates can transfer into the organisation on their existing terms and conditions, any move back to the Civil Service may mean that continuity of service is not automatically recognised by the receiving department, and new starter or modernised terms and conditions may apply, subject to the receiving department's policies and arrangements. However, employees who move directly to a Civil Service department without a break in service may retain continuity of service for redundancy and pension purposes.  

Any previous service with local government or other external Modification Order bodies will not be carried forward or count when calculating redundancy entitlement.  

The College embraces diversity and promotes equal opportunities. As such, we comply with the Disability Confident Scheme (DCS) and apply the minimum selection criteria at sift stage of the recruitment process. Where necessary, we may increase the minimum selection criteria to support the effective management of the recruitment process, while ensuring our approach remains fair, transparent and consistent with our Disability Confident commitments. 

Person specification

Some of your responsibilities will include:  

Leading the design, development and deployment of AI-enabled products, translating operational needs into scalable, secure and effective technical solutions.  
Building and maintaining reusable testing, evaluation and integration tooling to support the TEVV of internally developed and third-party AI products.  
Making technical decisions across architecture, data flows, APIs, model deployment, security and performance, ensuring solutions are fit for policing use.  
Supporting live AI services through monitoring, automated testing, incident resolution and continuous improvement.  
Providing technical leadership, coaching engineers and working with multidisciplinary teams to improve engineering standards and delivery quality. 

To be successful in this role you’ll need 

Proven experience leading the end-to-end delivery of complex AI or machine learning solutions from user need through to production deployment and measurable outcomes.  
Strong technical expertise in Python, AI/ML frameworks, AI application patterns and modern software engineering and MLOps practices.  
Experience developing testing, evaluation or comparable tooling that supports the assessment and assurance of AI systems.  
Experience designing, integrating and operating AI-enabled services, data pipelines and APIs within cloud-based environments 
The ability to provide technical leadership, coach others and communicate technical decisions, risks and findings to both technical and non-technical stakeholders. 

Please see the attached job description which contains full details of the role. Please read the key criteria section in the job description (linked with the advert) carefully before applying. Applications will only be considered from candidates who can clearly demonstrate that they meet the essential requirements outlined for the role.

Internal College applicants who are at risk of redundancy or in need of redeployment and pass the recruitment process, will be given priority over other applicants. 

 

How to apply: 

As part of the application process, you will be required to complete the following: 

1) Curriculum Vitae (CV), not exceeding two sides of A4 

2) Personal Statement (500 words maximum) - Your personal statement should provide a clear, concise, and compelling account of why you are applying for the role, the skills and experience you would bring, and how you meet the essential criteria. Use relevant, well-chosen examples to demonstrate your achievements and impact, drawing on STAR principles where appropriate. While evidence and examples are important, the statement should read as a coherent and engaging narrative rather than a series of separate responses to individual criteria. 

To ensure you are assessed on merit alone, we ask you to anonymise your application. This means removing personal identifiers such as your name, age, and place of education. You do not need to remove your employment history, job titles, or any information about your work.

Where a high volume of applications is received, an initial sift may be conducted based on candidates' CV. As part of this process, shortlisted applicants may be invited to take part in a brief informal discussion to explore their experience, skills, and achievements in more detail before applications progress to the next stage. 

This discussion will help assess suitability for the role and may be used to determine whether candidates proceed further in the selection process. Candidates who are successful at this stage may either be subject to a full sift or progressed directly to assessment and/or interview, depending on the number of applications received and the requirements of the recruitment process.

Interviews will be conducted via Microsoft Teams. As part of the assessment process, candidates will be required to deliver a 10-minute presentation and complete a coding exercise. During the coding exercise, you will be expected to share your screen with the interview panel. Details of the presentation topic and coding exercise will be provided when you are invited to interview. 

Interviews will include questions based on the listed behaviours and experience.

About the job
Job summary

Fraud is a hidden crime that is increasingly diverse, complicated, and often perpetrated remotely. To address this, the government has invested in a Public Sector Fraud Authority (PSFA), which launched in August 2022. The PSFA brings together capability across government to bring a cohesive and collaborative approach. 

The National Fraud Initiative (NFI) is a remote/virtual team that forms part of the wider PSFA Data, Analytics and AI Team. The NFI Team members are located across the UK so they can be accessible to those that take part in the NFI. There will, however, be a requirement to be flexible with regard to working hours and with travel, as you will be required to attend in-person meetings across the UK. The majority of these meetings will be in Stoke on Trent, Birmingham, Manchester, Newcastle upon Tyne, York, London or Glasgow.

Job description

Structurally, the NFI team is made up of the Operational Delivery (OD) Team and Business Development (BD) Team. This Senior Executive Officer (SEO) post is on the Operational Delivery Team. The post holder will contribute to the leadership, well-being and development of the OD Team.

The post holder will be responsible for the following areas of work:

Supporting the Operational Delivery Lead with the delivery of data matches to 1,000 participants, including local government, NHS, and central government, private sector (including financial, insurance, utilities, and hire car sectors), in a timely manner, through biennial national matching, biannual mortality screening and the annual council tax single person discount exercise. 
Contributing to maximising the outcomes (value of fraud and error detected and prevented) reported by all NFI participants from match releases across the full suite of NFI products to achieve the target of up to £150 million per year. This is underpinned by a broad spectrum of data analytics, involving the extraction and manipulation of key management information reports containing metrics that allow effective programme management and profiling progress against targets.
Working with the Operational Delivery Lead to plan and manage the work of the team using project management software to ensure the key deliverables and targets are met.
Leading one or more complex dataset areas, that involves maximising outcomes specific to those dataset areas, the management of associated data matching pilots, associated improvements to the web application, and promotion of NFI services to existing and new participants.
Project management of elements of the National exercise, including monitoring progress against PSFA deliverables. Lead the change control tool used to record developments to the NFI web application in line with agreed contractor KPIs. Coordinate the timing and delivery of NFI developments across OD and BD, assessing risks and balancing priorities to maximise efficiency and meet delivery targets.
On-boarding new voluntary participants, including oversight of high-quality communications, preparation and delivery of workshops, presentations, and written guidance, and maintaining working relationships with these new participants such as new government departments and other public and private sector bodies to ensure the benefits of participation are maximised.
Analysis and assurance of fraud and error outcomes of up to £150 million per annum, including monitoring and profiling outcomes against targets to underpin outcomes maximisation strategies. Assurance and development of management information reports to improve the accuracy and efficiency of reporting. Research and develop evidence-based methodologies to determine estimated preventative and detected savings for NFI matching and design and implement assurance processes that are subject to internal and external scrutiny.

Please note

Recruitment campaigns for the Public Sector Fraud Authority (PSFA) are continuing as usual, but candidates should be aware that following the Government’s announcement on the changes to some civil service departments, roles will be subject to the machinery of government move of the PSFA to DWP. We will provide more information on any potential or future impact this will have on office locations and other elements if you are selected to interview. This work remains of high importance to the civil service, and we thank you for your continued interest. 

Person specification

Essential

Experience of, and a high level of technical understanding of, complex and sophisticated data processing operations.
A background in data and/or counter-fraud.
Strong technical knowledge and skills in fraud prevention and detection techniques.
Advanced data handling and analytical capabilities, with a proven ability to manipulate complex datasets to identify patterns, anomalies, and outliers, directly informing fraud detection and prevention strategies and programme performance.
Excellent oral and written communication skills.
Excellent project management skills.
Strong team-working skills, with the ability to work cooperatively to achieve corporate objectives.
Strong interpersonal, influencing, and people management skills.
Experience managing varied and challenging priorities through a team.
Experience of using and developing management information reports.
Experience in maintaining and developing relationships with key stakeholders at a senior level.
Experience using project tracking and workflow management tools.
Use of Google, e.g., Google Docs, Sheets, and Microsoft Office, in particular Excel.

Desirable

Experience working as part of a virtual team and building or contributing to inclusive, psychologically safe virtual team environments.
Experience with visualisation tools (like Power BI or Tableau).
Experience in engaging with local government, NHS, or central government bodies.

About the job
Job summary

Job description

Nature Recovery is a key outcome of Natural England’s strategy, and Local Nature Recovery Strategies are a critical and potentially powerful delivery tool.

With almost all Local Nature Recovery Strategies now published, Natural England is moving into a phase of enabling their delivery, both through continued support to Responsible Authorities and through a process of ensuring that our delivery of all NE’s work in a place takes appropriate account of the relevant Local Nature Recovery Strategy.

You will join a small, busy team in National Delivery, which manages the demands and opportunities that LNRS’ provide for NE, and which will have overall responsibility for ensuring that NE’s Operations is able to meet the expectations of Defra, Arm’s Length Bodies (FC and EA) and Responsible Authorities.

You will be expected to use your geospatial data science knowledge and experience to lead the delivery of geospatial services to the Local Nature Recovery Strategy (LNRS) programme, through the maintenance and development of the ArcGIS Online LNRS map and collation and analysis of the LNRS data submitted by each Responsible Authority, leading engagement with key stakeholders and NE/Defra colleagues as required.

The role requires a strong and visible presence, both virtually and in person. This includes confidently leading and contributing to calls, maintaining engagement, and building strong relationships with stakeholders.

The role description is not exhaustive, and we will expect post holders to work collaboratively across the team and beyond.

Job description  

Key Tasks/Principal Accountabilities

Principally, to act as the project manager and technical lead for the national LNRS map when it has been collated from the individual LNRSs submitted by the Responsible Authorities (RAs).
Functionally manage the higher officer and provide progress reporting to LNRS colleagues in Natural England, Defra, Environment Agency and Forestry Commission.
Leading engagement with external stakeholder and data providers such as the Defra LNRS Policy team, Forestry Commission, Environment Agency, Rural Payments Agency, Responsible Authorities and LNRS partnerships to ensure their data and requirements are successfully incorporated into the map, particularly regarding future data requirements for the monitoring of LNRS delivery.
Lead the LNRS Data & Evidence (D&E) workstream. Arrange regular team calls, write minutes etc for Bi-weekly D&E Workstream calls, and D&E Technical sub group calls.
Support NE LNRS senior officers with data, licensing and mapping queries from RAs.
Lead the work to support the development of GIS tools for the sharing and dissemination of LNRS geospatial data within the Defra group and externally to stakeholders and the general public, using ESRI’s ArcGIS suite of products.
Lead the collation of 48 individual LNRS from Responsible Authorities into a National LNRS dataset.
Work with the Data Services licensing team to manage project data and data from external stakeholders in accordance with data licensing and data management procedures. Ensure licensing of national LNRS map product into an Open Government Licensing (OGL) Liaise with Ordnance Survey & RAs to enable this.
Work with the LNRS team / workstreams to assist in the recording of Mapping of Actions Undertaken by RAs to deliver their respective LNRS and the national monitoring of LNRS delivery. To assist the dissemination of government data (e.g. RPA agri-environment data) to RAs to assist with RA reporting.
Develop GIS expertise through a programme of Continuing Professional Development.

Knowledge, Skills & Experience

Advanced level use of ArcGIS Online and associated online tools and apps such as Experience Builder.
Advanced level use of desktop ESRI ArcGIS products (e.g. ArcMap, ArcGIS Pro, etc.).
Experienced in transforming data, including integrating different data types (e.g. spatial and non-spatial) and from different data sources. Applying appropriate geospatial techniques to clean and merge multiple datasets.
Good data presentation skills, such as producing maps and statistics for reports or external publications.
Good data management skills and experience of working within data licensing and data standards (e.g. metadata standards, Open Data, GDPR, etc.).
Able to work within a framework of agreed Quality Assurance standards.
Experience of working with stakeholders and colleagues within Defra and Defra-family organisations.

Working within the National Delivery Team, you will provide strategic direction, lead collaboration across organisations, and help ensure effective delivery of LNRS objectives.

The role requires strong data literacy, policy understanding, stakeholder engagement and leadership skills, alongside the ability to support operational delivery and build effective partnerships to drive nature recovery at scale.

The postholder will work closely with project colleagues, Defra Group partners and Responsible Authorities, contributing flexibly to shared objectives and successful programme delivery.

Engage across LNRS workstreams to identify current and future data and evidence needs.
Contribute to Defra Group activity addressing data licensing challenges.

Oversee delivery, including milestones, risks, dependencies and issue resolution.

About the job
Job summary

Please note that the PSFA (including the National Fraud Initiative) will imminently be moving from the Cabinet Office to the Department for Work and Pensions.

The Public Sector Fraud Authority is at the cutting edge of the government’s response to tackling fraud against the public sector and builds on the internationally recognised reputation of the Counter Fraud Function as a world-leader in tackling fraud and corruption in the public sector. 

Fraud represents a cost to the government which is estimated at £33.2bn - £58.8bn per year. At PSFA, we play an instrumental role in spearheading the Government's response to fraud by developing innovative policies and initiatives to counter this threat with the mission of funnelling real, tangible financial benefits back to the public. 

In pursuing this goal, we utilise a network that spans across public and private sectors. Serving as the foremost experts in public sector fraud, PSFA affords those who work with us unrivalled access to Ministers in an area that is rapidly rising to the forefront of the Government’s agenda. With an ever-expanding remit in an arena of growing ministerial priority, now is a truly exciting time to join a team that has an impact throughout the machinery of government. 

The NFI team manages and delivers the NFI data matching service. This service includes a national data matching exercise to identify fraud and error across a range of public sector datasets, and data pilots to test the effectiveness of processing new and different types of data for fraud. The team works as part of the PSFA’s wider fraud data services team. This role offers flexibility in location, with a requirement to attend face-to-face meetings across the UK at least 5-10 times per year. This includes Stoke-on-Trent, Manchester, Birmingham and other regional hubs.

Job description

This hands-on, specialist delivery SEO role, will be a shared strategic resource across both the NFI Operational Delivery Team (ODT) and the NFI Business Development Team (BDT). This SEO role acts as the NFI’s primary operational assurance lead for data governance, legal compliance, and security standards and is one of seven SEOs across the NFI team. 

You will take day-to-day operational ownership for reviewing data protection impact assessments (DPIAs), managing memoranda of understanding (MOUs) and Data Sharing Agreements (DSAs), and coordinating security policies and data deletion. You will serve as the governance bridge between the NFI team, external IT suppliers, and security colleagues outside the PSFA (e.g., wider Civil Service Security function, and broader public sector partners). This role may involve line management responsibilities.

Key responsibilities include:

1. Operational Assurance & DPIA Drafting
Lead the technical review, and quality assurance for all NFI Data Protection Impact Assessments (DPIAs), ensuring they meet UK GDPR/DPA standards prior to formal submission through the internal governance process.
2. Supplier & External Stakeholder Liaison
Act as the primary day-to-day governance liaison with external third parties, including the NFI IT supplier/platform teams and security colleagues outside of the PSFA (e.g., Cabinet Office or DWP Security). Ensure technical changes, supplier workflows, and platform architectures are tabled as appropriate before the NFI Security Working Group (SWG) so they adhere strictly with government security standards.
3. Legal Frameworks & Agreements
Lead the operational drafting, maintenance, review and tracking of all Memoranda of Understanding (MOUs) and Data Sharing Agreements (DSAs) with participating public and private sector bodies (as appropriate).
4. Policy Compliance & Incident Management
Monitor, audit, and enforce adherence to the official NFI Data & Match Deletion Policy across external suppliers, data processors, and internal operational systems in accordance with data protection law.
Draft, update, and exercise NFI-specific Security Incident Response Plans and internal staff data security guidelines. Act as the primary operational coordinator during near-misses or data incidents, liaising directly with supplier and external security leads.
5. Governance Technical Expert Support
Act as the Single Point of Contact (SPoC) for central PSFA, Data Governance teams and the Data Protection Officer for NFI related DPIAs.
Representative to the NFI Security Working Group (SWG).
Manage and maintain the NFI Risk Register, ensuring risks, mitigations, and actions are accurately recorded and tracked.
Provide high-capability capacity to absorb urgent ad-hoc compliance commissions and ministerial briefing requests for G7 leads.
Person specification

Practical DPIA & Data Protection Expertise: Hands-on experience drafting, evaluating, and reviewing Data Protection Impact Assessments (DPIAs), managing information governance compliance and applying UK GDPR / Data Protection Act principles in data-heavy operational environments.

Third-Party & Supplier Liaison: Proven ability to work collaboratively with external IT suppliers, contractors, or cross-departmental security stakeholders to enforce data asset management compliance and security standards.

Governance Framework Management: Experience preparing, negotiating, or managing operational agreements such as MOUs, Data Sharing Agreements (DSAs), or multi-agency data policies.

Analytical Risk, Compliance & Governance: Experience monitoring compliance (e.g., data deletion or retention schedules), managing operational risk, overseeing data governance processes, and coordinating responses to security incidents or near-misses.

Autonomy & Delivery at Pace: Track record of driving work forward independently, managing competing priorities across multiple teams (ODT and BDT), and producing high-quality briefing materials under tight deadlines.

Central Government or Counter-Fraud Experience: Proven experience working in a central government environment or in a counter-fraud role.

Regional Mobility: Willingness and ability to travel (approx. 5-10 face-to-face meetings per year) to key regional operational sites and stakeholder hubs (including Stoke-on-Trent and Manchester).

Note: Experience of working with Google (Mail, Sheets, Drive, etc.) and Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, PowerPoint) is also required.

Desirable Criteria

Specialist Counter-Fraud Insight: Deep understanding of NFI data-matching frameworks, public sector counter-fraud strategy, or complex data-matching environments.

Formal Assurance Qualifications: Professional certification or formal training in Data Protection or Information Security (e.g., CIPP/E, BCS Data Protection Certificate).

Strategic Stakeholder Engagement: Demonstrable experience influencing senior leadership within central government or complex multi-agency public sector environments.

The successful candidate must meet the security requirements before they can be appointed. The level of security check needed is BPSS.

We’re recruiting for a Senior WordPress/PHP Developer here at Justice Digital, Data and Science to be part of our warm and collaborative Website Builder Platform Team.

We currently have over 200 experienced developers who make up the engineering community across the MoJ. You will coach and mentor junior colleagues and take part in informal support networks with your peers. You will be encouraged to play an active role in the engineering community and culture.

Our Tech Stack 

We use a range of technologies and we’re looking for people who have experience of building web applications or back-end systems in an object-oriented language, and love learning new languages and frameworks.   

We use WordPress/PHP and React JS to write our application code, GitHub Actions for CI/CD, Sentry for application monitoring, Kubernetes and Docker to schedule and run our services (read about our Cloud Platform), AWS for most of our infrastructure and use a MacOS developer environment. 

For front-end development, we value a robust understanding of the underlying web technologies. We value well-maintained, open-source tools that can be used to produce semantic HTML, performant CSS and unobtrusive JavaScript and we assess all our services against accessibility criteria. 

Check out GitHub for a closer look at the technologies we use, and a complete list of services that we build and maintain. We subscribe to the manifesto for agile software development.

Introduction

HM Courts & Tribunals Service (HMCTS) is responsible for the administration of criminal, civil and family courts and tribunals in England and Wales. Our roles support our service users and colleagues, where people and businesses access potentially life-changing justice.  We’re looking for individuals who are committed to public service and want to make a difference in people’s lives in delivering justice. If you’re interested in developing a career with a real purpose, please apply. 

Job Description 

As a Senior Software Developer at HMCTS you will work with a wide range of stakeholders such as user researchers, product managers, designers, business analysts, delivery managers and digital architects, all of whom share a vision for making better government through smarter use of technology. You will innovate to radically transform public services for the better. 

The development squad you are placed on will be agreed closer to your start date, but examples of products can be found in our GitHub repository: 

https://github.com/hmcts 

You can find more information about our ways of working in the HMCTS Way: https://hmcts.github.io  

Technologies we rely heavily on: 

Java and Spring Boot to write our backend services 
Node.js to write our frontend services 
Power Platform for low-code development 
Jenkins for CI/CD 
Dynatrace for application monitoring 
Kubernetes and Docker to run our services 
Azure for most of our infrastructure 
Terraform for infrastructure as code 
Postgres and Redis as our databases. 
GOV.UK Design System for our web interfaces 
Macs to do all the above 
In addition, we use a range of other technologies and continue to evolve by employing new technologies that help us deliver better services to our users 

As a Senior Developer in HMCTS you will: 

Develop, improve and document code, following best practices and internal standards.  
Continuously learn and stay up to date with relevant technologies, identifying potential issues.  
Ensure product security, data confidentiality, and integrity, raising risks as needed.  
Support and maintain software, including limited out-of-hours work when required.  
Plan development, coordinate integration, and contribute to process improvement.  
Manage service availability effectively and cost-efficiently.  
Build and test system interfaces.  
Use test-driven development, write automation scripts, and participate in code reviews.  
Mentor junior colleagues and share technical expertise. 
Take ownership of the technical roadmap and promote best practice across the development lifecycle. 
Influence product strategy by providing technical insight to stakeholders 
Design and develop software based on user stories. 
Participate in recruitment and procurement. 

Essential skills 

We’re seeking a full stack developer with the ability to develop and deploy high-quality code. The ideal candidate will have: 

Experience in building scalable enterprise applications using Java. 
Strong frontend proficiency with modern JavaScript frameworks (e.g., Angular, React, or Vue). 
A solid grasp of RESTful API design and relational database architecture (e.g., PostgreSQL). 
Proficiency in cloud-native architecture including infrastructure as code (e.g., Microsoft Azure, Terraform) 
Knowledge of the full development lifecycle, including CI/CD, authentication (OAuth2/OIDC), and system monitoring. 
Leadership capabilities, with a proven track record of mentoring junior engineers and driving technical standards. 
Experience utilising DevOps practices and containerisation tools (Docker/Kubernetes). 
A security-first mindset, with the ability to identify and mitigate vulnerabilities (OWASP top 10) during the design phase.

About the job
Job summary

Job description

The Ministry of Justice (MoJ) priorities include improving public safety and reducing reoffending by reforming prisons, probation and youth justice, and building a justice system which makes access to justice swifter and more certain for all citizens whatever their background. Project professionals in the MoJ help to improve the government’s ability to protect the public and reduce reoffending, and to provide a more effective, transparent and responsive criminal justice system for victims and the public.

The Project Delivery Function aim is to have capable and empowered teams, delivering Project Delivery excellence. We will maintain and enhance our reputation as leaders in project delivery, recognised for highly skilled and professional practice that evolves beyond our current achievements to consistently deliver outstanding results. ​We will excel at initiating projects with strong foundations and then deliver on our commitments by improving and sustaining delivery confidence to successfully realise outcomes and benefits. ​Our people will be empowered to develop the skills they need to succeed, and our line managers will be accountable for upholding functional standards and demonstrating excellence in project delivery.

The MoJ’s Functional Operating Model is unique across government. All project delivery professionals are line managed through the Function and then assigned to projects and programmes across the MoJ and its Agencies.  The MoJ Project Delivery Function sees the centralisation and coordination of all project delivery within the Ministry. These opportunities provide a unique chance to be at the forefront of implementing significant projects across the MoJ.

Successful candidates will be part of a flexible resource pool and may be placed in roles based on business needs. If we’re not able to offer a post in the specific role applied for, we will match you to a suitable position at the same grade that aligns with your skills and experience. Successful candidates are expected to commit to the role for a minimum of 18 months. MoJ expects its leaders to show openness, honesty and commitment, and, of course, to deliver results.

Key responsibilities of the role

The Senior Project Manager leads and manages the project and project team. They are responsible for driving and overseeing the delivery of the project to ensure objectives are clearly defined and achieved within agreed time, cost, and quality constraints. The Senior Project Manager plays a key role in project governance and works with stakeholders to ensure agreed project outputs are delivered, enabling benefits to be realised. 

These may be further shaped and adjusted dependent on business needs and team resources / skills.

Delivery – Creates and leads the project to achieve agreed outcomes within time, cost, and quality constraints.
Project Management – Provides daily management and leadership of the project and team. Providing effective leadership and management controls. Designs the project structure and organisation suitable for each stage, establishes project controls, selecting appropriate delivery methodologies, and managing transitions between project phases.
Business Case – Develops and drafts the business case, incorporating input from specialists as needed.
Budget – Develops the budget and monitors delivery within it.
Resources – Identifies skill requirements, deploys and develops resources, and manages a medium-sized team.
Benefits Realisation – Delivers the benefits and outcomes stated in the business case. Ensures a suitable benefits realisation strategy is in place and monitors long-term benefit delivery against the business case.
Stakeholder Management – Identifies and manages stakeholder relationships, ensuring necessary senior-level support. Manages internal and external relationships appropriately.
Risks and Issues – Identifies and monitors project risks and issues, develops mitigating actions and escalates when necessary. Collaborates with related projects to manage interdependencies.
Governance – Supports effective governance and decision-making. Provides reporting and engages with mechanisms that hold the project manager accountable for delivery.
Assurance – Participates in assurance reviews and supports implementation of recommendations. Organises assurance processes, such as gateway reviews, when required.
Change Management – Ensures change management processes are in place to agree on and document changes to deliverables with stakeholders.
Guidance and Support – Offers support, guidance, and coaching to the project team, shows commitment to personal development, and promotes effective team performance.
Project Performance and Controls – Communicates the vision and translates it into delivery objectives for the team. Develops and maintains the Project Plan, sets project controls, manages performance, and reports progress to sponsors.
Digital and Data - Uses digital tools to analyse data to understand progress against the plan and takes mitigation actions and exploits opportunities. Uses data to forecast future outcomes and address issues before they escalate. Introduction:

These are exciting times at HM Court and Tribunals Service (HMCTS). As an agency of the MoJ, we support the judiciary across England and Wales to deliver justice by running courts and tribunals and processing outcomes, and we are looking for talented people to help us achieve our ambitions. It will be challenging, important and rewarding.

HMCTS Digital and Technology Services (DTS) is a specialist technology directorate which provides support to HMCTS in the use of IT and Digital.

DTS is committed to being a great place to work and part of our offer is brilliant training opportunities and support from expert colleagues. As well as that you’ll find flexible working, an inclusive culture and a place where your opinion is valued.

Please follow the link below for further information about HMCTS. 

www.gov.uk/government/organisations/hm-courts-and-tribunals-service

Job Description:

As an Associate Delivery Manager, you will be expected to support the Senior Delivery Manager with a strong focus on delivery. You will be accountable for the effective delivery of complex, high-risk products and services. You will have a strong background and experience of working in a project-based environment, across a range of products and services, throughout the entire product life cycle. You will have some responsibility and accountability as a point of escalation. You will also be supporting the Senior Delivery Manager who is accountable for the performance and coaching of agile software development teams. Your CV should demonstrate your ability and experience of creating and coaching self-organising, high performing agile delivery teams.

Key Responsibilities:

·      Supporting in the leading of Agile ceremonies and or coaching sessions

·      Planning and implementing agile ways of working whilst supporting the multi-disciplinary team and suppliers.

·      Managing the risks and issues log, including proactively following up on actions which may help mitigate current and future risks or issues.

·      Communicating with key stakeholders to support the resolution of blockers and highlight any dependencies, risks & issues to delivery.

·      Supporting in the management of the team’s incident dashboard and various incident management MS Teams channels.

·      Work with Senior Delivery Manager and Principal delivery Manager to provide delivery updates to key stakeholders and or the delivery team.

·      Supporting in the management of delivery products and services at different phases to understand how the needs of the team and the product vary across the stages of the product lifecycle

·      Maintaining the monthly ROI database for all automation streams based off cost savings vs costs analysis.

·      Responsible for identifying and comparing the best processes or delivery methods to use, including measuring and evaluating outcomes

·       The post holder is required to work in a flexible way and undertake any other duties reasonably requested by line management which are commensurate with the grade and level of responsibility of this post.

Skills & Experience:

·       People management skills to successfully lead your teams, with the coaching aptitude to support and empower your people. Allowing people to develop the skills, confidence and experience to independently deal with business and people related issues.

·       Management skills; ability to plan, set realistic performance measures, delegate and review progress to improve performance and manage risks.

·       Able to build and maintain effective relationships with key internal and external stakeholders at all levels. To influence and negotiate to resolve competing priorities and issues.

·       Ability to work to tight timescales, managing your priorities and ensuring timely delivery of quality products.

·       Effective communication skills including delivering and leading on key messages, ensuring that they are understood and implemented consistently.

·       Ability to analyse data, identify trends and workflow requirements to make informed decisions that contribute to local and national priorities and improving service delivery.

Desirable Criteria:

·       Experience of working within a multi-disciplinary team.

·       Experience of using IT applications and an interest in technology as a way of resolving business problems or meeting business needs.

·       Have had experience in applying Agile principles in practice, can identify and compare the best framework or delivery methods to use.

·       Can facilitate difficult discussions within the team or with diverse senior stakeholders.

Number of vacancies: 3  

*We offer a hybrid working model, allowing for a balance between remote work and time spent in your local office. Office locations can be found ON THIS MAP 

Please note that unless you are an existing member of staff at Justice Digital, Data and Science, the only London location being recruited to is 10 South Colonnade, E14 4PU. We are no longer recruiting to 102 Petty France, SW1H 9AJ. 

The Role 

We’re recruiting for Senior User Researchers here at Justice Digital, Data and Science to be part of our warm and collaborative teams. 

This role aligns against Senior User Researcher from the Government Digital and Data Framework 

User Researchers help our teams develop a deep understanding of our people - citizens, businesses or government colleagues - who use our services. Their findings allow our teams to design and build better services more quickly and at lower cost and risk. And to continuously improve services, based on data and evidence.  

As a senior user researcher at JDDS you’ll be an experienced practitioner who can plan and lead user research activities within a multidisciplinary team and uncover insights of the staff and end users of our complex but fascinating Justice system.   

You’ll be joining a highly supportive community of researchers who meet regularly to share their knowledge and project experience within a safe learning environment. You may work with other user researchers (junior and mid-level) to assure and improve their research practice.  

Background  

We design, build and support user-centred digital and technology services for the justice system: services that make a real difference to our staff, members of the public and their families who use them. Millions of people interact with our services, and Digital & Technology play an important role in improving access to justice and making that experience much easier and less distressing.  

We are using digital, data, technology, and AI to build capability, work smarter, and more efficiently. We want to create a digitally enabled end-to-end justice system which can adapt and respond to changing needs. We were the first digital team in a government department, and the first to deliver an exemplar service, with experts in web development, design, delivery and product management and user research, alongside around 50 organisations, including the courts service and Government Digital Service (GDS) 

You’ll receive a range of excellent benefits when you join our department, including: 

A generous employer pension contribution of 28.97% through the Civil Service Pension Scheme. 
25 days of annual leave, (increasing to 30 days once you have reached 5 years of service), plus 8 bank holidays and a privilege day for the King’s birthday. 
Flexible working arrangements including hybrid working, working part time or compressed hours. Designed to support a positive work–life balance. 
Employees are allocated 10% of their working time for personal and professional development. 
A £1k per person learning budget is in place to support all our people, with access to best-in-class conferences and seminars, accreditation with professional bodies, fully funded vocational programmes and e-learning platforms. 
Compassionate maternity, adoption, and shared parental leave policies, with up to 26 weeks leave at full pay, 13 weeks with partial pay, and 13 weeks further leave. And maternity support/paternity leave at full pay for 2 weeks, too! 

You can find more details of the Benefits we offer here. To help picture your life at MoJ Justice Digital, Data and Science please take a look at our blog. 

Key Responsibilities 

Researchers on our teams are:  

Great at using quantitative and qualitative research methods  
Comfortable with metrics and able to synthesise data quickly  
Great storytellers and communicators  
Very good at collaborating in a dynamic, data-driven, creative environment with diverse stakeholders  

Primary Responsibilities:  

Scope, plan, conduct, analyse and communicate research  
Lead colleagues to analyse and synthesise research data  
Communicate research findings across the organisation.  
Work closely with product managers, designers, data scientists, and developers/ engineers to turn user research findings into actions that lead to valuable services  
Mentor, support and line manage mid-level and junior User Researchers   
Educate stakeholders and colleagues on how user research can be beneficial within their project 

If this feels like an exciting challenge, something you are enthusiastic about, and want to join our team please read on and apply! 

Person Specification  

Essential 

Research. You can demonstrate experience in a wide range of user research methods, and can help teams to adopt them. You can plan user research for services with challenging user needs and complex user journeys. You can advise colleagues on the choice and application of research methods to assure best practice. 
User-centred and Agile practices. You can understand and demonstrate experience in a range of user-centred practices. You can help inexperienced teams adopt user-centred practices and embed them into their Agile workflow. You can advocate for user research, and engage potentially sceptical colleagues and stakeholders.   
Analysis and synthesis. You can understand and help teams to apply a range of methods to analyse research data and synthesise findings. You can work collaboratively with colleagues in carrying out analysis and synthesis. You can advise on the choice and application of techniques, and can critique colleagues’ findings to assure best practice. You can share insights with a range of colleagues and stakeholders to help elevate the user's voice.  
Inclusive research. You can help teams understand the diversity of users of government services. You can effectively include all kinds of users in appropriate research activities. You can advocate inclusive practices and help teams design and deliver accessible services that work for all users. You recognise the ethical implications when planning and carrying out research for both the researcher and participant.  
Stakeholder relationship management. You can influence stakeholders and manage relationships effectively. You can build long-term strategic relationships and communicate clearly and regularly with stakeholders.  
Research management, leadership and assurance. You can evaluate the quality of research against accepted professional standards for user research, explain what good practice involves and give constructive feedback to other user researchers to ensure their work meets good practice standards 

Willingness to be assessed against  the requirements for BPSS clearance 

We welcome the unique contribution diverse applicants bring and do not discriminate based on culture, ethnicity, race, nationality or national origin, age, sex, gender identity or expression, religion or belief, disability status, sexual orientation, educational or social background or any other factor.   

Our values are Purpose, Humanity Openness and Together. Find out more here about how we celebrate diversity and an inclusive culture in our workplace.  

The Civil Service is committed to attract, retain and invest in talent wherever it is found. To learn more please see the Civil Service People Plan and the Civil Service D&I Strategy.

A Personal Statement (no more than 750 words) which should outline your experience and skills, giving clear examples of work undertaken. It should specifically address the following 3 criteria listed below, using a separate paragraph for each.  
Research. You can demonstrate experience in a wide range of user research methods, and can help teams to adopt them. About the job
Job summary

The Public Sector Fraud Authority is at the cutting edge of the government’s response to tackling fraud against the public sector and builds on the internationally recognised reputation of the Counter Fraud Function as a world-leader in tackling fraud and corruption in the public sector. 

Fraud represents a cost to the government which is estimated at £33.2bn - £58.8bn per year. At PSFA, we play an instrumental role in spearheading the Government's response to fraud by developing innovative policies and initiatives to counter this threat with the mission of funnelling real, tangible financial benefits back to the public. 

In pursuing this goal, we utilise a network that spans across public and private sectors. Serving as the foremost experts in public sector fraud, PSFA affords those who work with us unrivalled access to Ministers in an area that is rapidly rising to the forefront of the Government’s agenda. With an ever-expanding remit in an arena of growing ministerial priority, now is a truly exciting time to join a team that has an impact throughout the machinery of government. 

This is an exciting role as Strategy and Business Analytics Lead, as part of the NFI team. The role is pivotal in ensuring that the PSFA meets its commitments to deliver counter-fraud outcomes through data sharing and analytics. The successful candidate will demonstrate a deep, practitioner-level understanding of counter-fraud methodologies and be capable of applying these across complex data-sharing landscapes.

Job description

The NFI team manages and delivers the NFI data matching service. This service includes a national data matching exercise to identify fraud and error across a range of public sector datasets, and data pilots to test the effectiveness of processing new and different types of data for fraud. 

The team works as part of the PSFA’s wider fraud data services team.  Structurally, the NFI team is made up of the Operational Delivery (OD) Team and Business Development (BD) Team. This role offers flexibility in location, with a requirement to attend face-to-face meetings across the UK at least 5-10 times per year. This includes Stoke-on-Trent, Manchester, Birmingham and other regional hubs.

The Strategy and Business Analytics Lead will be one of four G7s in the NFI team. The post holder will contribute to the leadership of the NFI and the wellbeing and development of the NFI team. This role will involve line management of at least three other team members.

Lead on the NFI savings assurance process and audit including engagement with relevant oversight boards and auditors. Manage the review and auditing of reported savings including oversight of  the evidence based methodologies used to determine estimated preventative and detected savings for NFI matching. Represent the NFI on the Savings Assurance Board and Prevention Panel as a subject matter expert. Maintain a close working relationship with the NFI BD team, acting as a key link so the boundary between Business Development and Operational Delivery research is clearly defined;  
Lead on delivery of the commercial modelling and framework for NFI (with associated income of £1.5 million - £2 million per year) including designing competitive fee scales/models, delivery of the statutory consultation for the proposed fee scales, working with PSFA colleagues, legal experts and other stakeholders to secure ministerial approval for both pre and post consultation proposals; 
Lead the development and implementation of the National Fraud Initiative strategy and monitoring activity against the strategy, working with NFI G6’s, the wider PSFA, Audit Scotland, Audit Wales and the Northern Ireland Audit Office;
Coordinate the research and development of pilot data match opportunities, utilising existing datasets (managed by the Operational Delivery team), to support the overall NFI pilot pipeline, and act as a bridge to facilitate the transition of successful pilots into sustainable business as usual (BAU) operational delivery.
Shape and deliver the NFI external stakeholder and user engagement strategies with and through the team and lead on the production of the NFI biennial report;
Manage the delivery of data analytics for the NFI including overseeing the collating, monitoring and reporting of fraud and error outcomes;
Work with the PSFA policy team as the policy and legislation lead for the NFI, to further the NFI strategy and requirements across policy and legislation including any future revisions to the Code of Data Matching Practice;
Represent the NFI as part of the PSFA across Government to deliver on the NFI strategy and support the counter-fraud and data in counter fraud agendas; and
Support the wider NFI - including governance, reporting, recruitment and learning and development.

Key responsibilities include:

Leading on the development and implementation of the National Fraud Initiative strategy. Monitoring activity against the strategy and reporting the outcomes internally. Working with the rest of PSFA, Audit Scotland, Audit Wales and the Northern Ireland Audit Office to ensure strategies are aligned 
 Leading on the design of robust competitive fee scales and fee models for around 1,000 NFI customers. This requires consideration of operational costs, profit margins and value for money. These fee scales form the basis of the NFI work programme and scale of fees. You will work with the Deputy Director for Data and Analytics, Head of the NFI, legal experts and other PSFA colleagues to secure ministerial approval to consult on the work programme and scale of fees, analyse the consultation responses and conclude the consultation with publication. 
Overseeing the NFI data analytics and reporting of outcomes from the NFI’s data matching exercises. This involves carrying out quality and assurance checks on the data that is extracted to ensure accurate figures are presented for internal reporting. Data analytics underpin the outcomes maximisation strategy, ensuring the Operational Delivery Team meets its outcomes target. 
Overseeing the robust assurance processes, as the NFI analyses and reports are subject to internal and external scrutiny. Where actual outcomes are not available this post leads on research and developing evidence based methodologies to determine estimated preventative and detected savings. These are presented for approval by senior leaders and cross government experts.
In addition to these core responsibilities, the post holder will be expected to support the NFI leadership team on ad-hoc strategic tasks and cross-cutting commissions arising across the full spectrum of the NFI’s business activities.
Person specification

Essential criteria

Strategic Leadership & Policy: Proven track record in developing and implementing complex strategies and leading on policy/legislation, specifically within a counter-fraud or public sector integrity context. You must demonstrate success in monitoring performance against organisational goals and working with legal teams to ensure compliance and strategic alignment.
Commercial & Financial Modelling: Expertise in designing robust commercial frameworks and fee models for large-scale public sector services. You must demonstrate experience in developing competitive fee scales that account for operational costs, profit margins, and value for money, and in securing ministerial approval for such models.
Data Analytics & Counter-Fraud Methodology: Strong data handling and analytical capabilities with proven experience in a counter-fraud or data-matching environment. You must have experience overseeing data quality, designing evidence-based research programmes, and establishing defensible methodologies for savings assurance that withstand internal and external audit scrutiny.
Governance & Regulatory Compliance: Proven experience in designing and implementing governance frameworks, specifically within a public sector or data-handling context. You must demonstrate a solid understanding of data governance, GDPR compliance, and how these apply to complex data-sharing or counter-fraud programmes.
Stakeholder Management & Governance: Proven ability to navigate complex political and audit landscapes. You must have experience engaging with senior leaders, Ministers, and cross-government stakeholders (such as Audit Scotland/Wales/NI) to build consensus, manage risk, and represent the organisation as a subject matter expert.
Operational Delivery & Leadership: Ability to manage varied, high-pressure priorities autonomously and lead teams effectively. This includes overseeing research programmes, managing communications, and driving team development in a fast-paced environment.

Note: Experience of working with Google (Mail, Sheets, Drive, etc.) and Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, PowerPoint) is also required.

Questions

1. Strategy & Regulatory Alignment

Scenario: You are leading a cross-jurisdictional data-matching initiative. Key oversight bodies express conflicting views: one flags data protection concerns while the other views the proposal as a critical modernisation step.

Question: How would you navigate this regulatory friction to build consensus while minimising risk to project timelines? Detail the specific influencing strategies you would use with key stakeholders and the governance framework you would establish to maintain long-term compliance.

2. Methodological Assurance & Risk Management

Scenario: You are preparing an annual savings report and discover an unexpected variance in a key "preventative savings" metric due to a dataset issue.

Question: How do you handle this? Explain your escalation and resolution process, including how you validated the methodology with senior stakeholders and the long-term assurance standards you set to prevent recurrence.

Job description

This role will lead and support the delivery of a range of Earth Observation (EO) projects, and 

the wider development of EO skills in the team and across Natural England. In the Earth Observation Service, we undertake a wide range of EO work, including drone data capture 

and processing, coastline monitoring, as well as wildfire and habitat mapping. We use data from drone, crewed aircraft and satellite platforms, and from a range of different sensors, including aerial photography, and multispectral, LIDAR and RADAR sensors. 

We are seeking someone to be both an EOS Drone Pilot and Earth Observation Analyst, with significant experience and capability in both drone surveys and applying EO techniques. About half of the role’s time will be dedicated to planning and carrying out drone surveys for environmental monitoring and analysis, as described further below. You will be operating rotary drones including DJI M300 and Parrot Anafi USA, as well as a Fixed Wing drone (Sensefly eBee X), using multiple sensors, including aerial photography, multispectral, and thermal.

The other half of the role’s time will be dedicated to the other post holder responsibilities, including EO data analysis, contributing to and helping lead a variety of projects to support Natural England’s objectives. These may include analysis of sand dunes and coastal habitats, monitoring geomorphological change, and wild animal detection.

This role will require substantial traveling within England, including overnight stays, most likely around once or twice per month.  A full driving licence is essential; as is the ability to swim (due to surveying near water).

Job description  

The post holder will: 

Be an EOS Drone Pilot. Carrying out drone surveys across England, including planning, ground control, survey, post processing, data management and equipment maintenance. These surveys are carried out with our fleet of drones: a fixed wing Sensefly eBee X, with Aeria-X (RGB camera), MicaSense Red-Edge-MX (Multispectral Sensor) and Duet-T (Thermal Sensor); a Multi Rotor DJI Matrice 300, with DJI P1 (RGB Camera), MicaSense Dual (Multispectral Sensor) and DJI M30T; a Multi Rotor DJI Mavic 3 Enterprise, with integrated RGB Camera; and a Parrot Anafi USA with integrated RGB and thermal sensors.
Carry out Drone data post processing. You will post-process and create ortho-mosaics for our own drone surveys as well as surveys carried out by pilots in other teams, following our existing GDPR/DPIA policy at all times.
Contribute to EO Analysis. Develop and run EO analysis, including through data acquisition, handling, manipulation, integration, and analysis, using a variety of tools including standard EO software (and/or R and Python scripting), on different platforms, including cloud computing environments.
Maintain and develop relationships with customers and partners.Engage with partners and end users to share knowledge on EO approaches and products, build partnerships on common problems and understand customer needs for EO data products/support. 
Support capability building, documentation and quality assurance.Work to help build and deliver technical skills training and create reproducible analytical pipelines and standardised products, including through documentation of methods and quality assurance approaches.
