About the job
Job summary

The Public Sector Fraud Authority (PSFA) is a fast paced delivery and operational team that is responsible for holding departments and arms-length bodies to account for their handling of fraud in the public sector. The Authority will write the standards for counter fraud work across government and hold public bodies to account against these. Working in the PSFA offers access to a wide range of stakeholders across government and the opportunity to work with various sectors in a high-profile policy area with high media, parliamentary and ministerial interest.

The PSFA was launched on the 3rd August 2022 following an increased focus in government on tackling fraud. It succeeded the Government Counter Fraud Function (GCFF) in the Cabinet Office.  The PSFA is at the centre of this function and leads work across government and public bodies to improve the prevention, detection and recovery of fraud. The PSFA is outcome and performance driven, offers a depth and breadth of expertise and works jointly with HM Treasury (HMT) to tackle fraud in the public sector.

The National Fraud Initiative (NFI) team is a remote/virtual team that sits within the PSFA Data and Analytics function. Team members are spread across the UK. We are looking for a full time member of staff, but alternative working patterns may be considered. We can be flexible about the location of the post holder, but there will be a requirement to be flexible with regard to working hours and with travel as you will be required to attend meetings across the UK, with the majority being in Stoke on Trent, London, York, Newcastle, Glasgow  and Manchester.

Structurally the NFI team is made up of the Operational Delivery (OD) Team and Business Development (BD) Team. The objectives of the BD Team are to: design and deliver strategies and a work programme to counter both existing and new fraud, work in collaboration with organisations across the public and private sector, and to innovate the way in which data is used. 

Please note that the PSFA (including the NFI) will imminently be moving from the Cabinet Office to the Department for Work and Pensions but will remain sponsored by HMT.

Job description

The post holder will be responsible for supporting and managing all aspects of the NFI’s Business Development strategy and work programme, managing the relationships with key external stakeholders and promoting the uptake of new products and services to existing and new participants.

Candidates should have strong project management skills with the ability to manage competing demands and priorities in a fast-paced environment.

Responsibilities 

The post holder will be responsible for leading on the delivery of the NFI Strategy in relation to Business Development including targets for growth. This will involve managing relationships with key internal and external stakeholders, oversight of a pilot pipeline that aligns with  PSFA objectives, supporting on the creation and promotion of new products, services  and innovations for existing participants and potential new participants with a view to: 

Increasing both the volume and frequency of data that is used in, or accessed through, the NFI:
Develop and deliver a data acquisition strategy - identify and secure access to additional data (participants and 3rd party) that can improve the effectiveness of the NFI in preventing and detecting fraud; work with participants and stakeholders to evaluate the options for, and benefits of, more regular data feeds into the NFI;
Develop and deliver a pilot pipeline - work with participants and stakeholders to identify new data/data matching areas to pilot with a view to including them in the national exercise, or another suitable NFI product;
Maximise stakeholder participation  in NFI - work with Local Authorities to develop and utilise the NFI products;develop relationships with established regional counter fraud hubs to enable utilisation of data for mutual benefits; and work with participants to promote the use of the NFI on an ongoing rather than a cyclical basis.
Embracing new technologies and techniques through an innovation strategy to improve existing products and to develop new products including:

Other key work will include:

Line Management of approximately 3-5 SEOs and HEOs
Agree and deliver new business growth targets - including volume and financial outcomes.
Establish key metrics on performance of NFI products 
Analyse and report on performance against strategy and targets to relevant audiences including Stakeholders and Senior Management. 
Promote the business development elements of the NFI Strategy across senior management and wider stakeholders, including shaping and delivering an effective marketing strategy
Proactively manage business development collateral and communication to promote NFI products and the benefits of participation
Attend/Report to the NFI Governance Board, as required
Attend the NFI Innovation Working Group
Chair the Bi-monthly Fraud Hub User Group meeting

Project Delivery & Regulatory Compliance: Excellent project management skills (including pipeline management) in a fast-paced environment, combined with a strong understanding of data protection regulations and data-sharing legislation.
Leadership & Change Management: Proven management experience, including guiding teams through periods of organizational change and coordinating varied, challenging priorities.
Stakeholder Engagement & Communication: Experience developing relationships with a complex range of stakeholders, backed by strong interpersonal, influencing, and audience-tailored presentation skills.

About the job
Job summary

Job purpose

We are seeking a commercially astute Procurement Lead to manage and improve the IAA’s procurement and contract management activity. The role will support the Head of Finance to develop and deliver a clear procurement roadmap aligned with organisational priorities, ensuring compliance, value for money and effective management of commercial advice staff risk.

The postholder will be the main point of contact for procurement advice within the IAA, working with colleagues and with direction from Home Office Commercial to support compliant, proportionate and timely procurement decisions. The role will strengthen procurement policy, contract oversight, supplier management and organisational capability.

Job description

Key responsibilities

Procurement leadership

Lead procurement planning and delivery across the IAA, including priority areas such as ICT, automation and regional delivery.
Promote best practice in commercial governance, ensuring procurement processes are efficient, proportionate and compliant.
Advise the Head of Finance and budget holders on procurement routes, approvals, commercial risks and value for money considerations.
Represent the organisation at relevant commercial forums and working groups within the Home Office.
Act as the lead liaison with Home Office Commercial on IAA procurement activity, ensuring appropriate engagement, assurance and escalation.

Contract review and pipeline management

Review and maintain oversight of the IAA’s existing contracts, software licences and supplier arrangements.
Identify upcoming contract end dates, renewal points and procurement requirements, recommending appropriate next steps.
Maintain the contract register and commercial pipeline, ensuring planned activity is completed on time and in line with legislation, governance requirements and value for money principles.

Procurement, contract and supplier management

Support the Head of Finance to implement practical contract management arrangements, including monitoring of contract terms, performance and renewal dates.
Establish proportionate contract management practices, including supplier performance monitoring, review meetings, issue resolution and value assurance.
Work with budget holders to define requirements, agree timelines and support the successful mobilisation of new contracts.
Coordinate procurement activity across teams to support smooth implementation and clear ownership of actions.

Governance & Compliance

Ensure procurement activity aligns with the Procurement Act 2023, Cabinet Office controls, Home Office Commercial requirements and Government Commercial Function standards.
Support appropriate procurement documentation, audit trails and decision records to demonstrate compliance and transparency. Develop and maintain a commercial risk register, working with the Head of Finance and relevant stakeholders to agree and monitor mitigation actions.

Stakeholder Engagement

Act as the first point of contact for procurement queries, providing clear advice and practical support to staff across the IAA.
Work with internal stakeholders to scope requirements, consider sourcing options and develop effective procurement solutions.
Liaise with Home Office Commercial and Legal colleagues to ensure the correct use of frameworks, approvals and commercial assurance routes.
Work with the Head of Finance and Senior Leadership Team to align procurement activity with the IAA’s strategic objectives and operational priorities.

Additional responsibilities

Provide a proactive, efficient and compliant procurement service for the IAA, using initiative and sound judgement to make evidence-based recommendations.
Manage competing priorities and deliver high-quality work at pace, including under pressure.
Use IAA equipment, information and resources responsibly and in line with organisational policies.
Undertake other reasonable duties within the scope of the role as required by the Head of Finance or relevant budget holders.
Person specification

Essential criteria

Member of (or working towards) the Chartered Institute of Procurement and Supply;
Proven experience of public sector procurement, ideally in an arm’s-length body, regulator or central government environment;
Good working knowledge of UK public procurement legislation, including the Procurement Act 2023, and relevant government commercial frameworks and controls;
Experience supporting procurement activity across the commercial lifecycle, from requirements definition and sourcing through to contract mobilisation and supplier management;
Experience identifying and managing commercial risk, with the ability to provide clear advice and influence decision making;
Strong stakeholder engagement, communication and negotiation skills, with the confidence to work with senior colleagues and suppliers;
Strong analytical skills and commercial judgement, with the ability to assess options and recommend practical solutions; and
Experience of ICT, digital or business transformation procurement.

Job description

The Role

The Deputy Director, Chief People Officer Function and HR Profession plays a pivotal role in supporting the Director General People & Capability and Chief People Officer to lead one of the largest corporate functions in government, with responsibility for around 1,100 colleagues across the Ministry of Justice People & Capability Group and a significant leadership role across the Government HR Profession, representing approximately 12,000 HR professionals across government.

Operating at the centre of both departmental and cross-government priorities, the role enables the Chief People Officer to deliver organisational transformation, workforce reform and professional leadership agendas. The postholder provides the strategic grip, insight and leadership necessary to support effective decision-making, drive organisational performance and ensure the successful delivery of priorities across a complex and high-profile portfolio.

As a member of the People & Capability Senior Leadership Team, the postholder works across organisational boundaries, building strong partnerships with Cabinet Office, Government People Group and departmental leaders to strengthen the HR profession, support its future direction and improve outcomes for both the profession and the Ministry of Justice.

Key Responsibilities

Reporting into the Director General – People and Capability you will:

Lead the Chief People Officer's Office, providing strategic leadership across the support arrangements for the Director General People & Capability and Chief People Officer, including both departmental responsibilities and the role as Joint Head of the Government HR Profession.
Lead governance, business planning, performance, risk and assurance across People & Capability, ensuring senior leaders have the insight, challenge and evidence needed to make effective decisions and deliver strategic priorities.
Lead transformation and organisational improvement activity across People & Capability and support delivery of the Government HR Profession transformation agenda, translating strategic priorities into delivery and measurable outcomes.
Maintain strategic oversight of corporate and profession portfolios, ensuring risks, dependencies, resources and delivery priorities are effectively governed and managed.
Work closely with Cabinet Office and Government People Function counterparts to provide strategic oversight of Government HR Profession activity, ensuring effective governance, reporting, accountability and decision-making arrangements are in place to support the Joint Heads of Profession in setting direction, exercising stewardship of the profession and delivering agreed priorities.
Work closely with Cabinet Office counterparts to lead engagement activity on behalf of the Joint Heads of Profession, supporting development and delivery of the Government HR Profession strategy, brand and engagement approach, reflecting the profession's leadership arrangements across government.
Act as a principal adviser to the Chief People Officer, providing strategic advice, challenge and assurance on organisational priorities, performance, risk and delivery.
Lead and develop a high-performing multidisciplinary team, creating an inclusive culture focused on delivery, continuous improvement and professional excellence.

 Essential Experience

Senior strategic leadership and advisory experience - Significant experience operating at a senior level within a complex organisation, providing strategic advice, challenge and assurance to executive leaders and influencing high-profile decisions.
Corporate leadership, governance and organisational performance - A strong track record of leading corporate functions such as governance, business planning, performance, risk, assurance, strategy, private office or executive support, ensuring effective decision-making and organisational grip across complex portfolios.
Transformation and change leadership - Proven experience of leading complex organisational transformation, reform or improvement activity, translating strategic ambition into delivery and achieving sustainable change across organisational boundaries.
Cross-organisational influence and partnership working - Outstanding stakeholder management and influencing skills, with the ability to build trusted relationships, secure consensus and drive outcomes through collaboration across organisational and professional boundaries, including where there is no direct authority.
Leadership of high-performing teams - Proven experience of leading and developing multidisciplinary teams through senior managers, creating an inclusive culture focused on delivery, continuous improvement and professional excellence.

Job description

This is a rolling campaign; applicants cannot reapply within a six-month period. 

This scheme is open to former, qualified probation officers who have left the Civil Service within the last five years.

If you are a former qualified probation officer who has left the Civil Service less than 5 years ago, and have completed your probationary period and training, we would like you to consider returning to the Probation Service and joining your former colleagues, to keep the public safe and rehabilitate people on probation. 

Should you meet the eligibility criteria, and your application is accepted by the Probation Service, we can offer you a fast-track return to the service with no requirement to undertake a lengthy application form, interview and repeat any entry level training or assessment process. 

When considering applications, we take into account a range of relevant factors such as business need, location availability and previous employment history.

We will contact you to discuss your potential work base location, subject to passing pre-employment checks.

Please note: Former civil servants do not have the right to return. It is at the discretion of the Probation Service whether to reinstate former civil servants. This Returners Scheme utilises Exception 5 of the Recruitment Principles, which provides a mechanism for former civil servants to return, without necessarily going through fair and open competition again. 

Further information can be found here: Home - Civil Service Commission (independent.gov.uk)

If you have left the service more than 5 years ago, please visit Current vacancies – Prison and Probation Jobs for all our current vacancies. 

If you are not yet ready to re-join at this time, you can still be part of our Probation Alumni Network to be kept up date on the latest developments for probation returners. Click here to register to the Probation Alumni Network.

Eligibility:

Civil Service Exception 5 terms are as follows: 

Former civil servants who were previously appointed on merit on the basis of fair and open competition may be re-appointed (to a permanent or fixed-term appointment) within a maximum of five years of leaving the Civil Service.
Civil Servants can return to a role that is the same grade as when they left, or lower.
Civil servants cannot return on promotion under Exception 5.
Civil Servants can return within 5 years of leaving their last post.
There is no right of return for any individual, this is a matter of business need in the relevant civil service organisation.
This offer is open to all former qualified probation officers subject to meeting the eligibility criteria and who have left the Civil Service:
Through resignation or retirement in the last 5 years and who, before leaving, had successfully completed their probationary period.

 Options for working arrangements and contract:

During the application process, you'll need to choose a probation region. If your application meets the eligibility criteria, we'll subsequently get in touch with you to talk about your designated work base 


Please only indicate preferences where you are prepared to work. We will therefore endeavour to offer you a vacancy within a 60-minute commute of your home location. 

 The following options are available:

Full or part-time either permanent or temporary contract –temporary contracts are available for three, six or nine months.
Flexible contractual terms. 

For temporary contract appointments: 

We are offering temporary contracts on a three, six- or nine-month basis with the opportunity to extend the contract up to a maximum of two years, should you wish to do so and if there is a continuing requirement for your services. 

As a temporary member of staff, you will receive the full range of Civil Service benefits other than permanent tenure. You will be automatically enrolled for pension although you may opt out. You will be entitled to 25 days' leave per annum, pro rata.

Pre-employment checks:

You will be subject to pre-employment checks, including an Occupational Health Review, and security vetting which all successful candidates are required to pass. The level of security checks required is Enhanced Level 2, including DBS Enhanced. 

Once in your role, you will require access to the multi-agency ViSOR database, and you will therefore be required to undertake Non-Police Personnel Vetting (NPPV) Level 2.

This is routine and will apply to anyone who has been absent from the service for more than 28 days.

Training:

At the point of return, an individualised training needs analysis will be completed to identify training that has been completed and to schedule any relevant training that is required.

 Full time salary: 

£35,130 + London allowance of £4,250 for London, Staines, and Watford base location where applicable.
Higher starting salaries (in line with current policy) can be considered on a case-by-case basis.

About the job
Job summary

​​This post is open to applicants who can meet the College’s nationality, UK residency and vetting requirements.​ 

Please note that this is a part-time role.

About us: 

Our mission is: Leadership, Standards, Performance. This guides our work with individuals, forces, and policing partners towards our vision. We exist to support police officers, police staff and volunteers to deliver the best service to the public. Only through high quality leadership, consistent standards and continual performance improvement can everyone in policing reach their full potential. Our mission guides our work with individuals, forces and partners towards our vision. 

Although we are a relatively small organisation, our work has a big reach. We are uniquely placed to work both with national policing organisations and local forces to support frontline officers, staff and volunteers in their day-to-day roles. 

We offer a supportive and inclusive environment for people to thrive. Our extensive flexible-working policy, employee wellbeing support, family friendly policies, employers’ network for equality and inclusion membership (ENEI silver award winners), and status as a disability confident leader means everyone can bring their whole self to work. 

Additional Information: 

We recruit by merit on the basis of fair and open competition, as outlined in the Civil Service Commission's recruitment principles. 

Due to our status as Public Servants, we are not eligible to participate in the Civil Service transfer process. Therefore, while successful candidates can transfer in on their existing terms and conditions, any subsequent transfer out of the College to the Civil Service cannot be guaranteed on existing terms and conditions, and new starter/modernised terms may apply.  

The College embraces diversity and promotes equal opportunities. As such, we comply with the Disability Confident Scheme (DCS) and apply the minimum selection criteria at sift stage of the recruitment process. 

Our vetting 

If you are successful at interview, you will be required to undertake pre-employment security checks. You will be sent a security questionnaire which must be accessed within 24 hours. 

Please note, these checks can take up to 10 weeks. You will only be offered a start date after the checks have been completed. If the outcome of these checks is not satisfactory, your recommendation for employment will be withdrawn.

Job description
​Policing touches every community in the country. The evidence and insight you provide will help shape how we communicate with the public, with officers and staff, and with partners across the policing system, supporting the College's mission to cut crime and keep people safe. We're looking for an experienced communications analyst to join our Digital Communications team on a part-time basis. This is a genuine opportunity to use data and insight to improve how policing communicates, at a time when evidence-based decision-making has never mattered more. You’ll need to work closely with colleagues across the whole communications unit, including media, internal communications, external affairs and strategic communications. You'll collect, organise and interpret data on communications performance across a range of channels, turning complex information into clear, actionable insight. Your work will help us understand what's working, what isn't, and what to do next, supporting better decisions on messaging, audience engagement and channel selection.
Person specification

Some of your responsibilities will include: 

​​Maintaining and growing our audience personas, gathering insight on the attitudes, behaviours and motivations of key audience segments through desk-based and field research.​ 
​​Measuring and analysing communications performance across channels, producing clear reports for management use, identifying trends and recommending improvements to ongoing and future campaigns.​ 
​​Helping build and improve our communications approach to insight and analysis, developing our reporting infrastructure and working with colleagues to extend our data capture and analysis methods.​ 

To be successful in this role you’ll need: 

​​Experience producing and analysing statistics and management information, and working with complex data, including gathering, quality-checking, analysing and presenting it in a range of formats.​ 
​​Experience evaluating communications activity, identifying trends and drawing conclusions that inform ongoing improvement against key performance indicators.​ 
​​The ability to turn business needs and goals into meaningful communication performance measures, and to produce reports that present complex data in an easily digestible way.​ 
Experience gathering and analysing qualitative data, reporting actionable insight on behaviour and attitudes. 
The ability to identify the most effective research and measurement methods and adapt your approach to different contexts, audiences and situations. 
Excellent interpersonal skills, with the ability to influence, challenge and build effective working relationships with senior stakeholders. 
Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to translate technical and academic language for all stakeholders. 
Behaviours

We'll assess you against these behaviours during the selection process:

Making Effective Decisions
Communicating and Influencing
Working Together
Technical skills

We'll assess you against these technical skills during the selection process:

Ability to identify the most effective research and measurement methods and adapt approach.
Using appropriate tools to present analysis in a clear, meaningful and engaging way.

About the job
Job summary
This position can be based at Bristol , Cambridge , Eastleigh , Worcester or York
Job description

Join us in shaping a future where nature and people thrive. Whether you're drawn to hands-on conservation or playing a vital part behind the scenes, your work at Natural England will support lasting benefits for the environment and society. 

Our Role

Natural England is the Government’s adviser for the natural environment and the Nature regulator with a wide range of statutory duties and powers. We provide the evidence, expertise and advice to recover Nature and shape better places for people to live. We do this working through and with others. 

 Strategic Outcomes for Nature

 Our strategy is framed through four strategic outcomes. Each of these outcomes reinforces and amplifies the others, and together they address environmental, social and economic actions critical to thriving nature. 

Recovering Nature– Increased scale and quality of places where nature thrives. 
Building Better Places– Greener homes and infrastructure create healthier, more investable places, recognising we live better where nature thrives around us. 
Improving Health and Wellbeing– Build nature into everyday life so people can support, access and benefit from nature, wherever they live. 
Delivering Security through Nature– Nature helps us adapt to the threats of a changing climate and improves our national security, supporting more resilient food production, healthy soils, clean and plentiful water and clean air. 

Find out more about the work of Natural England at: 

Natural England’s Strategy: Recovering Nature for Growth, Health and Security - GOV.UK

The Role

Our Customer Service function provides a vital connection between Natural England and the people, organisations and communities we serve.

We manage a diverse range of customer contact, including general and operational enquiries, complaints, correspondence from Members of Parliament and Parliamentary Questions. We also support Natural England to learn from customer feedback, improve its services and deliver a consistent, high-quality customer experience.

We are looking for Higher Officers who are committed to excellent customer service and enjoy working in a varied, fast-paced environment. This is an exciting opportunity to build your knowledge and skills while contributing to work that supports Natural England’s objectives.

 As part of the team, you will:

help embed consistent customer service and quality standards across Natural England
work collaboratively with colleagues, customers, stakeholders and other government organisations
use customer information, feedback and performance data to support sound and evidence-based decisions
help improve customer service processes, performance and organisational capability
provide advice and support to colleagues handling complex or sensitive customer contact
monitor telephone services and undertake quality assurance checks

 

We are interested in applicants who can bring relevant customer service, operational delivery, communication or case-management experience and apply it effectively in a new environment.

 

 

Job description  

Key Tasks/Principal Accountabilities

As a Customer Services Higher Officer, you will help deliver a professional, high-quality customer service for Natural England. You will manage customer enquiries, complaints and correspondence, support colleagues in resolving complex issues, and contribute to service improvements that enhance the customer experience. Working collaboratively across Natural England and the wider Defra group, you will use sound judgement, strong communication skills and customer insight to ensure fair, timely and effective outcomes.

Key Tasks

Manage customer enquiries and casework

Handle a varied caseload of enquiries, complaints and correspondence, ensuring responses are accurate, timely and customer-focused.

Investigate and resolve complex customer issues

Gather and assess information from multiple sources, work with subject matter experts, and coordinate appropriate responses to complex or sensitive cases.

Support customer service quality and performance

Undertake quality assurance activities, identify opportunities for improvement, and use customer feedback and performance information to help improve service delivery.

Provide operational support and guidance

Support and coach colleagues, assist with managing telephone services, and help ensure customer demand is effectively balanced against available resources.

Drive continuous improvement and innovation

Contribute to projects and initiatives that improve customer service processes, systems and ways of working, including the effective use of digital and AI-enabled tools such as Microsoft 365 Copilot.

 Knowledge, Skills & Experience

 Essential Criteria

We are looking for candidates who can demonstrate:

Experience of delivering a high-quality customer or stakeholder service, including handling enquiries and providing clear, accurate and customer-focused responses.
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to communicate professionally and empathetically, adapt to different audiences, and build effective working relationships.
Strong organisational and decision-making skills, including managing competing priorities, meeting deadlines, exercising sound judgement and knowing when to seek advice.
The ability to gather, assess and accurately record information, with strong attention to detail and a commitment to producing high-quality work.
Confidence using digital systems and Microsoft 365 applications, with the ability to work independently and collaboratively in a busy operational environment while demonstrating integrity and professionalism.

Desirable Criteria

It would be helpful, but is not essential, if you have:

Experience of complaint handling, correspondence management or casework.
Experience of quality assurance, coaching, supervising or coordinating the work of others.
Experience of using customer feedback, performance information or service data to improve delivery and customer outcomes.
Experience of using generative AI tools, such as Microsoft 365 Copilot, to improve productivity, analyse information, draft communications and support decision-making, while applying appropriate governance and data protection requirements.
An understanding of the work of Natural England, Defra or another public-sector organisation.

 Benefits 

At Natural England, we support a healthy work-life balance by offering full-time, part-time, and flexible working arrangements. 

We provide excellent opportunities for career progression, training, and development tailored to your role. This includes ten days annually for personal learning and development, plus three additional days for volunteering. 

You’ll receive a generous leave allowance of 25 days per year (pro rata), increasing by one day for each year of service up to 30 days (pro-rata), access to the Civil Service Pension scheme with a 28.97% employer contribution, and a range of benefits such as shopping discounts and a cycle-to-work scheme. Staff can also join the Civil Service Sport club for discounts on sports, leisure activities, and social events. 

We are committed to fairness, equality, and inclusivity. Our employee-led diversity networks help foster a welcoming environment where everyone feels valued and supported. 

Locations 

Natural England has adopted hybrid working – which means our staff work from a flexible range of locations, encompassing home, offices (ours and our partners) and relevant sites. All new staff will be formally linked to one of our 25 offices across England, and the expectation is that all new staff will be able to access their local office to be part of the community of staff in their geographical area. Staff are expected to attend their associated office for 20% of their contractual hours. 
 
Staff members are required to carry out all their duties working in this way and cannot do so from an overseas location at any time. Travel expenses will be paid if work-related travel is required but does not apply to travel between home and your associated office.  

Pay 

It is Natural England policy to employ at the entry point of the salary range.

Please note: Licensed visa sponsoring organisations are employers authorised by the government to recruit and sponsor overseas workers, enabling them to obtain the appropriate visa to work legally in the country. Natural England is NOT a licensed sponsorship employer.

 As part of the Natural England’s application process, candidates are asked to confirm their right to work and remain in the UK. If a candidate says that they meet these requirements, ID is checked, a provisional offer of permanent employment is made and pre-employment eligibility checks commence. Only after these checks are candidates given firm offers of employment.

Natural England is unable to employ individuals who cannot provide the required evidence of their right to work.

How to Apply

We welcome and encourage applications from all communities. Natural England is accredited to the Disability Confident Scheme, which denotes organisations which have a positive attitude towards disabled people. Disabled applicants who meet the minimum requirements for the role at the shortlisting stage are guaranteed an invitation to interview. 

If you require a reasonable adjustment at interview, or there is anything else you would like the panel to take into consideration, you should notify us of this at application stage where possible, or well in advance of your interview. We now provide primary interview questions in advance for all formal recruitments. 

This vacancy uses competency-based assessment. We'll assess you against the competencies below during the selection process. Please be aware that we reserve the right for roles that receive a high volume of applications to initially sift applications for one competence only.

Technical Skills and Knowledge
Personal Effectiveness
Putting People at the Heart of the Environment
Work Delivery

When completing the application form you should present relevant examples using the STAR format. The Member Capability Officer: has responsibility for activities and actions relating to:

•    Assess, implement and support capability needs for members

Essential

•    People skills and experience of relationship building

Strategy

•    Promote an organisational culture of learning, transparency, fairness and independence.

Delivery of core L&D programme
•    Support the delivery of the core L&D programme for members ensuring this develops to meet changing needs and fully utilises innovative approaches to L&D in person and hybrid events including but not limited to:

New member induction training
MCA training
Chair training

•    Support the implementation of new e-learning systems
•    Track and record data and outcomes accurately 
•    Collate and evaluate feedback from members on the accreditation programmes with the view of improving future programmes
•    Provide administrative support for Practice Developers and Training facilitators in delivering the programmes.
•    Work closely with the other colleagues across the Board, such as Listings and MCA teams to support and deliver plans for member’s progression to the relevant casework.

•    Monitor and update records and data to report on capability, member progression and accreditation, to inform training needs and business priorities.

Networking events
Forums

•    Work closely with the other Member Capability Executive Officers understanding each other’s designated areas of responsibility to build resilience.
•    Work closely with the Standards team to share learning and outcome reports where appropriate
•    Build excellent working relationships with colleagues across the Board.
•    Establish and maintain strong relationships with members who support L&D as facilitators, practice developers, quality developers and delegates.
•    Build and maintain collaborative working relationships with external stakeholders to ensure the Parole Board’s L&D needs are fully supported.
•    Work closely with the Staff and Member Recruitment and Member Engagement Team within the Corporate Services Hub. Report on data requested by the team and flag member welfare concerns where appropriate.

Other
•    Other tasks appropriate to the role as assigned from time to time by the Senior Member Capability Manager or Head of Capability.

Number of Vacancies: 1

*We offer a hybrid working model, allowing for a balance between remote work and time spent in your local office. Office locations can be found ON THIS MAP

Please note that unless you are an existing member of staff at Justice Digital, Data and Science, the only London location being recruited to is 10 South Colonnade, E14 4PU. We are no longer recruiting to 102 Petty France, SW1H 9AJ.

The Role

Please note this role requires you to pass Security Check clearance. Please click on the link for details.

We’re recruiting for a G7 Local Prevention data Lead, here at Justice Digital, Data and Science to be part of our warm and collaborative, to be part of our warm and collaborative Cross-Government and Academia team, which is part of the Better Outcomes through Linked Data (BOLD) partnership.

Public services collect a large amount of data which is used to improve the quality of services offered to the public, but it is often not shared between organisations, making it difficult to understand whether certain services have been effective.

This role sits within the BOLD Prevention workstream, which supports cross-government efforts to improve outcomes for people with multiple needs. The workstream aims to enhance data sharing across organisations, deepen our understanding of individuals' needs, and provide earlier, better-quality information to support decision-making.

This role will lead the development of national-local data products with local authority partners, including linked national justice-local resident datasets, creating a single view of residents needs and experiences to surface to the frontline and developing a scalable frontline tool that can be shared with other areas. The post holder will lead analysis to the data to provide insights to support the national plan to end homelessness, reducing reoffending strategy and place based policy making.

This post requires working closely with data and digital professionals to deliver the products, as well as analysts, policymakers, operational partners, and data providers across government and other organisations.

You’ll receive a range of excellent benefits when you join our department, including:

A generous employer pension contribution of 28.97% through the Civil Service Pension Scheme.
25 days of annual leave, (increasing to 30 days once you have reached 5 years of service), plus 8 bank holidays and a privilege day for the King’s birthday.
Flexible working arrangements including hybrid working, working part time or compressed hours. Designed to support a positive work–life balance.
Employees are allocated 10% of their working time for personal and professional development.
A £1k per person learning budget is in place to support all our people, with access to best-in-class conferences and seminars, accreditation with professional bodies, fully funded vocational programmes and e-learning platforms.
Compassionate maternity, adoption, and shared parental leave policies, with up to 26 weeks leave at full pay, 13 weeks with partial pay, and 13 weeks further leave. And maternity support/paternity leave at full pay for 2 weeks, too!

You can find more details of the Benefits we offer here.  To help picture your life at MoJ Justice Digital, Data and Science please take a look at our blog.

This Post

This role will focus on bringing national and local data together and working in partnership with local areas. The postholder will lead a pilot from inception, including data acquisition, data linkage, the development of frontline tools, and hands-on analysis of multiple data sources to understand people's journeys and experiences of public services. They will also work closely with others across the data directorate and other government departments to identify use cases, assess the feasibility of future projects, explore innovative analytical solutions, and deliver analytical products.

We welcome applications from candidates to be based in either London or Leeds HQ offices (with flexible working arrangements available). Applicants must be willing to travel regularly to London and to local authorities partner sites as required.

Key Responsibilities

The core responsibilities of the role are:

Lead the development of linked national justice and local authority resident datasets and associated analysis, ensuring they are based on comprehensive, high-quality data, using robust methodology, and fit for operational, analytical, and strategic use.
Manage the delivery of data-driven tools and products that support frontline practitioners to identify need, target support effectively, and improve outcomes for people with multiple needs.
Build strong relationships with local authorities and other partners, working collaboratively to understand user needs and ensure that data products and tools are practical, flexible, and scalable across different local contexts.
Lead a small team of analysts, namely two junior analysts and any matrix managed staff, providing clear direction, coaching and support to build capability and ensure delivery of high-quality analytical outputs.

This is a new team, and you will have the opportunity to shape your role and the wider team approach and culture.

If this feels like an exciting challenge, something you are enthusiastic about, and want to join our team, please read on and apply!

Person Specification

The following experience and skills are essential:

A strong track record of developing and analysing large government datasets to deliver robust analysis. This includes data preparation, data linkage and manipulation, applying analytical techniques and quality assurance. You should be able to manipulate data in either R or Python (technical skills).
Experience of applying statistical and technical methods to deliver robust analysis to inform policy and/or operational decisions (technical skills).
Good demonstration of managing analytical or technical projects, ensuring clear plans and resources are in place, risks mitigated and outcomes are delivered to time and high quality (managing a quality service).
Good experience of managing stakeholder expectations and navigating difficult discussions, including communicating complex findings to non-technical audiences (communicating and influencing).
Strong leadership skills and the ability to work with and get the best out of a multidisciplinary team (leadership)

Willingness to be assessed against  the requirements for SC clearance

We welcome the unique contribution diverse applicants bring and do not discriminate based on culture, ethnicity, race, nationality or national origin, age, sex, gender identity or expression, religion or belief, disability status, sexual orientation, educational or social background or any other factor.

Our values are Purpose, Humanity Openness and Together. Find out more here about how we celebrate diversity and an inclusive culture in our workplace.

The Civil Service is committed to attract, retain and invest in talent wherever it is found. To learn more please see the Civil Service People Plan and the Civil Service D&I Strategy.

Salary Information**

Base salary for this role is from £63,343 to £70,725 based London location, £58,511 to £65,329 for those based on national location.

New entrants to the Civil Service joining the MoJ are expected to start at the minimum of the pay band.
Existing Civil Servants moving on a level transfer will retain their current base salary or move to the minimum of the pay band for the role, whichever is higher.
Existing Civil Servants who are promoted will either move to the bottom of the new grade’s pay band or receive a 10% uplift, whichever provides the greater increase.

How to Apply

In Justice Digital, Data and Science, we recruit using the Success Profiles Frameworks. We shall assess a combination of your Experience, Technical skills and Behaviours during the assessment process.

Stage 1 - Application and sift:

To apply for this position, you must submit the following as part of your application:

A CV detailing your career history (including any relevant qualifications). Your CV will be assessed against the essential criteria outlined within the Person Specification of this advert.
A Personal Statement (no more than 750 words) which should outline your experience and skills, giving clear examples of work undertaken. It should specifically address the following criteria listed below, using a separate paragraph for each.
Experience of analysing large government datasets to deliver robust analysis. This can include data or analytical specification, data preparation, data linking, data manipulation, analysis and quality assurance.
Experience of leading analytical projects, ensuring clear plans and resources are in place, risks mitigated and outcomes are delivered to time and high quality
Leadership skills showcasing the ability to work with colleagues from different profession to get the best out of a multidisciplinary team

A diverse sift panel will review the information in your CV and Personal Statement to assess the sift criteria specified above.  We operate an anonymous shortlisting process. Please ensure your CV and Personal Statement do not include your name or any other identifying details.

Should we receive a high volume of applications, a pre-sift based on “Experience of analysing large government datasets” will be conducted before the sift.

Please access the following link for guidance on how to apply - Application Guidance

Stage 2 - Interviews:

Successful candidates who meet the required standard will then be invited to a panel interview held via Microsoft Teams. At interview stage, you will be assessed against the following Success Profile elements - Experience, Technical and the following Behaviours:

Managing a Quality Service
Leadership

Technical skills:

Analysing large government datasets, applying statistical and technical methods

As part of your interview, you will be asked to deliver a presentation that assesses your technical experience. Further details will be provided if successful at sift.

Appointments are made strictly in merit order. In the event that two or more candidates receive identical interview scores, the Managing a Quality Service will be applied as the primary lead criterion to determine the final merit order.

Should you be unsuccessful in the role that you have applied for but demonstrate the capability for a role at a lower level, we reserve the right to discuss this opportunity with you and offer you the position without needing a further application.

Role: Head of Supplier & Service Management

Business: Office of Public Guardian (OPG)

Location: National

Contract Type: Permanent

Minimum Hours: 21 Hours per week

Organisational Overview

The Office of the Public Guardian (OPG) protects people in England and Wales who may not have the mental capacity to make certain decisions for themselves, such as about their health and finance. We are an Executive Agency of the Ministry of Justice (MoJ), set up in 2007 following the introduction of the Mental Capacity Act of 2005.

OPG is responsible for registering lasting powers of attorney (LPA) and enduring powers of attorney (EPA) and supervising deputies who are appointed by the Court of Protection.

OPG is a fantastic place to work offering a range of development opportunities.  The OPG is a disability confident employer and is committed to developing a supportive and inclusive environment that reflects the diverse community we serve.

OPG is currently delivering an ambitious transformation programme. This will change the way we provide services and help us meet the growing needs of our users, partners and our stakeholders. It will make sure our users experience a better level of support and will help us to respond to the changing needs of society. Transformation will ensure we can better support adults at risk and create high-quality services that are accessible and affordable.

Team Overview

The role will be situated in the Business Design, Development & Delivery (BD3) team within the Operational Directorate. The BD3 team covers a wide range of change-related activities including continuous improvement projects for operational teams, implementation of policy and digital changes, and involvement in OPG’s larger transformational projects. The small systems (User Defined Applications or UDAs – non-Sirius operational software) development, maintenance and improvement work is also situated within BD3. This role Will be a new role in the team. 

Duties and Responsibilities 

As Head of Supplier and Service Management, you will lead OPG's approach to operational management of key supplier-delivered services, with responsibility for supplier performance, service assurance and service management. You will be responsible for ensuring that key strategic suppliers deliver the outcomes, service levels and performance standards agreed through contractual arrangements, and that services continue to meet the needs of OPG and its customers.

Key suppliers/contracts you will be managing include:

Scanning
Remote print and post
Telephony

Working closely with Commercial, Technology, Operational and Delivery colleagues, you will establish robust operational supplier governance, performance management and service assurance arrangements, ensuring suppliers are held accountable for delivery against contractual commitments.

You will also provide leadership for OPG’s internal IT service management activities through direct line management of the SEO ITIL Service Manager, ensuring services are well governed, continuously improved and aligned to organisational needs.

Responsibilities will include, but not be limited to: 

Operational Contract and Supplier Management

Act as the senior business owner for supplier performance and service delivery management across a portfolio of digital and technology contracts.
Establish and lead effective operational supplier governance arrangements, including supplier performance management, service review boards and clear escalation processes.
Ensure suppliers deliver contracted services in accordance with agreed KPIs, SLAs and contractual obligations.
Validate supplier performance information, using data and evidence to identify performance issues, trends and areas requiring improvement.
Hold suppliers operationally accountable for underperformance and agree and oversee service improvement plans where contractual expectations are not being met.
Lead strategic supplier relationship management activities, developing constructive relationships that support effective service delivery while providing robust challenge on operational performance.
Oversee operational compliance with contractual service requirements, risk management and assurance activities.
Work collaboratively with commercial and procurement colleagues on contract variations, extensions, renewals and procurements.
Ensure contractual issues, risks and disputes are identified and managed appropriately, including escalation to Commercial where required.
Develop supplier performance dashboards and executive reporting for senior governance forums.
Identify and drive opportunities for continuous improvement, innovation, operational efficiency and improved value for money across supplier-delivered services.

Service Management Leadership

Provide leadership and strategic direction for IT service management capabilities across OPG.
Line manage and develop the SEO ITIL Service Manager.
Ensure effective management of incidents, problems, changes, service requests and service performance.
Drive continual service improvement initiatives across live services.
Ensure services are aligned with government and organisational service management standards.
Support service transition activities for new and changing digital services, ensuring operational requirements, supplier responsibilities and support arrangements are clearly understood before transition into live service.

Leadership and Stakeholder Engagement

Build effective relationships with senior stakeholders across OPG, MoJ and supplier organisations.
Provide expert advice on operational contract management, supplier performance, service assurance and service management.
Lead multidisciplinary discussions to resolve complex supplier performance, service delivery and operational issues, escalating commercial or contractual matters to Commercial as appropriate.
Contribute to strategic planning and decision-making relating to supplier-delivered services.
Champion a culture of accountability, transparency, collaboration and continuous improvement.

Agreed Expectations

The successful candidate will be expected to work from their base location on a weekly basis in line with current Civil Service requirements, outside of any reasonable adjustments.

Occasional travel to OPG sites in Birmingham and Nottingham will also be required.

The role holder will line manage the ITIL Service Manager for OPG.

Skills & Qualifications                                                                                                             

Essential Skills

Proven ability to manage complex supplier relationships and service contracts, supported by substantial relevant experience. (Lead criterion)
Experience of operational contract management and supplier performance management, including holding suppliers to account for delivery against contractual commitments, performance targets and service levels.
Strong understanding of contract management, supplier relationship management and commercial governance.
Experience of managing supplier performance through KPIs, SLAs, service reviews and improvement plans.
Excellent stakeholder engagement and influencing skills, including experience working with senior leaders and external suppliers.
Experience managing operational risks and resolving complex service delivery issues.
Experience leading and developing teams and individuals.
Strong analytical skills with the ability to interpret performance data and use evidence to drive decision-making.

Desirable Skills

The below criteria are desirable only. These will not be assessed throughout the recruitment process but will be used in the event of tied scores between candidates.

Professional qualification in contract management, procurement or commercial management (e.g. CIPS, WorldCC, Government Contract Management Capability Programme accreditation or equivalent).
ITIL Foundation or higher qualification.
Experience of Digital, Data and Technology services.
Experience of working within central government or the wider public sector.
Knowledge of Government Commercial Function standards and best practice.

Application process 

This recruitment will follow the Civil Service Success Profile process. Candidates will be expected to complete the following as part of the application:

A CV detailing your career history. CV’s will be assessed against the essential and desirable skills above.
Statement of Suitability of no more than 1,000 words, to demonstrate your experience against the essential and desirable skills required for this role.

Should a large number of applications be received, an initial sift will be conducted on the following lead essential criteria: -

Proven ability to manage complex supplier relationships and service contracts, supported by substantial relevant experience. (Lead criterion)

Interview Process

If you are successful at sift, you will be invited to an interview which will use the Civil Service Success Profiles. At interview, candidates should expect questions on:

Introduction

HM Courts & Tribunals Service is responsible for the administration of criminal, civil and family courts and tribunals in England and Wales. Our work supports the judiciary and helps people and businesses to access justice, often at significant moments in their lives. We are looking for individuals who are committed to public service and want to make a difference through the delivery of justice.

Job Description

This is an opportunity to lead Board governance at the heart of HMCTS, one of the largest and most complex operational organisations in government.

As Head of Board Secretariat and Deputy Head of Corporate Governance, you will serve as Secretary to the HMCTS Board, lead support to the Board, its committees, the Chair and Non-Executive Directors, and act as a trusted governance adviser to senior leaders.

You will shape strategic agendas, strengthen the quality of decision-making and ensure that governance arrangements support accountability, organisational performance and delivery. You will also act as the principal deputy to the Head of Corporate Governance on governance matters, leading significant improvement and reform work under delegated authority.

The role sits within an evolving function and will require flexibility, sound judgement and confidence operating with senior stakeholders. You will lead a multi-grade team and may oversee separate Board Secretariat and corporate governance portfolios as the future structure and priorities of HMCTS develop.

Your key responsibilities will include:

Key accountabilities

Leadership of HMCTS Board secretariat

The postholder will:

Serve as Secretary to the HMCTS Board, providing authoritative advice on Board procedure, responsibilities, decision routes and escalation. Lead the effective operation and continuing improvement of the Board, its committees and senior executive governance.
Focus the Board, its committees and senior executive governance on HMCTS’s key priorities by shaping strategic agendas and an integrated forward programme that anticipates dependencies, risks and capacity pressures.
Ensure Board and committee papers meet the required standard and provide clear advice or challenge where submissions are not decision ready.
Work with sponsors and senior leaders to assure clear, decision-ready governance proposals and eliminate duplication.
Strategic support for the Chair and Non-Executive Directors, and senior stakeholder influence

The postholder will:

Provide dedicated support and governance advice to the HMCTS Chair and Non-Executive Directors, enabling their effective contribution to Board business and overseeing their appointment, induction, development and engagement.
Build trusted relationships with Board and committee members, judicial office holders, Ministry of Justice colleagues and partners, providing impartial advice and influence to improve governance, manage sensitive issues and translate recommendations into practical improvements.
Deputy Leadership of Corporate Governance

The postholder will:

Act as principal deputy to the Head of Corporate Governance and Board Secretariat, advising senior leaders and translating strategic direction into effective governance, accountability and decision-making arrangements.
Lead governance improvement and effectiveness reviews arising from organisational or leadership change, using evidence, stakeholder feedback and good practice to strengthen decision-making and forum effectiveness.
Leadership and Management

The postholder will:

Lead, develop and line manage a high-performing, inclusive and resilient multi-grade team, setting clear objectives, priorities, standards and accountabilities across strategic, delegated governance and operational secretariat delivery.

The accompanying Key Accountabilities document provides further detail on the responsibilities and expectations of the role.

The postholder will be expected to work flexibly across the Corporate Governance and Board Secretariat portfolio, and the scope and responsibilities of the role may evolve in response to changing organisational priorities and governance arrangements.

Essential skills

A strong understanding of corporate governance, accountability and effective decision-making.
Experience supporting senior decision-making bodies, shaping agendas and forward programmes, and producing high-quality governance products.
Ability to provide authoritative, impartial advice and build trusted, influential senior relationships.
Strategic judgement to identify priorities, risks, dependencies and governance routes, with discretion in handling sensitive or high-profile matters.
Strong written communication skills, with the ability to analyse complex material and produce clear, concise and accurate advice.
Experience of leading teams, setting standards and developing capability.
The ability to manage competing priorities and deliver high-quality outcomes in a fast-moving and ambiguous environment.
Evidence of leading continuous improvement, organisational change or governance reform.

The following criteria are desirable. They will not be assessed as part of the main selection process but may be used as a deciding factor where candidates achieve equal scores.

Desirable skills

Experience of working directly with a Chair, Non-Executive Directors, judicial office holders, Ministers or senior public servants.
Knowledge of public body governance, departmental sponsorship or government accountability arrangements.
Experience of Board or committee effectiveness reviews, developing governance frameworks, delegations and/or terms of reference.
Knowledge of HMCTS, the Ministry of Justice or the wider justice system.
Experience of using technology or artificial intelligence to improve governance or corporate services.

The post holder will be responsible for ensuring the faith and belief systems’ needs for their respective tradition are met, for providing support to the chaplains of their tradition and for relations with their respective faith or belief system organisations. 
 
Developing and implementing a strategy for the recruitment and retention of the respective chaplains in conjunction with HMPPS Chaplaincy and Faith Services (CFS) and MoJ People Group. 
 
To collaborate with and support CFS in the delivery of chaplaincy services. 




Responsibilities, Activities and Duties      




The job holder will be required to carry out the following responsibilities, activities and duties: 
 
• Provide prison related advice and on the rehabilitation and resettlement of offenders on release into the community and potentially longer term support, those under Probation 
Supervision for their respective faith or belief system, working with CFS on the delivery of Prison Service Instruction 05/2016 Faith and Pastoral Care for Prisoners (and successor documents), related policy guidance while mindful of financial and human resources and to contribute to related Departmental and Ministerial priorities. 
•    Supporting Chaplains, CFS, Prison Group Directors (PGDs), Governors/Directors and other stakeholders, ensuring advice is provided in a timely and appropriate manner. 
•    Be proactive in the recruitment of Chaplains from the post holder’s faith or belief system through maintaining links with their respective organisation/ structures and following up interest from prospective applicants. 
•    Advise establishments on matters relating to recruitment, advising HMPPS on their respective faith and belief systems and the recruitment of their respective Chaplains.  
•    Endorse or facilitate the endorsement of their respective Chaplains. 
•    Line management responsibility for their respective Chaplains who work across multiple sites in conjunction with the establishments the Chaplains serve. 
•    As far as possible, and in conjunction with local support systems, enable pastoral care and professional support for Chaplains. 
•    With the prior agreement of the Chaplain General, work with Chaplains of their faith and belief system from other sectors, e.g. health, armed forces, higher education, on matters of common interest. 
•    Liaising with the Chaplain General and other Faith and Belief Advisers in their development of tools to enable theological engagement and reflection by Chaplains from across the faith traditions represented within prison chaplaincy and to explore how these may enable dialogue between prisoners of different faith and belief systems. 
•    Be a member of the Chaplaincy Faith and Belief Advisory Committee and work collaboratively with other members, sharing information, experience and with colleagues and where appropriate senior management.

An ability to fulfil all spoken aspects of the role with confidence through the medium of English or (where specified in Wales) Welsh.

This is a vacancy working for the Environment Agency, part of Defra Group. EA are not Civil Servants so terms will reflect that. Anyone moving from the Civil Service will lose their CS terms and benefits starting new employment with the EA
Job description

The Environment Agency are seeking a Deputy Director, Thames Strategy & Partnerships to join our Thames Programme Delivery Directorate. This is a unique opportunity to shape the future of flood resilience for London, the Thames Estuary and the wider River Thames through leadership of some of the UK's most significant and ambitious infrastructure programmes.

Reporting to the Director of Thames Programme Delivery, you will play a pivotal role in developing the long-term strategy, business cases, funding approaches and partnerships required to support the future of the Thames Estuary 2100 programme and major investment across the River Thames. At a crucial stage in programme development, you will help define the pathway for multi-billion-pound investment decisions that will protect communities, infrastructure and economic growth for generations to come.

This is a highly influential role operating at the intersection of policy, strategy, infrastructure and government. You will lead engagement across Whitehall, working closely with HM Treasury, Defra and other government departments to secure support for future investment programmes and Spending Reviews. You will also build trusted relationships with Ministers, local authorities, delivery partners and industry leaders to help shape the future of one of the UK's most important resilience programmes.

We are looking for an exceptional strategic leader with experience of developing major programmes, securing investment and operating in complex stakeholder environments. You may have gained your experience in central government, infrastructure, transport, energy, environmental resilience or another major project setting. Most importantly, you will bring strategic judgement, political awareness and the ability to navigate complex challenges while maintaining focus on long-term outcomes.

The role offers the opportunity to lead major feasibility and options development work, influence national investment decisions, and help shape the future delivery model for programmes that are expected to become increasingly prominent within government's major projects portfolio. It is an opportunity to make a lasting impact on the resilience of London and the Thames Estuary in the face of climate change

For more information, please see our candidate pack

proposals, Spending Review submissions or equivalent.

navigating complex political and organisational environments.

ministerial briefings, advice and recommendations.
• Experience leading, developing and motivating high-performing teams in complex, fast-paced environments.

leading major infrastructure programmes from an early stage of development.
• Experience leading large-scale feasibility studies, options appraisals and strategic planning activity, including securing
major funding or investment approvals through engagement with HM Treasury and other key stakeholders.
• Strong understanding of infrastructure planning and delivery, including knowledge of consenting, land acquisition,
regulatory processes, and experience within infrastructure, transport, engineering, environmental resilience or related
sectors.
• Demonstrable programme leadership, organisational credibility and commitment to professional development, including
MPLA accreditation or a willingness to work towards accreditation.
