*We offer a hybrid working model, allowing for a balance between remote work and time spent in your local office. Office locations can be found ON THIS MAP
Please note that unless you are an existing member of staff at Justice Digital, Data and Science, the only London location being recruited to is 10 South Colonnade, E14 4PU. We are no longer recruiting to 102 Petty France, SW1H 9AJ

The Role

We’re recruiting for two Lead Delivery Managers here at Justice Digital, Data and Science to be part of our warm and collaborative Probation Digital Team, and the Office of the Chief Technology Officer.

This role aligns against Delivery Manager Profession from the Government Digital and Data Framework

Lead Delivery Managers are accountable for effective delivery of groups of products and are responsible for the recruitment and performance management of delivery managers within their area. They also remain ‘hands-on’, supporting high-priority product delivery.

Lead Delivery Managers define and implement standards and processes for delivery and are experienced in leading multidisciplinary teams that build, support and continuously improve products of significant scale and complexity.

As a Lead Delivery Manager, you will have a proven ability in successfully delivering large software development projects/programmes. This is a high-impact role where you will be building, maintaining and motivating teams; protecting them and making sure the teams in your area collaborate effectively. You’ll coach teams and facilitate a culture of continuous improvement, proactively managing dependencies and risks to overcome obstacles to delivery. 

As an Agile delivery leader in our organisation, you will have a proven record of working with senior leaders, stakeholders and third parties to drive agile transformations at an organisational level. You will be part of our digital delivery leadership community driving cultural and procedural change and embedding Agile approaches and ways of working. With a strong background as a Scrum Master or Agile Coach (or similar roles) you will primarily focus on delivery strategy, while supporting the creation of self-organising and high-performing teams, supported closely by Senior Delivery Managers.

You will have the ability and experience of establishing/driving Agile delivery/transformations, through a solid coaching background. As well as demonstrating your leadership qualities in building new teams through hiring of FTEs but also using managed services suppliers.

The Team

Probation Digital

Probation Digital is a rapidly growing and transforming organisation. It works to deliver and maintain sustainable live services and new products that support staff who work with vulnerable members of society. It is an organisation built up of experts in UCD, software development, agile and product disciplines who collaborate together to create an inclusive culture and work towards strategic goals to improve operational services in His Majesty’s Probation Service.

Office of the Chief Technology Officer

The Chief Technology Office sets technical direction across the organisation. It defines standards, shapes shared platforms and ways of working and supports teams to build and operate systems that are secure, reliable and sustainable.
We aim to enable teams across MoJ and accelerate digital delivery by identifying common user needs and organisational challenges, and delivering high-quality, user-centred solutions.

We are driving key transformations across MoJ while transitioning to a product operating model, ensuring we continue to deliver measurable value to users at pace. With products and services across engineering, data architecture and governance.

You’ll receive a range of excellent benefits when you join our department, including:

A generous employer pension contribution of 28.97% through the Civil Service Pension Scheme.
25 days of annual leave, (increasing to 30 days once you have reached 5 years of service), plus 8 bank holidays and a privilege day for the King’s birthday.
Flexible working arrangements including hybrid working, working part time or compressed hours. Designed to support a positive work–life balance.
Build and lead an Agile Delivery Management function with approximately 15 Delivery Managers managing upwards of 50 digital products. 
Accountability for product implementation planning with the associated product managers ensuring backlog items are addressed and prioritised alongside other deliverables.
Lead project planning and work closely with the Lead Product Manager ensuring MVPs are clearly defined and value slicing is optimised for delivery.
Line management and coaching of Senior Delivery Managers.
Responsibility for managing the contingent labour or other 3rd party suppliers. who augment the civil service workforce, ensuring 3rd party resources are managed effectively and in line with the contractual obligation.
Tracking and reporting of KPIs such as cycle time, throughput/velocity, bug arrival/departure rates, progress against roadmap, project delivery forecasting etc, across a group of products.
Managing escalations to senior leadership. As a senior level professional, providing effective interface with the highest levels within the organisation and bringing strategic value to the relationship.
Defining and monitoring policies and procedures for the Delivery Management profession.
Responsibility for contract and budget management working closely with the Commercial and Finance teams to appropriately manage public finances.
Coordinating the teams' project plans, roadmaps, risk assessments, sprint boards and retrospective lessons to ensure usefulness, engagement, accountability and predictability.
Optimising the teams' backlog, ensuring it has enough buffer, correct priorities, stories are well understood, have adequate acceptance criteria in alignment with definition of ready.
Developing, guiding and improving process related ceremonies (refinement, planning, standups, demos and retrospectives).
Employees are allocated 10% of their working time for personal and professional development.
A £1k per person learning budget is in place to support all our people, with access to best-in-class conferences and seminars, accreditation with professional bodies, fully funded vocational programmes and e-learning platforms.
Compassionate maternity, adoption, and shared parental leave policies, with up to 26 weeks leave at full pay, 13 weeks with partial pay, and 13 weeks further leave. And maternity support/paternity leave at full pay for 2 weeks, too!

You can find more details of the Benefits we offer here. To help picture your life at MoJ Justice Digital, Data and Science please take a look at our blog.

Key Responsibilities:

If this feels like an exciting challenge, something you are enthusiastic about, and want to join our team please read on and apply!

Person Specification

Essential

Agile and Lean practices (skill level: expert) You know how to coach and lead teams in Agile and Lean practices. You are a recognised expert that advocates these approaches, continuously reflecting and challenging the team. You can create or tailor new ways of working; you are always innovating.
Commercial management (skill level: expert) You can act as the escalation point and resolve large or high-risk commercial management issues. You know how to coach others in appropriate commercial management. 
Communication skills (skill level: expert) You can mediate between people and mend relationships, communicating with stakeholders at all levels. You can manage stakeholder expectations and facilitate discussions about high risk and complexity even within constrained timescales. . You can speak and represent the community to large audiences inside and outside of government. 
Life-cycle perspective (skill level: expert) You know how to successfully lead teams through the full product life cycle. You can identify which tools and techniques should be used at each stage. You can develop sustainable support models. You can identify and deal with potential risks across or between all stages of the product life cycle. You know how to coach others. You can contribute to the assessment of other teams, providing guidance and support as they move through stages of the product life cycle. 
Maintaining delivery momentum (skill level: expert) You know how to optimize the delivery flow of teams. You actively address the most complicated risks, issues and dependencies including where ownership exists outside the team or no clear ownership exists. You can identify innovative ways to unblock issues. 
Making a process work (skill level: expert) You can identify and challenge organizational processes of increasing complexity and those processes that are unnecessarily complicated. You can add value and can coach the organization to inspect and adapt processes. You know how to guide teams through the implementation of a new process. 
Planning (skill level: expert) You know how to lead a continual planning process in a very complex environment. You can plan beyond product delivery. You can identify dependencies in plans across services and coordinate delivery. You know how to coach other teams as the central point of expertise.
Team dynamics and collaboration (skill level: expert) You know how to change organisational structures to fixable and sustainable designs. You can lead on strategy for an entire organisation, joining up business needs with innovative analysis. You can make and justify decisions characterised by high levels of risk, impact and complexity. You know how to build consensus between organisations (private or public) or highly independent and diverse stakeholders. You can solve and unblock issues within teams or departments at the highest level. You understand the psychology of a team and have strong mediation skills. You can coach an organisation on team dynamics and conflict resolution.

About the job
Job summary

​​Applications for this role are restricted to existing officers or staff of a UK police force or UK policing organisation.​ 

About us: 

PoliceAI is a nationally significant technology and transformation programme in UK policing. Backed by central government investment and positioned at the heart of the police reform agenda, PoliceAI is the new National Centre for AI in Policing, helping to shape how policing uses data, technology and artificial intelligence to tackle crime, protect the public and modernise frontline operations. 

We bring together operational policing, technical expertise, product delivery, assurance and the responsible use of AI to develop and scale capabilities that improve public safety outcomes. Our work helps forces respond more effectively to demand, strengthen investigations, identify risk and harm earlier, and free up frontline time for the activities that matter most to communities. 

This is an opportunity to contribute to a programme with national reach and meaningful public service impact, helping to define how AI is developed, governed and adopted across one of the UK’s most important public services. The work is varied and complex, moves at pace, and has the potential to deliver better tools for policing, better outcomes for the public, and stronger foundations for the responsible use of AI. 

PoliceAI is hosted within the College of Policing.  

About the College of Policing: 

Our mission is: Leadership, Standards, Performance. This guides our work with individuals, forces, and policing partners towards our vision. We exist to support police officers, police staff and volunteers to deliver the best service to the public. Only through high quality leadership, consistent standards and continual performance improvement can everyone in policing reach their full potential. Our mission guides our work with individual, forces and partners towards our vision. 

We offer a supportive and inclusive environment for people to thrive through our extensive flexible-working policy, employee wellbeing support, family friendly policies, and status as a disability confident leader. 

For further information visit our ‘Work for us’ page. 

Location:

This role is available as a designated homeworking role, remote working (anywhere in the UK). Please note some travel may be required.  

Job description

We are looking for people who are motivated by public service, interested in responsible innovation, and comfortable working collaboratively across organisational, operational and technical boundaries. Joining PoliceAI means contributing to a supportive, multidisciplinary team that is helping to shape the future of policing and ensure AI is used in ways that are effective, responsible, operationally useful and worthy of public trust. 

As a Co-pilot Developer, you will help shape how policing adopts and benefits from Microsoft Co-pilot, AI agents and automation technologies. Working as part of the national PoliceAI programme, you will support the development, testing and refinement of Co-pilot solutions that can be used across forces to improve productivity, consistency and efficiency. Your work will help ensure AI enabled tools are reliable, safe and effective, enabling policing organisations to realise greater value from emerging technologies while maintaining appropriate governance and responsible AI principles.   

We're looking for someone who has strong frontline operational Policing experience and combines technical curiosity with a practical approach to problem solving. You will have experience working with digital systems, automation services, AI-enabled tools or IT support environments and be confident collaborating with a range of stakeholders to develop and improve solutions. Successful candidates will be comfortable learning about emerging technologies, refining agents and prompts, supporting user adoption, and ensuring solutions remain secure, well governed and aligned to organisational needs. 

Additional Information: 

We recruit by merit on the basis of fair and open competition, as outlined in the Civil Service Commission's recruitment principles.  

Due to our status as Public Servants, we are not eligible to participate in the Civil Service transfer process. Therefore, while successful candidates can transfer into the organisation on their existing terms and conditions, any move back to the Civil Service may mean that continuity of service is not automatically recognised by the receiving department, and new starter or modernised terms and conditions may apply, subject to the receiving department's policies and arrangements. However, employees who move directly to a Civil Service department without a break in service may retain continuity of service for redundancy and pension purposes.  

Any previous service with local government or other external Modification Order bodies will not be carried forward or count when calculating redundancy entitlement.  

The College embraces diversity and promotes equal opportunities. As such, we comply with the Disability Confident Scheme (DCS) and apply the minimum selection criteria at sift stage of the recruitment process. Where necessary, we may increase the minimum selection criteria to support the effective management of the recruitment process, while ensuring our approach remains fair, transparent and consistent with our Disability Confident commitments. 

Person specification

Some of your responsibilities will include: 

Developing, testing and refining Copilot agents, prompts and automation solutions that support policing organisations to work more effectively.  
Supporting the adoption and ongoing improvement of AI-enabled solutions by identifying issues, analysing performance and implementing enhancements.  
Creating and maintaining prompt libraries, templates, guidance and supporting documentation to promote consistent and safe use of Co - pilot technologies   
Working with colleagues and stakeholders to transition new AI and automation solutions into sustainable operational use.  
Ensuring AI-enabled tools operate within agreed governance, security and responsible AI frameworks, escalating risks and issues where appropriate.  

To be successful in this role you’ll need:  

Experience working with digital technologies, automation services, AI-enabled tools or IT support environments.  
The ability to develop, test, refine or support digital solutions while applying structured problem-solving and service management approaches.  
Strong analytical and communication skills, with the ability to work collaboratively with stakeholders and translate requirements into practical solutions.  
An understanding of information governance, data sensitivity, security requirements and the safe use of AI-enabled technologies.  
A proactive approach to learning, continuous improvement and helping users gain maximum benefit from emerging technology.

Things you need to know:

The Cyber Threat Team sits within the Risk and Capabilities Unit. We support His Majesty’s Prison and Probation Service (HMPPS) to understand and respond to digital offending and technology-related risks. Working with internal teams and partner organisations, the team helps strengthen cyber awareness, develop practical guidance and improve how people whose offending involves technology are managed.

As Projects, Policy and Insights Manager, you will use evidence, analysis and stakeholder engagement to support delivery, inform decisions and develop clear, practical guidance for colleagues across HMPPS.

The role focuses on three connected areas:

Insight and reporting

Managing and developing new reporting and insight capabilities, identifying trends and risks, and turning information into clear insights for decision-making and future planning.

Policy and guidance

Supporting policy and guidance that helps staff identify, assess and manage technology-related offending risks, using evidence and operational insight to ensure products are practical and proportionate.

Project delivery

Leading or supporting projects that improve practice across prisons, probation and partner organisations.

About you

You will need to understand, or quickly develop an understanding of, the criminal justice system and be able to explain the risks linked to the current cyber threat landscape and online criminality.

We are looking for a confident and curious self-starter with strong research skills, sound judgement and an interest in developing creative ways to communicate cyber and digital subject matter to operational teams. You will be security minded, comfortable working with others to solve problems, and able to turn complex information into clear, practical outputs for prisons, probation, approved premises and youth custody services.

About the Risk and Capabilities Unit:

The Risk and Capabilities Unit (RaCU) sits within the Directorate of Security and is comprised of three distinct pillars:

1)    Operational Countermeasures (includes the Cyber Threat Team)
2)    Personnel Security Countermeasures
3)    Procedures, Practice and Capability.

RaCU is dedicated to identifying and prioritising security risk and providing and enhancing capabilities in prisons, probation and youth custody to counter them.

The term ‘Capabilities’ covers a wide spectrum of support and interventions. For example, our technological or physical advances to detect, prevent usage of, or disable illicit items; our formal training and skilling; our clear and constant learning communications; as well as our contemporary security procedures and practice improvement to enable staff to perform their duties consistently well.

These are all ‘Capabilities’ and give people the tools to achieve.

Our purpose is to identify and prioritise live and future risks, and in turn provide a range of creative and effective capabilities to support others to manage, mitigate or remove them.

About the job
Job summary

Are you an experienced public sector finance leader? Could you contribute at board level to scrutinise and assure financial management, risk, control and governance in an independent public body? Would your career benefit from that experience?

We are seeking an independent, financially qualified, Member of our Audit and Risk Committee. The Committee is a critical part of our governance which supports the Board and Chief Executive manage risk, control, governance and finances.

Formed of two non-executive Board members, and an independent member, the Committee is also attended by the Chief Executive and Accounting Officer, and other senior officials.

It meets quarterly, with one additional meeting each year to scrutinise the annual report and accounts. Each meeting is held virtually, for two hours.

This is a voluntary position, which will suit a finance leader in the public sector seeking exposure to working at board level in an arm’s-length body. The time commitment is for meeting preparation and attendance, and any other engagement and support agreed to enable you to contribute at your best, for example through briefings with senior staff, the Committee Chair or others in advance of key issues being debated.

The Office for Environmental Protection’s mission is to protect and improve the environment by holding Government and public authorities to account. We cover England, Northern Ireland, and environmental matters reserved to the UK government. We have 80 staff based in Worcester and Northern Ireland.

We report independently to Parliament and the Northern Ireland Assembly on progress against environmental targets. We also report on how effectively environmental law is implemented, and advise on changes to environmental laws. We receive complaints from the public, and investigate and can enforce potential failures to comply with environmental law by public bodies.

To find out more about the OEP, what we do, who we are and our current work, visit the OEP website . You may want to review the annual report from the Audit and Risk Assurance Committee, to understand the work of the Committee.

Given our independent role to hold government and other public authorities to account, we manage conflicts of interest very carefully. We are open to applicants in a wide range of roles. It is likely to be most difficult to manage conflicts of interest from applicants working within those organisations most often subject to our oversight in Defra and its arm’s-length bodies.


 

Job description

Drawing on your professional expertise and experience, you will provide independent insight, constructive challenge and objective scrutiny. You will help the OEP maintain high standards of governance, accountability, financial management and organisational resilience as it delivers its mission to protect and improve the environment. 

You will;

Provide independent and objective scrutiny of the OEP’s governance, risk management, internal control and assurance arrangements. 
Review the comprehensiveness and reliability of assurances provided to the Committee and the Board, identifying gaps and areas where further assurance may be needed. 
Advise and constructively challenge senior leaders on the effectiveness of internal controls, audit arrangements and the management of strategic and emerging risks. 
Scrutinise financial management, financial reporting and the annual report and accounts, helping to ensure that public money is used properly, transparently and with regard to value for money. 
Engage effectively with internal and external audit, supporting the Committee’s oversight of audit plans, findings, recommendations and management responses. 
Contribute fully to collective Committee discussions and decisions, while exercising independent judgement and maintaining appropriate confidentiality. 
Promote high standards of integrity, propriety, accountability and public service. 



Person specification

Essential criteria

Recent experience of operating in a senior role with financial responsibilities in a public body, government department, or similar.
A strong understanding of governance, risk management, internal control and assurance, supported by sound financial acumen.
Sound judgement and the confidence to offer constructive, straightforward and proportionate challenge to senior leaders.
A commitment to public service, the Seven Principles of Public Life and the OEP’s purpose and independence.
The capacity to devote sufficient time to the role, including preparation, meetings, induction and any relevant training.
A relevant professional qualification in areas such as accountancy or audit.


Qualifications
A relevant professional qualification in accountancy or audit such as CCAB, CIMA (or equivalent).
Benefits

This post is being advertised on a voluntary basis only and attracts no pay. All meetings will be held online.

The time commitment is 1 day per quarter to attend a maximum of five two-hour meetings with necessary preparation time. The appointment will last for a minimum of 1 year, up to a maximum of 3 years.

By taking the opportunity to volunteer as part of the OEP ARAC, you will:

use your skills and knowledge to gain valuable experience and exposure working at board level in a public sector arms length body
use your experience to provide independent insight, constructive challenge and objective scrutiny
gain valuable career experience
participate in a new interesting challenge
expand your network

The Role

Please note this role requires you to pass Security Check clearance. Please click on the link for details.

We’re recruiting for Senior Quality Engineers here at Justice Digital, Data and Science to be part of our warm and collaborative Digital Probation and Legal Aid (LA) Digital teams.

This role aligns against Senior Test Engineer from the Government Digital and Data Framework

Probation Digital builds and supports digital services that probation practitioners rely on every day to manage risk, record accurate information, and deliver effective supervision. These services directly support better outcomes for individuals, communities and the justice system as a whole. Our work is essential to public safety and to the people under probation supervision.

Legal Aid Digital seeks to provide swift access to legal aid for those who need it and ensure efficient payment to providers of those services. Our work is incredibly important to some of the most vulnerable people in our society.

As a Senior Quality Engineer, you will assist teams to build quality into the products and services they deliver. You will work with multidisciplinary teams to engineer quality throughout the delivery lifecycle.

You will work early and collaboratively with product, delivery, architecture, software engineers, operational colleagues and other quality engineers to help teams deliver services that are reliable, accessible, secure, performant and maintainable.

You will help teams understand and manage quality risk, build effective quality practices into their ways of working, and use automation and engineering approaches to provide fast, reliable feedback. You will bring specialist expertise where it is needed, while enabling teams to adopt effective quality practices and take greater ownership of quality.

You will be part of a wider Quality Engineering community, sharing knowledge, developing standards and practices and helping others grow their quality engineering capability. You will have opportunities to develop your own technical and leadership skills through knowledge sharing, mentoring others, communities of practice, involvement in wider quality initiatives and helping to improve quality engineering capability.

The products and services you work on will vary, giving you the opportunity to work with different technologies, teams and challenges and to shape how quality is engineered across complex digital services.

You will be hands-on , working directly with teams to apply quality engineering practices, investigate risks and build automated and exploratory testing solutions. You will also work across team and service boundaries where needed, particularly where there are complex integrations, dependencies or end-to-end risks.

You’ll receive a range of excellent benefits when you join our department, including:

A generous employer pension contribution of 28.97% through the Civil Service Pension Scheme.
25 days of annual leave (increasing to 30 days after 5 years of service), plus 8 bank holidays and a privilege day for the King’s birthday.
Flexible working arrangements including hybrid working, working part-time or compressed hours. Designed to support a positive work–life balance.
Employees are allocated 10% of their working time for personal and professional development.
A £1k per person learning budget is in place to support all our people, with access to best-in-class conferences and seminars, accreditation with professional bodies, fully funded vocational programmes and e-learning platforms.
Compassionate maternity, adoption, and shared parental leave policies, with up to 26 weeks leave at full pay, 13 weeks with partial pay, and 13 weeks further leave. And maternity support/paternity leave at full pay for 2 weeks, too!

You can find more details of the Benefits we offer here. To help picture your life at MoJ Justice Digital, Data and Science please take a look at our blog.

Key Responsibilities:

Work collaboratively with multidisciplinary teams to engineer quality throughout the delivery lifecycle to live service.
Enable teams to own and improve quality, providing coaching, guidance and practical support while bringing hands-on experience where it adds value.
Provide technical and strategic leadership for multiple product teams, ensuring alignment with service outcomes and business goals.
Develop and apply risk-based quality strategies, identifying quality risks, dependencies and opportunities for early intervention.
Be hands-on where required, designing, developing and maintaining automated tests and quality checks, and undertaking exploratory testing to investigate risk and uncertainty.
Advance automation initiatives, extending and standardising automated testing solutions using appropriate tools and frameworks.
Apply appropriate testing and quality practices across API, integration and end-to-end testing, working with engineers to establish effective coverage at the right levels.
Work with others to improve testability and observability and promote shared ownership of quality.
Contribute to quality across functional and non-functional areas, including accessibility, security, performance, resilience and maintainability.
Work closely with the Lead Quality Engineer to develop, apply and continuously improve quality standards, patterns and best practices, ensuring they are practical, proportionate and appropriate to the context.
Use evidence from testing, delivery and live service to make quality, risk and confidence visible and support informed decisions.
Implement shift-left testing practices, enabling early defect detection and prevention.
Provide technical quality expertise across team and service boundaries, helping identify and address gaps in assurance.
Coach and mentor colleagues and contribute to the Engineering community, sharing learning and building capability.
Continuously improve quality strategies, processes and tooling and continuously explore and adopt effective approaches, tools and technologies.
People manage and develop other Quality Engineers, supporting their growth and career progression.

If this feels like an exciting challenge, something you are enthusiastic about, and want to join our team please read on and apply!

Person Specification

Essential

Experience overseeing testing across multiple teams throughout the software development lifecycle, demonstrating both technical and test leadership.
Practical experience of quality engineering within modern software delivery, with the ability to work collaboratively and to be hands on where required.
Experience of designing and implementing automated tests, with a good understanding of where different types of testing and quality checks provide value.
Demonstrable experience designing, implementing and optimising automated UI and API test frameworks using tools such as Playwright, Selenium, Cypress, Bruno and Pact, driving quality through the adoption of test automation best practice and the integration of testing within CI/CD pipelines and source control environments.
Experience applying risk based and exploratory testing approaches to identify and investigate quality risks and uncertainty.
The ability to work across functional and non-functional quality, considering areas such as accessibility, security, performance, resilience and maintainability.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to use evidence to understand risk, investigate failures and improve quality.
The ability to enable and influence others to adopt holistic quality practices, communicating effectively, including with people who are not quality specialists.
A commitment to continuous learning and improving quality engineering practice, with the curiosity to learn new technologies, approaches and Coaching others

Role: Executive Assistant to the Transformation Director 

Business: Office of Public Guardian (OPG)

Grade: EO (Executive Officer)

Salary: £29,303 – £31,061 (National), £33,551 – £35,564 (London)

Contract Type: Fixed-term Appointment (18 months)

Minimum Hours: Full-time

Organisational Overview

The Office of the Public Guardian (OPG) protects people in England and Wales who may not have the mental capacity to make certain decisions for themselves, such as about their health and finance. We are an Executive Agency of the Ministry of Justice (MoJ), set up in 2007 following the introduction of the Mental Capacity Act of 2005.

OPG is responsible for registering lasting powers of attorney (LPA) and enduring powers of attorney (EPA) and supervising deputies who are appointed by the Court of Protection.

OPG is a fantastic place to work offering a range of development opportunities. The OPG is a disability confident employer and is committed to developing a supportive and inclusive environment that reflects the diverse community we serve.

OPG is currently delivering an ambitious transformation programme. This will change the way we provide services and help us meet the growing needs of our users, partners and our stakeholders. It will make sure our users experience a better level of support and will help us to respond to the changing needs of society. Transformation will ensure we can better support adults at risk and create high-quality services that are accessible and affordable.

Team Overview

This is a critical, fast-paced role at the heart of the Transformation Directorate in the Office of the Public Guardian, working closely with and providing direct support to the Transformation Director.

We are looking for a confident, proactive and highly organised individual who is comfortable taking ownership, using their initiative and building strong relationships with colleagues at all levels. You will need to be able to anticipate priorities, manage competing demands and exercise sound judgement in a busy and changing environment.

At the core of the role is the effective management of the Transformation Director’s diary, inbox and day-to-day business. You will play an important role in ensuring their time and attention are focused on the right priorities, identifying issues that require action and helping to maintain effective communication and coordination across the Directorate.

You will be trusted to work with a high degree of autonomy, using your judgement to manage and respond to correspondence on behalf of the Transformation Director, prioritise and delegate requests, and make decisions about meeting invitations and diary commitments.

You will work closely with the Directorate Business Manager and build strong relationships across the Transformation Directorate, OPG and wider stakeholder network.

Duties and Responsibilities 

Inbox management: Proactively manage and triage the Transformation Director’s inbox, identifying priorities and ensuring correspondence is actioned, delegated, signposted or responded to promptly. Use judgement to deal with issues where appropriate and ensure the Transformation Director is sighted on key information, decisions and emerging priorities.
Diary management: Take ownership of the Transformation Director’s diary, confidently managing competing demands and prioritising their time. Schedule and coordinate meetings, organise travel, plan visits and engagements, and prepare daily schedules to ensure they are well prepared and their time is used effectively.
Business coordination: Anticipate upcoming commitments and requirements, helping to ensure the Transformation Director has the information and materials they need and following up actions with colleagues where required.
Information and records management: Set up and maintain effective team filing and information-management systems, ensuring records are managed appropriately in line with GDPR and OPG governance requirements.
Meeting support: Provide occasional secretariat support, including coordinating agendas and papers, recording key actions and decisions, and tracking actions through to completion.
Directorate support: Provide administrative support for the Directorate’s Reward and Recognition process and other Directorate-wide activity as required.
Relationships and stakeholder management: Build strong and effective working relationships across the Directorate, with other Private Offices and with colleagues and stakeholders across OPG and MoJ.
Communications and engagement: Support the Business Manager with Directorate communications, including sharing key updates and messages and supporting Directorate-wide meetings, events and engagement activity. Take an active role in maintenance of the Directorate’s SharePoint.
Directorate culture and continuous improvement: Play an active role in the wider Directorate, contributing to events, initiatives and resources and identifying opportunities to improve how the team works.
Undertake other reasonable duties as agreed with your manager.

Agreed Expectations

The successful candidate will be expected to work from their base location on a weekly basis in line with current Civil Service requirements, outside of any reasonable adjustments. Ad hoc travel to Birmingham/Nottingham/London may be required.

Skills & Qualifications

Essential Skills

Highly organised and proactive: Proven ability to take ownership, anticipate what is needed and manage multiple competing demands effectively in a fast-paced environment. (Lead)
Sound judgement and initiative: Able to work with a high degree of autonomy, prioritise effectively and make confident, appropriate decisions, knowing when to act independently and when to escalate.
Confident communicator: Able to communicate clearly, confidently and professionally with colleagues and stakeholders at all levels across OPG and MoJ.
Strong relationship-builder: Able to build trusted relationships with a range of stakeholders, including senior leaders, using tact, diplomacy and good judgement.
High standards and attention to detail: Takes pride in delivering high-quality work, with the ability to manage tasks reliably and follow through on actions.
Strong digital skills: Confident using Microsoft 365 tools, including Outlook, Teams, Word, Excel, PowerPoint and SharePoint.
Discretion and confidentiality: Able to handle sensitive information appropriately and maintain confidentiality at all times.

Prior experience of working in a private office or secretarial/administrative function.

About the job
Job summary

GCHQ is an intelligence, cyber and security agency with a mission to keep the UK safe. We use cutting edge technology, ingenuity and partnerships to identify, analyse and disrupt threats. Working with our intelligence partners MI5 and MI6, we protect the UK from terrorism, cyber attacks and espionage. At GCHQ you’ll do varied and fascinating work in a supportive and inclusive environment that puts the emphasis on teamwork.

Our GCHQ strategy focuses on:

delivering impact where it is needed most;
harnessing technology to operate at the edge of impossible;
investing in our people to build an inclusive, diverse workforce; and
being a well run organisation.

Further information can be found here.

Job description

About the Role

We are seeking a Non-Executive Director to join our Board of Directors with recent and extensive experience of large scale digital and technological delivery and innovation.

This position complements the balance of skills, experience, and perspectives of our existing Board. Working with our executive and non-executive directors in a dynamic and demanding environment, you will help to shape, scale, and promote the long-term sustainable success of GCHQ.

As a Board member you will contribute your knowledge and expertise to the Board’s collective decision making, formulating strategy, providing direction and assessing performance. You will help us achieve cultural change and our Equality, Diversity and Inclusion (EDI) ambition.

You will act as a critical friend to the Director, and coach executives as required. You will bring independent and constructive challenge, along with advice, to help set our future direction navigating complex digital modernisation and responding to the opportunities and risks of AI at the pace of the frontier.

Key responsibilities:

Provide strategic advice to help set our future direction as we move into a fast-paced changing world, navigating complex digital modernisation;
Provide external and independent views on large digital transformations and AI adoption, readying us to consume advanced services, future-proofing our processes, and enabling this at scale;
Be able to offer informed challenge on GCHQ’s major strategic technology challenges;
Shape and embed our purpose, values, and strategy, ensuring cultural alignment;
Provide an internal and independent view on the running of the business, ensuring high levels of appropriate accountability and governance best practice are upheld;
Provide independent counsel to the Director, acting as a trusted sounding board in specialism or more generally;
Provide independent oversight and challenge of executive and business performance, ensuring it is strategically aligned and prioritised;
Ensure the Board is operating within the risk appetite and risk management framework agreed by the Board;
Ensure that workforce policies and practices are consistent with GCHQ’s values and support long-term sustainable success;
Provide valued input and contribution to Board meetings and, where appropriate, constructive independent challenge to the thinking and decision-making of the Executive Board;
Ensure the effective implementation of Board and Committee decisions by the Director and executives;
Actively participate in Board Committees and sub-committees, supporting and chairing where required;
Advise and support other members of the department on defined topics and support, mentor, and coach directors where requested;
Regularly update own skills, knowledge, and familiarity with the business, risks to the business, and regulatory environment

As the Tech and Digital Lead NED, you will also be expected to:

Attend, in person, the GCHQ Board and annual offsite. This will include preparation / reading time in advance (often on location at secure sites) and on occasion, pre-briefs, to ensure the necessary background and knowledge for full participation in Board activities. Plus ad-hoc support to the department, and attendance at any other relevant committees or sub-committees.
Allocate sufficient time to discharging the key responsibilities of this role.
Complete all mandatory training.
Regularly update and refresh your skills, knowledge, and familiarity with GCHQ’s business, the risks it runs, and the legal framework and ethics with which it must comply.
Have a high degree of resilience, integrity, and impartiality, avoiding conflicts of interest.
Adhere to, and promote, GCHQ values and behaviours.
Undertake duties in accordance with the Cabinet Office Code of Conduct for Board Members.
Person specification

About You – Person Specification

Experience

We are seeking recent and extensive experience of:

Working at board and executive level in an organisation of scale and complexity.
Leadership within a leading-edge technological environment and technical industry experience.
Delivering significant transformation and able to offer informed challenge on GCHQ’s major strategic technology challenges.
A track record of achievement in digital/technological improvement, innovation, and research & development.
Leading large operational businesses through large scale change, including people and cultural aspects of change, and the associated challenges.
Supporting, mentoring and coaching Directors.
Delivering EDI initiatives and organisational culture change.




Desirable:

NED experience.
Operating in a political environment with complex operational challenges and multiple collaborative dependencies.
Working directly with central government and in a large-scale regulatory environment.
Balancing the needs of a variety of stakeholders.



Skills and Qualities

Provide advice to help set our future direction as we operate in a fast-paced changing world.
Have the intellect, breadth of vision, inclusion, and team focus that will enable full contribution to strategic discussions.
Bring a truly independent perspective and original input to board meetings, and constructive challenge to strategy, process, and practice at a high level.
Proven track record of holding executive teams to account.
Motivated to act in the public interest to make a meaningful contribution to the governance of an organisation of critical national importance.
Absorb complex issues quickly, see what is important and articulate confidently and clearly.
Be a calm and considered listener, with an open approach, good emotional intelligence, and the ability to develop effective relationships.
Be comfortable with ambiguity and uncertainty.



KEY TERMS

Fee payable: c.£1000 per day, dependent upon attendance

Location: Required to attend meetings at sites across the UK.

Time commitment: Up to 20 days a year - 9 board meetings plus a strategic away day, plus any board committee commitments and sub-committees.

Allowances: Reasonable travel & subsistence (we are a public sector body and bound by public finances, ethics, and integrity in how public money is spent)

Term: Three-year period with a formal review point after two years.

Notice: 3 months

Things you need to know
Artificial intelligence
Artificial intelligence can be a useful tool to support your application, however, all examples and statements provided must be truthful, factually accurate and taken directly from your own experience. Where plagiarism has been identified (presenting the ideas and experiences of others, or generated by artificial intelligence, as your own) applications may be withdrawn and internal candidates may be subject to disciplinary action. Please see our candidate guidance (opens in a new window) for more information on appropriate and inappropriate use.
Selection process details


Selection Process and Timetable

Our recruitment process is fair, transparent, and based on merit.

The closing date for applications is 30th October 2026 at 10am. We ask that you submit your applications as early as possible to ensure that they are processed before this deadline; any late applications received are unlikely to be considered.

Please note that you will initially be required to complete a short eligibility application and Situational Judgement Test, before you are invited to complete the full application form which will include the submission of:

Suitability Statement (1000 words) evidencing how you have met the experience, skills and qualities detailed in the person specification.
CV and Technical Career Summary.

The application process in in depth and can take significant time to complete, so we strongly advise leaving plenty of time in advance of the closing date to complete and submit your application.


Application Stages:

You must successfully pass each stage of the process to progress to the next.

Your application will be sifted to assess your evidence against the person specification as detailed in this job description.
    - scheduled for w/c 9th November 2026
If longlisted, you will participate in a telephone interview with our recruitment partners.
    - scheduled for w/c 16th & 21st November 2026
If shortlisted at telephone interview, you will be invited to participate in a Technical Panel Discussion with a small group of GCHQ staff. This will be held virtually, with full details of the assessment process made available to shortlisted candidates.
    - scheduled for w/c 14th December 2026
You will be invited to attend a panel interview held in person, where your motivational fit, values, competency evidence and technical experience will be assessed.
    - scheduled for w/c 4th January 2027
If successful at panel interview, you will be invited to a face-to-face discussion with Anne Keast-Butler, Director GCHQ.
    - scheduled for w/c 11th January 2027

Please note that these dates are subject to change, and we do ask that you employ flexibility throughout the process with regards to your availability.

For more information about the role or a confidential discussion please contact confidential@recruitmentoffice.org.uk

Eligibility

To be eligible to apply, you must be a British Citizen. One of your parents must be a British Citizen or must have the nationality or citizenship from our approved list of countries. If you hold dual nationality, of which one component is British, you will nonetheless be considered. You can apply at the age of 17 years, if successful you will not be offered a start date prior to your 18th birthday.

For more information, visit here.

Candidates must normally have been resident in the UK for seven out of the last ten years. This is particularly important if you were born outside the UK. Candidates will, however, be considered if they have, for example, served overseas with HM Forces or in some other official capacity as a representative of Her Majesty’s Government, studied abroad or lived overseas with their parents. Further guidance around eligibility can be sought from us around candidates with private sector experience who have spent significant periods in the last 10 years working abroad.

Successful candidates will have to hold or obtain Developed Vetting – this is the highest form of security clearance. As part of the vetting process, candidates will have to complete a number of vetting forms including a financial questionnaire and have a confidential security interview with a trained vetting officer. Developed Vetting clearances are subject to review.

We have a strict drugs policy, so once you start your application, you cannot take any recreational drugs and will need to declare your previous drug usage at the relevant stage.

Discretion is vital. You should not discuss your application, other than with your partner or a close family member. Successful candidates would not normally be able to disclose that they are a NED for the organisation.

There must be no conflict of interest(s), including other roles in your portfolio, or national security conflicts.

You should only launch your application from within the UK. If you are based overseas, you should wait until you visit the UK to launch an application. Applying from outside the UK will impact on our ability to progress your application.

Equal Opportunities

Diversity and inclusion are critical to our mission. To protect the UK, we need a truly diverse workforce that reflects the society we serve. This includes diversity in every sense of the word: those with different backgrounds, ages, ethnicities, gender identities, sexual orientations, ways of thinking and those with disabilities or neurodivergent conditions. We therefore welcome and encourage applications from everyone, including those from groups that are under-represented in our workforce such as women, those from an ethnic minority background, people with disabilities and those from low socio-economic backgrounds.

Find out more about our culture, working environment and diversity on our website.

We’re Disability Confident

We are proud to have achieved Leader status within the DWP’s Disability Confident scheme.  This is aimed at encouraging employers to think differently about disability and take action to improve how they recruit, retain and develop disabled people.  Being Disability Confident, we aim to offer a person-to-person interview to any candidate who self-identifies as disabled and meets the essential criteria for the role.  This is our ‘Offer of Interview’ (OOI). To secure an interview for this vacancy, the essential criteria (in order of application process) are:

You'll be required to reach the minimum pass mark for the online Situational Judgement Test (SJT), which assesses criteria important for all roles in our organisation.
Demonstrate senior leadership skills within a leading-edge technological environment, with significant technical industry experience and a track record of achievement in improvement, innovation, and R&D.

Demonstrate the ability to communicate effectively, provide constructive challenge and build confidence with a wide range of stakeholders – to be assessed at application sift.

There is a wide range of extra support available throughout the recruitment process to enable you to do your best, see our website for information on reasonable adjustments we can offer.

Job summary

We are seeking a creative Communications Manager to play a key role in the Media and Communication (M&C) team, enhancing the reputation of the Royal Air Force (RAF) among our target audiences.

The RAF M&C organisation is responsible for the delivery of communications that influence how people inside and outside the RAF understand, engage with, and think about us.

We work closely with the Ministry of Defence communications team, other communications teams across the Armed Forces, and the wider RAF Family of organisations that support our Whole Force.

RAF M&C is part of the Government Communication Service and we use the OASIS framework for strategic communications and the four communication competences of Insight, Ideas, Implementation, and Impact.

You will be responsible for owning and delivering proactive campaigns that support our communication priorities.

You will contribute creative ideas to lead projects and campaigns to engage target audiences across traditional, digital and social media channels.
You will also have responsibility for leading and delivering the PR for some of the RAF’s exciting national and international TV and film opportunities.

•    Effective oral and written communication skills.
•    Good understanding of excel, data gathering and reporting
•    Strong report writing skills
•    Willingness to learn new skills and work at pace

Desirable    
•    Working with Parole Board members or within another membership organisation
•    Understanding of the parole process
•    Understanding of the delivery requirements of the Parole Board

Main Duties

Strategy

Contribute to a capability and learning and development strategy for all members.
Provide relevant capability data to the Senior Member Capability Manager and Member Capability Managers to facilitate long term planning for the Board.
Promote an organisational culture of learning, transparency, fairness and independence.

Delivery of core L&D programme

Support the delivery of the core L&D programme for members ensuring this develops to meet changing needs and fully utilises innovative approaches to L&D in person and hybrid events including but not limited to:
New member induction training
MCA training
Chair training
Support the implementation of new e-learning systems
Track and record data and outcomes accurately
Collate and evaluate feedback from members on the accreditation programmes with the view of improving future programmes
Provide administrative support for Practice Developers and Training facilitators in delivering the programmes.
Work closely with the other colleagues across the Board, such as Listings and MCA teams to support and deliver plans for member’s progression to the relevant casework.

Capability and accreditation

Support planning and delivery of accreditation programmes: training, practice development and quality development
Proactively engage with Members so that they remain committed and engaged on their accreditation pathway and that they achieve accreditation in a reasonable timeframe
Appropriately escalate with the Member Capability Manager and Senior Member Capability Manager when members do not progress on their accreditation pathway
Monitor and update records and data to report on capability, member progression and accreditation, to inform training needs and business priorities.
Make suggestions for improvements in the delivery and administration of member accreditation programmes and work with the Capability Manager to implement these.

Engagement and L&D events

Support, plan and deliver member engagement and L&D events including but not limited to:
Parole Board and/or Chair Conferences
Networking events
Forums
Following feedback from the Standards team or other area of the business work with the Member Capability Manager and Senior Member Capability Manager to introduce new engagement and L&D events for members to improve their capability.

Relationship building

Be a reliable and supportive source for all members.
Work closely with the other Member Capability Executive Officers understanding each other’s designated areas of responsibility to build resilience.
Work closely with the Standards team to share learning and outcome reports where appropriate
Build excellent working relationships with colleagues across the Board.
Establish and maintain strong relationships with members who support L&D as facilitators, practice developers, quality developers and delegates.
Build and maintain collaborative working relationships with external stakeholders to ensure the Parole Board’s L&D needs are fully supported.
Work closely with the Staff and Member Recruitment and Member Engagement Team within the Corporate Services Hub. Report on data requested by the team and flag member welfare concerns where appropriate.

Working pattern:  Full-time, Part-time, Flexible working

Contract Type: Permanent

Number of vacancies: 4

Vacancy number: 23278

*We offer a hybrid working model, allowing for a balance between remote work and time spent in your local office. Office locations can be found ON THIS MAP
Please note that unless you are an existing member of staff at Justice Digital, Data and Science, the only London location being recruited to is 10 South Colonnade, E14 4PU. We are no longer recruiting to 102 Petty France, SW1H 9AJ.

The Role

Please note this role requires you to pass Security Check clearance. Please click on the link for details.

We’re recruiting for Lead Software Developers here at Justice Digital, Data and Science to be part of our warm and collaborative Legal Aid Agency (LAA) Digital team.

This role aligns against Lead Developer from the Government Digital and Data Framework.

We really want to hear from people who value making a difference and building user-centred services using modern tools and practices as part of a highly collaborative team. We strongly encourage empathetic approaches and cross functional working and are looking for people to help build on this culture of agility and openness.

As an example, you could be helping teams that are:

·      Building services to enhance an application for legal aid

·      Developing services to process and review applications for legal aid caseworkers

·      Providing access to court data

·      Building services to provide access to historic applications

You’ll receive a range of excellent benefits when you join our department, including:

·      A generous employer pension contribution of 28.97% through the Civil Service Pension Scheme.

·      25 days of annual leave, (increasing to 30 days once you have reached 5 years of service), plus 8 bank holidays and a privilege day for the King’s birthday.

·      Flexible working arrangements including hybrid working, working part time or compressed hours. Designed to support a positive work–life balance.

·      Employees are allocated 10% of their working time for personal and professional development.

·      A £1k per person learning budget is in place to support all our people, with access to best-in-class conferences and seminars, accreditation with professional bodies, fully funded vocational programmes and e-learning platforms.

·      Compassionate maternity, adoption, and shared parental leave policies, with up to 26 weeks leave at full pay, 13 weeks with partial pay, and 13 weeks further leave. And maternity support/paternity leave at full pay for 2 weeks, too!

You can find more details of the Benefits we offer here. To help picture your life at MoJ Justice Digital, Data and Science please take a look at our blog.

Key Responsibilities:

In addition to hands-on development, you will inspire, mentor, coach, manage and lead Software Developers within a business domain. You will focus on generating a culture of quality, maintaining balance between building sustainable well architected products and unlocking citizen value early.

The areas of your responsibility for leadership will shift between people, architecture, development and product strategy, depending on context and need.

You will have responsibility for one team, or two small related teams, and report to the Principal Developers.

Technical Leadership:

·      Collaborate with Technical Architects and Product Managers to set product direction

·      Collaborate with Technical Architects to help in the design of systems and implementation of coherent and sustainable technical roadmaps

·      Lead discussions with Developers to nurture consensus on technical/team decisions

·      Support backlog refinement, helping plan, define and prioritise actionable tasks for the team

·      Build inclusivity and understanding by promoting strategies to share technical knowledge of our systems with appropriate documentation and other activities

·      Support Delivery Managers in unblocking value where necessary and/or honest representations of effort in an agile environment as the teams learn more

Engineering Management:

·      Managing, coaching and growing people with a focus on their wellbeing and development

·      Support Delivery Managers in improving team maturity

Engineering Profession:

·      Work with your local Principal Developers and the wider community to improve and maintain good coding standards and practices

·      Help provide feedback on wider technical strategy of your business unit

·      Share knowledge and build enthusiasm for sharing via activities like brown bags, cooperative workshops, chat discussions and other means

·      Encourage open discussion and drive communities in our primary communication tools

·      Have a mindset for growth and learning, looking for emerging technologies, tools and good practice

·      Help build and maintain a diverse, inclusive culture across the development community, growing awareness, inclusivity, and balance

·      Take part in the recruitment and onboarding of other Developers

Our Tech Stack

We rely on Java, Python or Ruby to write our application code, GitHub Actions for CI/CD, Sentry for application monitoring, Kubernetes and Docker to schedule and run our services (read about our Cloud Platform), AWS for most of our infrastructure, GOV.UK Design System for our web interfaces and use MacBook Pros.

For front-end development, we value a robust understanding of the underlying web technologies. We value well-maintained, open-source tools that can be used to produce semantic HTML, performant CSS and unobtrusive JavaScript with Express.js and TypeScript, and we assess all our services against accessibility criteria.

We’re happy to help you learn our tech stack once you’re part of our team, and do not require an exact match in your experience of languages. Check out GitHub for a closer look at the technologies we use, and a complete list of services that we build and maintain. We subscribe to the manifesto for agile software development.

If this feels like an exciting challenge, something you are enthusiastic about, and want to join our team please read on and apply!

Person Specification

Essential

●      You have experience making and guiding complex technical decisions and contributing to technical strategy.

●      You have experience nurturing a culture of good software practice that makes change easy.

●      You have contributed towards building a high performing, inclusive team culture.

●      You have experience in delivering value sooner and safer, through DevOps, XP or other ways of working that lead to agility and collaboration.

●      You have experience either coaching or managing other people.

●      You have been involved in building or contributing to a community of practice.

●      Contribution towards the team e.g. being point of contact or team advocate, working with stakeholders, helping with Delivery Manager and Product Manager DM/PM activities, improving processes.

●      Contribution towards other developers: e.g. coaching / training / inspiring; encouraging L&D.

Willingness to be assessed against the requirements for SC clearance

We welcome the unique contribution diverse applicants bring and do not discriminate based on culture, ethnicity, race, nationality or national origin, age, sex, gender identity or expression, religion or belief, disability status, sexual orientation, educational or social background or any other factor.

Our values are Purpose, Humanity, Openness and Together. Find out more here about how we celebrate diversity and an inclusive culture in our workplace.

The Civil Service is committed to attract, retain and invest in talent wherever it is found. To learn more please see the Civil Service People Plan and the Civil Service D&I Strategy.

Salary Information**

Base salary for this role is from £63,343 – £70,725 (London), or £58,511 – £65,329 (National)

·      New entrants to the Civil Service joining the MoJ are expected to start at the minimum of the pay band.

·      Existing Civil Servants moving on a level transfer will retain their current base salary or move to the minimum of the pay band for the role, whichever is higher.

·      Existing Civil Servants who are promoted will either move to the bottom of the new grade’s pay band or receive a 10% uplift, whichever provides the greater increase.

·      Candidates may also be eligible for a non‑pensionable Government Digital & Data Allowance of up to £14,882 per year (London) or £14,939 (National). This is a temporary allowance, reviewed annually and may be retained, amended, or withdrawn.

The final offer will reflect the skills and experience you demonstrate during the assessment process.

How to Apply

In Justice Digital, Data and Science, we recruit using a combination of the Government Digital and Data Profession Capability and Success Profiles Frameworks. We shall assess a combination of your Experience, Technical skills and Behaviours during the assessment process.

Stage 1 - Application and sift:

To apply for this position, you must submit the following as part of your application:

·      A CV detailing your career history (including any relevant qualifications). Your CV will be assessed against the essential criteria outlined within the Person Specification of this advert.

·      A Personal Statement (no more than 750 words) which should outline your experience and skills, giving clear examples of work undertaken. It should specifically address the following 4 criteria listed below, using a separate paragraph for each.

-              You have experience making and guiding complex technical decisions and contributing to technical strategy.

-              You have experience in delivering value sooner and safer, through DevOps, XP or other ways of working that lead to agility and collaboration.

-              Contribution towards the team e.g. being point of contact or team advocate, working with stakeholders, helping with Delivery Manager and Product Manager DM/PM activities, improving processes.

-              Contribution towards other developers: e.g. coaching / training / inspiring; encouraging L&D.

Candidates who do not adhere to the Personal Statement directions above may be rejected on this basis.

A diverse sift panel will review the information in your CV and Personal Statement to assess the sift criteria specified above. We operate an anonymous shortlisting process. Please ensure your CV and Personal Statement do not include your name or any other identifying details.

Please access the following link for guidance on how to apply - Application Guidance

Stage 2 - Interviews:

Successful candidates who meet the required standard will then be invited to a panel interview held via Microsoft Teams. At interview stage, you will be assessed against the following Success Profile elements - Experience, Technical and the following Behaviours:

·      Leadership 

·      Working Together 

·      Developing Self & Others  

·      Making Effective Decisions 

·       Delivering at Pace  

Appointments are made strictly in merit order. In the event that two or more candidates receive identical interview scores, the Leadership Behaviour will be applied as the primary lead criterion to determine the final merit order.

Should you be unsuccessful in the role that you have applied for but demonstrate the capability for a role at a lower level, we reserve the right to discuss this opportunity with you and offer you the position without needing a further application.

A reserve list may be held for up to 12 months, from which further appointments may be made.

Terms & Conditions

Please review our Terms and Conditions which set out how we recruit and provide further information related to the role and salary arrangements.

MOJ is one of the largest government departments, employing around 70,000 people (including those in the Probation Service), with a budget of approximately £9 billion. attendance centres

A prison and probation service that reforms offenders

This role allows some remote working. 

Overview of the job      

The Long Term and High Security Intelligence Unit is responsible for collating, analysing and disseminating data relating to all counter terrorism, corruption prevention, serious and organised crime and general intelligence to and from the 13 establishments in the Long Term and High Security Estate. 
 
The post holder will work within one of the above functions, which will be indicated at the time of advertising the post.  
 
The post holder will play a critical role in developing the intelligence picture on a range of threats impacting on their area, drawing on existing intelligence products as well as developing their own analysis. The post holder will be responsible for providing quality assured strategic and tactical intelligence analysis which will look across prisons and probation contexts at ‘high priority’ offenders, offending groups and operational security vulnerabilities in their area. 
 
The post holder will report to the functional lead who in turn reports to the Head of Security and Intelligence LTHSE. 
 
The post holder may be expected to travel between LTHSE sites, as well as regional offices and HQ at times. The base location can be in a number of locations nationally. 
 
This is a non-operational role with no line management responsibilities.  

Summary      

The Long Term and High Security Prisons Group Intelligence Unit has a dual function; to develop operational policy, set national intelligence requirements and tasking and share best practice in relation to the management of offenders charged under antiterrorism legislation and offenders that exhibit extremist behaviours during their time in custody. Additionally it leads on supporting and advising the DDC and Governors on intelligence around Counter-Terrorism, Organised Crime, threat groups and general intelligence capabilities. 
 
The post holder will contribute towards the High Security Estate intelligence picture by analysing data and identifying key chains in collaboration with the team, establishments and management. The role will include identification of gangs, prisoner networks and analysing the impact of operational incidents. 
 
The post holder will also be expected to provide professional support and advice to intelligence analysts in HMPPS operating at local levels.  
 
The post holder will be expected to develop and deliver a high quality intelligence analytical service to the LTHSE and law enforcement partners. 

Responsibilities, Activities and Duties      

The job holder will be required to carry out the following responsibilities, activities and duties:  
 
•    Build productive working relationships with the wider analytical community in HMPPS, with related data analysis functions and with law enforcement partners to develop quality intelligence products.  
•    Work with intelligence consumers to ensure analytical products meet their needs – seeking and acting on feedback.  
•    Take an active role in HMPPS’ intelligence analyst community, supporting own and colleague’s professional development. 
•    Act as a Point of Contact (PoC) for all prisons to be a source of information, guidance, support and challenge in all CT and Intelligence matters.  
•    Partnership working with Police, Probation and Security Services: The HSIA is part of the national Point of Contact for Police, Probation and Security Services.  
•    Support the tactical management and transfer of known nominal within and between regions, liaising with prisons, SOCT Directorate and Police to best manage the risks posed.  
•    Support prisons in using Pathfinder to actively manage terrorist or suspected extremist prisoners through management action and further investigation.  
•    Training: To support establishment CT, Security and Intelligence teams by providing information and training where required in order to support these teams.  
•    Produce a weekly briefing based on notable incidents, gang activity, mobile phone finds and population statistics for distribution to senior managers and security departments within the directorate.  
•    Produce a monthly intelligence report in order to identify relevant patterns or trends from identified key threat priorities; Reporting and advising on what is important to the LTHSE, including issues of potential threats/risks; 
Identifying/Understanding intelligence gaps; Reporting and advising on setting intelligence requirements.  
•    Maintain Subject Profiles on those prisoners identified as LTHSE Nominals.  
•    Analyse trends, hot spots and general profile analysis, in order to identify potential areas of concern.  
•    Produce and present key findings to the Directorate on all non‐CT intelligence as and when required, flagging up key and emerging issues appropriately.  
•    Support the Category A Team with producing an intelligence picture of High Risk and Exceptional Risk prisoners within dictated timescales. 
•    Support the Long-Term and High Security Estates Population Management Strategy by providing sound intelligence led decision making regarding moves for potentially difficult prisoners. 
•    Support the 13 establishment intelligence functions by providing information around key themes and threats. 
•    Direct tasking directives for the LTHSE as a result of the above. 

The duties/responsibilities listed above describe the post as it is at present and is not intended to be exhaustive. The job holder is expected to accept reasonable alterations and additional tasks of a similar level that may be necessary. Data is at the heart of everything we do at Companies House.

As we continue our digital transformation, we're investing in our Data Architecture capability to improve data quality, modernise technology, and enable better decision-making across the organisation. Data Architecture is a critical capability that supports our strategic objectives and future ambitions.

We're looking for an experienced professional join us as a Senior Technical Architect (Data). Working across Data and Technical Architecture, you'll help shape the future of data at Companies House, collaborating with technical and business stakeholders to solve complex challenges, define architecture direction, and establish data standards that support long-term organisational goals.

This is an exciting opportunity for someone who thrives in complex environments, is comfortable working through ambiguity, and can influence stakeholders by translating technical concepts into practical solutions. Influence data-related decisions across programmes, projects and product teams

BPSS is an entry level security check. It uses the Police National Computer (PNC) to make sure a candidate has no convictions. The check returns evidence of any current criminal record and un-spent convictions under the Rehabilitation of Offenders Act 1974.
