About the job
Job summary

We're looking for a skilled communications professional who is passionate about strengthening communities and improving people's lives. You'll lead high-profile communications campaigns, work closely with government and senior stakeholders, and showcase how our funding is helping people and places thrive.

We’re recruiting for a Communications Manager (FTC ending in March 2028) in England to play a pivotal role in helping The National Lottery Community Fund to strengthen society as we deliver on our strategy, It Starts With Community.

Job description

You'll play a key role in delivering high-profile communications campaigns that support the distribution of hundreds of millions of pounds of Dormant Assets funding (money from long-forgotten bank accounts) to communities across England. Working closely with government, senior stakeholders and colleagues across the Fund, you'll help build awareness, inspire participation and demonstrate the impact of this investment.

The job will focus on two multi-million-pound funding programmes:

The Community Wealth Fund – a long-term investment programme that gives local communities the power to improve where they live.
The Youth Enrichment Fund - investment that helps disadvantaged young people access opportunities in the arts, culture, sports, and wider youth services, aimed at improving wellbeing and employability.

In this role, you’ll work closely with government and colleagues across the Fund to deliver integrated, multi-channel communications activities that effectively promote these programmes and showcase their impact on the communities we serve. Your work will help shape public understanding of the schemes, inspire communities to engage with them, and build trust with key stakeholders.

Key responsibilities may include:

Develop deep insight into these programmes, to enable you to implement effective communications plans for them while supporting Strategic Communications Leads to build and manage matrix teams.
Design, develop, and deliver messaging, narrative and content, as well as social and brand assets, working closely with colleagues in the wider team to deliver effective and impactful communications activities.
Build positive relationships with government comms and policy counterparts as well as with teammates and colleagues across the Fund to make programme communications relevant and resonate internally and within Government departments (specifically DCMS and MHCLG) and, most importantly, the communities we serve.
Work closely with colleagues in the media team to deliver integrated activities, monitoring media and advising on opportunities and risks. Ensure rapid response to emerging issues with processes and protocol on lines to take and spokespeople.

We are looking for a calm and organised strategic communicator and storyteller able to swiftly build relationships and adapt. You’ll be experienced in developing integrated campaigns and working across teams to deliver high-impact communications. The role will involve some travel from time to time.

Interview details:

Date: 16-17 November
Format: Online
Location: England.

We have a hybrid approach to working. Work pattern and location to be agreed with the successful candidate. The role can be based at any of our England offices: Birmingham, Exeter, Leeds, London, Manchester and Newcastle.

To ask any questions, please email: recruitment@tnlcommunityfund.org.uk

Upload your CV in word format and write a supporting statement (1000 words) with the above criteria, we will use this to score your application.

Demonstrable experience in a communications role within a complex organisational environment
Track record in planning and delivering integrated communications campaigns, with experience managing matrix teams
Excellent content and copywriting abilities, used to producing assets to tight deadlines. Able to adapt tone and style for different audiences and channels
Experience in complex institutions, involving colleagues and stakeholders up to leadership level
Project management abilities – confident working in a matrixed organisation with competing deadlines
Experience of strategic communications counsel and advising senior leaders and stakeholders, particularly in times of reputational risk and crisis management
Experience of working in high-pressure situations and an ability to adapt calmly to changing deadlines and requirements with short notice.
 Desirable
Experience in government and / or the voluntary, community and social enterprise sector.

Equity, Diversity and Inclusion  

Communities in the UK come in all shapes and sizes. National Lottery funding is for everyone – therefore, we are committed to equity, diversity and inclusion and we work hard to ensure our funding reaches where it is needed.  

We also believe our people should represent the communities, organisations and individuals we work with. That’s why The National Lottery Community Fund is committed to being an inclusive employer and a great place to work. We recognise and celebrate the fact that our people come from diverse backgrounds. We positively welcome applications from people from ethnic minority backgrounds, people with disabilities or longstanding health conditions, people who are LGBTQ+, and people from different socio-economic and educational backgrounds, as well as people of all ages. 

As a Disability Confident Employer, we take a proactive approach in making reasonable adjustments, if needed, throughout the recruitment process and during employment. (This can be related to a physical and mental health condition.)

About the job
Job summary

This post is open to applicants who can meet the College’s nationality, UK residency and vetting requirements, see below for details.  

About us:

PoliceAI is a nationally significant technology and transformation programme in UK policing. Backed by central government investment and positioned at the heart of the police reform agenda, PoliceAI is the new National Centre for AI in Policing, helping to shape how policing uses data, technology and artificial intelligence to tackle crime, protect the public and modernise frontline operations. 

We bring together operational policing, technical expertise, product delivery, assurance and the responsible use of AI to develop and scale capabilities that improve public safety outcomes. Our work helps forces respond more effectively to demand, strengthen investigations, identify risk and harm earlier, and free up frontline time for the activities that matter most to communities. 

This is an opportunity to contribute to a programme with national reach and meaningful public service impact, helping to define how AI is developed, governed and adopted across one of the UK’s most important public services. The work is varied and complex, moves at pace, and has the potential to deliver better tools for policing, better outcomes for the public, and stronger foundations for the responsible use of AI. 

PoliceAI is hosted within the College of Policing.  

About the College of Policing: 

Our mission is: Leadership, Standards, Performance. This guides our work with individuals, forces, and policing partners towards our vision. We exist to support police officers, police staff and volunteers to deliver the best service to the public. Only through high quality leadership, consistent standards and continual performance improvement can everyone in policing reach their full potential. Our mission guides our work with individual, forces and partners towards our vision. 

We offer a supportive and inclusive environment for people to thrive through our extensive flexible-working policy, employee wellbeing support, family friendly policies, and status as a disability confident leader. 

For further information visit our ‘Work for us’ page.

Location 

Remote working (anywhere in the UK). Please note, some travel may be required. 

Job description

We are looking for people who are motivated by public service, interested in responsible innovation, and comfortable working collaboratively across organisational, operational and technical boundaries. Joining PoliceAI means contributing to a supportive, multidisciplinary team that is helping to shape the future of policing and ensure AI is used in ways that are effective, responsible, operationally useful and worthy of public trust. 

The National Centre for AI in Policing is leading one of the most significant technology investments in modern policing, helping forces across the country adopt artificial intelligence in a responsible, secure and operationally effective way. As a Senior Platform Engineer, you will play a key role in designing, building and operating the cloud platforms that underpin this work, creating secure, reliable and scalable environments that support engineers, data scientists and AI specialists to deliver impactful solutions. 

We're looking for an experienced platform engineer who combines deep technical expertise with a practical, collaborative approach. You'll be confident leading complex technical delivery, making informed architectural decisions and driving high engineering standards through coaching and mentorship. You'll bring strong experience of cloud platforms, automation and modern engineering practices, alongside the ability to balance security, reliability, performance and cost while working with both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

Additional Information: 

We recruit by merit on the basis of fair and open competition, as outlined in the Civil Service Commission's recruitment principles.  

Due to our status as Public Servants, we are not eligible to participate in the Civil Service transfer process. Therefore, while successful candidates can transfer into the organisation on their existing terms and conditions, any move back to the Civil Service may mean that continuity of service is not automatically recognised by the receiving department, and new starter or modernised terms and conditions may apply, subject to the receiving department's policies and arrangements. However, employees who move directly to a Civil Service department without a break in service may retain continuity of service for redundancy and pension purposes.  

Any previous service with local government or other external Modification Order bodies will not be carried forward or count when calculating redundancy entitlement.  

The College embraces diversity and promotes equal opportunities. As such, we comply with the Disability Confident Scheme (DCS) and apply the minimum selection criteria at sift stage of the recruitment process. Where necessary, we may increase the minimum selection criteria to support the effective management of the recruitment process, while ensuring our approach remains fair, transparent and consistent with our Disability Confident commitments. 

Person specification

Some of your responsibilities will include: 

Leading the design, delivery and ongoing improvement of secure cloud platform services, coordinating technical work across engineers and delivery partners. 
Developing reusable infrastructure, automation and CI/CD solutions that improve consistency, quality and speed of delivery. 
Building self-service tools, deployment patterns and platform capabilities that support engineering, data and AI teams. 
Driving platform reliability through monitoring, incident management, operational readiness and continuous service improvement. 
Embedding security, governance and cost optimisation into platform design and operation, while supporting evaluation of technologies and suppliers. 

To be successful in this role you’ll need: 

Significant experience designing, building and operating production cloud platforms, ideally using Azure or comparable cloud technologies. 
Strong expertise in infrastructure as code, CI/CD pipelines, automation and modern engineering practices. 
Experience leading technical delivery, mentoring engineers and providing guidance across complex projects and stakeholders. 
A strong understanding of platform reliability, observability, incident management and operational resilience. 
Experience implementing security controls and working within regulated or security-conscious environments. 

Please see the attached job description which contains full details of the role. Please read the key criteria section in the job description (linked with the advert) carefully before applying. As part of the application process, you will be required to complete the following:

2) Personal Statement (500 words maximum) - Your personal statement should provide a clear, concise, and compelling account of why you are applying for the role, the skills and experience you would bring, and how you meet the essential criteria. While evidence and examples are important, the statement should read as a coherent and engaging narrative rather than a series of separate responses to individual criteria. 

To ensure you are assessed on merit alone, we ask you to anonymise your application. This means removing personal identifiers such as your name, age, and place of education. You do not need to remove your employment history, job titles, or any information about your work.

Stage 1 - Interview (30 minutes)
A competency-based interview focusing on your experience, suitability for the role, and the skills and knowledge outlined in the role profile. Only the highest-scoring candidates will progress to Stage 2.

Stage 2 - Assessment (60 minutes)

Interviews are currently anticipated to take place on 13th and 14th November. Please note that these dates are subject to change due to the operational requirements and availability of the interview panel.

Job description

As a Marine Office Dedicated Oral Examiner, you will conduct oral examinations of Marine Engineers and/or Masters and Mates, depending on your professional qualifications and discipline. Your work will help ensure that seafarers meet the required standards of knowledge, training and competence before being issued with a Certificate of Competency or Certificate of Equivalent Competency.

You will join the Maritime and Coastguard Agency’s UK Technical Maritime Services Directorate, which is responsible for the survey and inspection of UK and foreign-flagged vessels in UK waters, as well as supporting maritime safety, environmental protection, officer certification and seafarer competency standards.

Your responsibilities will include, but aren’t limited to:

When appropriately qualified as either an Engineer or Nautical examiner, the primary purpose of this role is to undertake oral examinations of seafarers leading to the issue of either Certificates of Competency (COC’s) or Certificates of Equivalent Competency (CEC’s), ensuring high standards of training and competence amongst seafarers holding UK certificates.
Undertake UKLAP examinations.
Implementing the requirements of STCW convention as amended for seafarers on UK vessels and for seafarers with UK Certificate of competency.
Provide advice to industry and the public in accordance with MCA policies, including acting as a point of contact for oral exam related. Contributing to the management of a first-class oral examination service by the MO to customers and stakeholders of the MCA.
Work with the BM and the MO Technical/Business Delivery teams in providing a customer service experience that both meets and manages expectations.
Contributing to the delivery of a regulatory climate that is clear, consistent, and supportive of UK maritime industries.
Contribute to internal projects i.e. digitisation of oral exams and MCA assessments etc.
Assisting in respect of readiness for both internal and external Audits of the Branch, ensuring that records are maintained in accordance with MCA policies.

The purpose is to identify any public posts or content that could raise concerns for employers, such as:

Hate speech or discriminatory behaviour
Threats or acts of violence
Illegal activity or substance misuse
Sexually explicit material
Extremist views or affiliations

About the job
Job summary

The Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA) is the UK's sovereign regulator for medicines, including biological medicines, medical devices and blood products. At the heart of its purpose is protecting public health, ensuring that medical products available to patients are safe and effective while enabling innovation to reach patients appropriately.

Today, that mission is increasingly international. Science and life sciences innovation do not stop at national borders, and neither can effective regulation. New medicines, technologies and ways of developing them are moving rapidly, making strong relationships between regulators, governments, researchers and industry more important than ever.

For the MHRA, international partnerships are therefore not simply about exchanging information. They are about building the relationships and connections that allow regulators to respond intelligently to innovation, learn from one another and create opportunities to work together where doing so can deliver better outcomes for patients.

This is a rare opportunity to take on a genuinely influential international role at an important moment for the MHRA and for UK life sciences. Our ambition is not simply to have a presence in the United States, but to build relationships that make a real difference: to patients, to innovation and to the UK's position as a global life sciences leader.

 The relationship between the UK and US is central to that ambition. Through the MHRA–FDA Pioneer Programme, we have an opportunity to deepen our relationship with one of the world's most important regulatory authorities, strengthen scientific and regulatory collaboration and create new connections across two of the world's leading life sciences ecosystems.

Job description

We are looking for a Regional Deputy Director of US Partnerships to join our International Partnerships Team within the Innovation & Compliance Group. The International Partnerships Team is responsible for shaping policy to guide the MHRA’s operations, for developing the global partnerships that the MHRA needs to be successful.

The role will serve as MHRA’s dedicated Liaison Officer to the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) under the MHRA-FDA Pioneer Programme. This role represents a significant milestone in UK–US regulatory collaboration, building on the UK-US pharmaceutical partnership. 

As MHRA’s senior representative in the United States, you will play a pivotal role in strengthening one of the Agency’s most important international relationships. Working at the heart of global regulatory policy, you will help advance collaboration in innovative medicines, medical devices, artificial intelligence and other emerging technologies, while supporting our shared commitment to protecting public health and fostering innovation. 

The MHRA-FDA Pioneer Programme formalises the longstanding partnership between the MHRA and FDA through dedicated liaison officer roles in both organisations. The programme is designed to strengthen scientific collaboration, support regulatory innovation and increase the exchange of expertise, while fully preserving the independent decision-making responsibilities of each regulator. 

The programme will help both organisations respond more effectively to emerging regulatory challenges, support resilient supply chains, strengthen clinical research oversight and accelerate collaboration in areas such as rare diseases, real-world evidence and innovative healthcare technologies. 

The successful candidate will maintain strong links with the MHRA in the UK and benefit from ongoing support, throughout their deployment. The experience and skills gained will bring significant value back into the Agency.

Person specification

Please refer to candidate pack for full details

Key responsibilities

Senior Representation and Advocacy.  Representing MHRA’s position as a global regulatory leader at senior-level meetings, international forums, and science diplomacy events. Act as MHRA’s senior representative with the FDA and in relevant international fora. 

Strategic Partnership Management.  Develop and maintain a strong, trusted relationship between the MHRA and FDA. Support long-term strategic engagement between both agencies and wider stakeholders. 

Programme and Project Leadership. Lead the delivery of high-profile bilateral initiatives, including joint inspections, reliance projects and regulatory policy collaborations. Ensure programmes are delivered to a high standard, on time and with measurable impact. 




Coordination, Intelligence and Policy Delivery 

Oversee effective communication and information sharing between the MHRA and FDA. 
Provide strategic regulatory intelligence and insights from MHRA leadership. 
Deliver high-quality briefings, policy advice and recommendations to ministers and senior officials. 

Leadership. Motivate others, use judgement to take decisions in real time. Actively promote the reputation of the MHRA with pride, both internally and externally

Essential criteria:

Experience of working within the life sciences, pharmaceutical, MedTech, BioTech or related sectors.
Proven senior leader with a strong track record of delivering high-impact, fast-paced and complex programmes and driving strategic outcomes across international organisational boundaries.
Highly developed strategy skills with the ability to align international collaboration, policy and partnerships with wider UK Government priorities, economic growth, public health and international objectives.
Exceptional interpersonal and relationship building skills, with a proven ability to develop trusted and influential networks across government, industry and international partners, fostering strong collaboration and long-term partnerships.
Proven international diplomacy skills, with experience navigating complex political, cultural and organisational environments and managing high-profile domestic and international engagements.
Strong judgement and decision-making, with the ability to operate confidently with a high degree of autonomy and resilience.

 Desirable criteria:

Experience of developing and delivering international policy, partnerships or diplomacy

This Estate Facilities Manager (EFM) position is based in Cyprus, within a joint services environment. An Estate Facilities Manager (EFM) plays a significant part in the delivery of services to our customers on a day-to-day basis focusing on the management of all services delivered in buildings, accommodation and workplaces, leading the operational oversight, delivered either directly or through a third-party supplier partner. 
A Facility Managers key responsibility is to reduce asset down time (by providing proactive asset management advice to Customers), so they fail less often; and when they do fail, they are fixed quickly (in line with Accepted Level of Performance (ALP)).

Cypriot nationals/Cypriot dual nationals are eligible to apply for this post, however you may be subject to taxation by both Cyprus and the UK Governments. About the job
Job summary

Applications for this role are restricted to existing officers of a UK police force or UK policing organisation.

The College consists of more than 850 staff who are passionate about policing and delivering for our communities.

Our organisational values guide how we work.

▪ Inclusive: we connect with our policing colleagues and our communities to ensure that we understand the complexities and realities of policing.

▪ Innovative: we are dynamic and responsive at both an individual and organisational level.

▪ Open: we act with honesty and integrity, and we will account for our actions.

▪ Collaborative: we collaborate with policing to tackle complex challenges in the public interest.

Examples of our work can be viewed on our website.

Formed in 2012, the College is an operationally independent arm's length body of the Home Office. We have dedicated ourselves to understanding the key issues facing policing, responding to them dynamically and strengthening our connection to all parts of the service.

Colleagues are organised into professional communities and business units. Core work and busin​ess plan deliverables are organised​ into portfolios. People and skills are drawn from our ​professional communities into each programme of work or ​project. Our organisation chart is shared below.

Job description

The Director of Operational Standards is a senior national leadership role, operating at the heart of the policing system. The breadth of the role is significant, spanning multiple areas of operational policing and requiring sustained engagement with the Home Office, national policing governance structures and Chief Constables across England and Wales.

The role sits at the intersection of standards, assurance and system leadership. Success depends on the ability to navigate complexity, balance competing priorities and make informed decisions about where the College can add the greatest value. This includes exercising judgement on when the College should lead delivery directly, and when responsibility is better held elsewhere in the system, taking account of capacity, capability and long‑term impact.

Stakeholder management is a defining feature of the role. Many of the most influential conversations take place at Chief Constable and Director level and require confidence, credibility and political awareness. The postholder must be able to position the College’s role clearly and constructively, particularly where decisions are contentious or where expectations across the system are misaligned.

The role also requires a willingness to step into difficult and high‑profile issues, including those arising from high‑impact reviews and inquiries. This involves ensuring learning is translated into practical standards, guidance and assurance activity that supports improvement and builds confidence across policing. Judgement is frequently required where evidence is complex, perspectives differ and there is no straightforward solution.

Person specification

To perform the role well, the Director must take a broad, corporate view, working closely with Executive colleagues and the College Board, and delegating effectively to a capable team. This is not a specialist role; it demands curiosity across the full breadth of policing, genuine enthusiasm for the profession, and the ability to explain complexity clearly to both expert and non‑expert audiences. When the role is being performed effectively, it results in strong engagement from stakeholders, confidence from across the policing system and clearer national leadership on operational standards.

A culture encouraging inclusion and diversity.

We also have a number of thriving staff networks that provide the opportunity for advice, support and to drive change. A place to get your voice heard, share experiences and challenge our working practices to ensure equality of opportunity for all.

Join our vessel crew and help support the important work that protects Scotland's seas and advances marine science.

The Marine Directorate is the Scottish Government's lead marine management organisation, bringing together scientific research, compliance, policy and management to support the sustainable use and protection of Scotland's marine environment. We are recruiting Seaman 1A positions to join our Marine Research Vessel fleet, working at sea as part of a professional onboard team that enables the successful delivery of scientific research programmes across Scottish waters.

As a Seaman 1A, you will play a key role in supporting deck, fishing and scientific operations aboard our research vessels, working closely with vessel officers, crew and scientific staff. Your contribution will help ensure the safe and effective operation of the vessel and the successful collection of the scientific data and evidence that underpins marine science, policy development and decision-making in Scotland.

This role will be based on-board MRV Scotia or MRV Alba na Mara, operating primarily in Scottish waters as part of a marine working pattern aligned to vessel operations.

Assist with the loading, stowing, deploying, recovery, discharging and the maintenance of fishing and science equipment.
Undertake all aspects of deck maintenance, including cleaning, painting, greasing, storing, ropework, etc as required by Commanding Officer or First Officer (Executive) and directed by CPO (Deck).
Operate deck machinery safely and equipment for mooring/lifting and fishing operations on the science vessel.
Watchkeeping duties as part of the bridge Watchkeeping team.
In port, quartermaster/nightwatchman duties, including security patrols.

Knowledge and application of safe working practices within a marine environment, ensuring compliance with relevant health and safety procedures.
Demonstrable experience of operating and handling Fast Rescue Craft (FRC) and/or Rigid Inflatable Boats (RIBs).
Recent experience of operating deck equipment such as davits, winches and cranes in support of marine operations.

A career in community payback gives you the power to make a positive impact on the lives of People on Probation as well as your community. People come from all walks of life to form one team in the Probation Service.    
It's all about supporting People on Probation on their journey and making your community a better place. Whether that's building benches or cleaning the streets, you're there because you genuinely want to help.   

If this sounds like you, apply now.

If you are successful in the recruitment process to join the Probation Service, your starting salary will be £28,064, Pro-Rata for Part-Time roles. 

On a typical day, you’ll spend up to 7 hours supervising a group at a Community Payback unpaid work placement.  Post holders may be required to undertake weekend working as part of their normal pattern of working.

Working pattern


The Community Payback supervisor role is accommodated to people on probation who work or have caring responsibilities. Community Payback projects run 7 days a week  therefore you will: work frequent weekends, and you may be asked to cover some evenings. You will be paid a higher rate of 50% for weekend days you do work. 


In this role, the pace of our work means that rest breaks don’t always happen in the standard way. When this happens, we make sure your wellbeing is looked after.


Your wellbeing really matters to us, so we want to be open about this from the outset. If you’re someone who enjoys a varied, active role where no two days are the same, this is a great environment to make a real difference while being fully supported.
The Probation Service offers the opportunity for annual pay progression through a Competency Based Framework (CBF), which if eligible, will see your pay increase. CBF is designed to enable you to move up through the pay band range as your competence grows.
New entrants are expected to join on the minimum of the pay band.
Probation Service also increase their pay band ranges annually in line with Civil Service Pay guidance, which will also apply an increase to band pay ranges where applicable.
Overview of the job
This is an operational role directly supervising work groups of offenders serving a community sentence. This may include driving service vehicles to transport people or equipment. The post holder will be responsible for all work site supervision tasks and will work with service users to ensure that all tasks are carried out to the best of their ability. This will include working alongside people to demonstrate good practice as necessary.

If you have held a Skilled Worker visa continuously, please raise this during your pre-employment checks and your eligibility will be assessed in accordance with the immigration rules and transitional provisions in place.

Community Payback Supervisors will work with a diverse mix of individuals, so it’s important that you’re empathetic, a good communicator and happy to take the lead.

Probation services officers can help make a real difference to peoples’ lives. It’s not always easy to help someone turn their life around, but it can be immensely rewarding.
We’re looking for empathetic, patient and resilient people to join us as probation services officers. As well as making a difference to others, the role offers plenty of on-the-job training and a real chance to build a career in the Probation Service.

Day-to-day, you’ll manage a caseload of offenders before and after sentence. About the job

Job description

Role: Permanent General Visitor 

Business: Office of Public Guardian (OPG) 

Location: Each candidate will be appointed to a specified core region and will be expected to undertake frequent travel throughout the region. We are recruiting for the following regions: 

North East Region to cover: Newcastle, Durham, Sunderland, Darlington, Cleveland 

Yorkshire Region to cover: York, Hull, Harrogate, Leeds, Wakefield 

East Anglia Region to cover: Peterborough, Norwich, Cambridge, Ipswich 

South West Region to cover: Bristol, Bath, Dorset, Bournemouth, Taunton 

South Wales Region to cover: Swansea, Cardiff, Newport 

Mid/North Wales Region to cover: Llandrindod, Llandudno, Shrewsbury 

Grade: Higher Executive Officer (HEO) 

Salary:  National minimum starting salary: £35,335 London minimum starting salary: £40,014 

Contract Type: Permanent 

Minimum Hours: 24 hours per week 

Organisational Overview 

The Office of the Public Guardian (OPG) protects people in England and Wales who may not have the mental capacity to make certain decisions for themselves, such as about their health and finance. We are an Executive Agency of the Ministry of Justice (MoJ), set up in 2007 following the introduction of the Mental Capacity Act of 2005. 

OPG is responsible for registering lasting powers of attorney (LPA) and enduring powers of attorney (EPA) and supervising deputies who are appointed by the Court of Protection. 

OPG is a fantastic place to work offering a range of development opportunities.  The OPG is a disability confident employer and is committed to developing a supportive and inclusive environment that reflects the diverse community we serve. 

OPG is currently delivering an ambitious transformation programme. This will change the way we provide services and help us meet the growing needs of our users, partners and our stakeholders. It will make sure our users experience a better level of support and will help us to respond to the changing needs of society. Transformation will ensure we can better support adults at risk and create high-quality services that are accessible and affordable. 

Team Overview 

Supervision and Investigation Services (SIS) sits within the Operations Directorate and supports the Public Guardian in carrying out their statutory functions. This includes supervising deputies and guardians to ensure they carry out legal duties, and investigating concerns about deputies, guardians and attorneys. 

Visitors play a vital role in this work by carrying out visits to clients, deputies, donors and attorneys, and other relevant parties. Visitors gather and assess information and provide clear, evidence-based reports containing their observations, findings and recommendations.   

As a Permanent General Visitor employed by OPG, you will undertake urgent, complex, high-priority and assurance work, often at short notice. You will also support quality and consistency across the wider visitor service through mentoring, knowledge sharing, peer support and service improvement activity. 

Are you passionate about supporting some of society’s most vulnerable people, including individuals who may lack mental capacity?
Do you enjoy working independently in a varied and fast-paced environment, managing complex work and collaborating with others to achieve positive outcomes?
Are you looking for an opportunity to share your expertise, influence positive change, and help shape the delivery of a high-quality visitor service? 

Duties and Responsibilities  

Independently organise and manage a varied caseload of visits to clients, donors, deputies, attorneys and other relevant people on behalf of OPG.
Undertake urgent, complex, high-priority and assurance visits, including work allocated at short notice, in line with operational priorities.
Plan visits efficiently across the geographical region, making effective use of available time and resources while meeting agreed performance expectations.
Gather, assess and analyse information and evidence through interviews, observation records and consultation with relevant professionals and other parties.
Prepare and submit timely, concise, evidence-based reports, ensuring that relevant issues are addressed and findings, observations and recommendations are presented accurately and objectively.
Identify and promptly escalate safeguarding concerns, immediate risks and other matters requiring urgent action in accordance with OPG procedures.
Liaise with deputies, attorneys, carers, family members, legal representatives, health and social care professionals, local authorities and other external organisations when gathering evidence and making recommendations.
Work collaboratively with the Visits Team, case managers, investigators and other colleagues to support effective case progression and the efficient delivery of the visitor service.
Maintain regular contact with independent visitors within the allocated region and contribute to mentoring, peer support, knowledge sharing and the promotion of consistent standards.
Contribute to quality assurance activity, including reviewing work and providing constructive feedback where required.
Maintain up-to-date knowledge of the Mental Capacity Act 2005, its Code of Practice, relevant safeguarding requirements and other legislative, policy or operational developments affecting the role.
Contribute to service improvement, working groups, training and relevant operational forums, sharing professional knowledge and identifying opportunities to improve quality, efficiency and consistency.
Undertake other duties commensurate with the responsibilities and grade of the post. 

Agreed Expectations 

This is a home-based role. Each successful candidate will be appointed to a specified core geographical region and will be expected to undertake frequent travel throughout that region. Travel outside of the region and to OPG office locations may also be required to meet business needs. 

Candidates must hold a full UK driving licence and have access to a vehicle that can be used for business purposes. 

Successful candidates will be expected to attend OPG offices, including Nottingham and Birmingham, for initial training and subsequently as required. This may involve overnight stays. 

Skills & Qualifications 

Essential Skills

Experience gained in a relevant field such as health, social care, law, finance, investigation, safeguarding or regulatory compliance.  
Knowledge and understanding of the Mental Capacity Act 2005, it’s principles and the supporting Code of Practice, or the ability to develop and apply this knowledge quickly.
Experience of interviewing, gathering information and assessing evidence in sensitive, complex or challenging circumstances.
Ability to communicate effectively and sensitively with people who may lack capacity, and with their families, representatives and professionals.
Experience of producing concise, accurate, objective and evidence-based reports within agreed timescales.
Ability to analyse information from a variety of sources, identify relevant risks and issues, and make clear, evidence-based recommendations.
Ability to work independently, use sound judgement and manage a complex and varied caseload with competing priorities.
Proficient in the use of standard Microsoft Office products.
A full UK driving licence. 

Desirable Skills 

The below criteria are desirable only. These will not be assessed throughout the recruitment process but will be used in the event of tied scores between candidates.

Experience of conducting Mental Capacity Assessments.
A relevant professional qualification or degree in an area such as law, social work, health, finance or regulatory practice.

Application process

 This recruitment will follow the Civil Service Success Profile process. Candidates will be expected to complete the following as part of the application: 

A CV detailing your career history. CV’s will be assessed against the essential skills above.
Statement of Suitability of no more than 1000 words, to demonstrate your experience against the essential skills required for this role.

At OPG we consider all applications on the basis of merit and want you to feel able to demonstrate your full potential whatever type of assessment is used. If you require any reasonable adjustments for any aspect of the selection process, do not hesitate to get in contact with us.

About the job
Job summary

On the Science and Engineering Fast Stream (SEFS), you will use your science and engineering skills to support government policy development and decision-making. The scheme is not designed to place you in roles based solely on your scientific or engineering experience; instead, you will be placed in roles where your skills strengthen and inform policy.

Society faces many challenges that science and engineering can help solve. The Civil Service needs talented, adaptable science and engineering leaders to deliver complex work that makes a difference to people across the UK. The government’s focus on science and innovation to drive the UK’s growth, prosperity and security highlights the vital role of scientists and engineers in decision-making. Their expertise helps ensure policy is informed by the best available evidence and that scientific advice is communicated clearly.

You might be a science or engineering graduate, an experienced postgraduate researcher, a professional from industry, or an existing civil servant with a technical background. Join the Science and Engineering Fast Stream and you’ll become part of a modern, vibrant community of professionals with a shared goal: improving outcomes for the public.

The specific towns and cities depend on the department you are posted to and its office locations. The Fast Stream evolves continually, so postings can vary from year to year.

As an indication, in 2026 new fast streamers were posted to government offices in the following regions: Greater London, North West, South West, West Midlands, and Yorkshire and the Humber.

On occasion, some individuals may need to move location. We aim to align postings with your preferences whenever possible; however, final decisions must support our wider business needs. Please note that Fast Streamers cannot choose their department or their specific role.

Job description

Over three years, you will complete a range of stretching but rewarding postings across the Civil Service. These could include supporting the MOD Chief Scientific Adviser, working on earth observation policy in DEFRA, or advising on materials in the Department of Business, Innovation, Science and Trade These postings are designed to broaden your experience and build your leadership capability, including in areas outside your previous technical specialism. The scheme also offers a unique interchange placement, which may include opportunities in local government, charities or the private sector.

Across your postings, you will help build and apply evidence so government can respond to major challenges such as climate change or sustainable housing. You might analyse complex datasets, model public health risks, or develop evidence to inform clean energy decisions. You may also help shape legislation and regulation, or work with industry on compliance with statutory requirements (for example, food safety standards or transport emissions).

You will draw on your scientific background to develop and communicate robust evidence, working with experts across government, academia and industry.

You will be passionate about science and engineering and, throughout the programme, you will advocate for the use of evidence in the Civil Service and help promote the Government Science and Engineering Profession.

As a future leader, you will be expected to lead work from an early stage, including (but not exclusively) technical work. This might involve managing research projects, or working with policy teams to develop solutions for ministers and senior officials. By acting as an intelligent customer, you could oversee technical delivery for programmes such as a major transport project or research into artificial intelligence. You will work strategically with academics, industry experts and delivery partners inside and outside government.

You may also contribute to horizon scanning to identify emerging trends and technologies, such as autonomous vehicles or genomics, and apply systems thinking to help address complex cross-government challenges. Your combination of technical expertise and leadership potential, and your ability to work in both technical and non-technical environments, will make you deployable across the Civil Service at the end of the programme. When you finish after three years, you may choose to specialise in a policy area and take on technical leadership roles, or apply your skills in policy or operational delivery, bringing fresh perspectives to teams. Alternatively, you may focus on leadership and management roles, while remaining affiliated to the profession and continuing to champion science and engineering across government.

Whatever path you take, the Science and Engineering Fast Stream will develop you into a confident and inspiring future leader, supporting our ambition to put science and engineering at the heart of government decision-making.

We expect you to have secured your postgraduate degree before you start the programme

GSR takes a scientific and tailored approach supported by bodies of knowledge and a range of research methods to inform, influence and provide robust and defensible decision-making at all levels.

About the job
Job summary

Position summary

The Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) is one of the government’s largest public service departments with a sizeable annual budget, serving over 20 million citizens.

The estate spans 1.4 million square metres across 800+ sites and supports around 78,000 colleagues.

Our vision includes DWP colleagues, supply chain, partners and, most fundamentally, the customers the Department exists to serve. They are the reason for our existence.​

We are responsible for the day-to-day operation of our vast Estate by managing a private sector supply chain that delivers essential services such as Security Guarding, Maintenance, Property and Leasehold Management, Construction, Cleaning and Facilities Management.

DWP Estates is not just about maintaining buildings - it’s about transformation. Our strategic goals include:

Transitioning to a smaller, more affordable, and adaptable estate to meet future needs
Investing in infrastructure through planned replacement works
Embedding sustainability in line with Government Greening Commitments (GGCs) 
Delivering cost-effective services while maintaining high standards
Creating a professional, best-in-class working culture across the Government Property profession

Our Estates strategy ambitions have been refreshed to take us through to 2030:

OPTIMISE: Continue to transition to a more affordable and adaptable DWP estate that creates productive environments
INVEST: Investment in an improved environment that better meets the needs of customers and colleagues and minimises service disruption
SUPPORT the drive for sustainability throughout DWP
DELIVER: Expertly deliver improving, cost-effective services for DWP
THRIVE: Continue to develop a working culture for DWP Estates that is best in class across government

There is no better time to join the award winning DWP Estates team.

Supporting the Lead Asset Surveyor and Investment Planning Lead your role will include the delivery of the Life Cycle Works (LCW) strategy, maintenance of the asset condition data, providing lifecycle planning, and providing technical support to operational and projects delivery teams, across a defined geographical region covering circa 100+ sites. 

The role will include management responsibility for technical review of reactive and remedial works orders, and support to the application and alignment to ISO 55001 with the aim of optimising the asset portfolio for DWP employees, customers and other stakeholders whilst at the same time maintaining the critical requirement of asset compliance.

Job description

You will play a key role in our department’s goal of improving the estate to provide a safer, more productive environment for staff and customers, whilst reducing the Department’s carbon footprint. You will support the delivery of the Department’s asset strategy commitments, working closely with the Service Delivery team and the national Facilities Management (FM) supply chain to optimise asset performance.

Important - This role involves extensive travel, a full UK motor car driving licence is therefore required. The successful applicant will have access to the provision of a fully funded hire car (including fuel costs) for site visits. Visits must be planned in blocks to enable best value for money.

Where your own car is used then it must be insured for business use (proof will be required). Currently the mileage rates when using your own vehicle are those published by HMRC (first 10,000 miles £0.55 pence per mile over this limit the rate drops to £0.25 pence per mile. Rates subject to change.

** The successful candidate will cover the whole of London & the South East. You can be based in any location with available space within these regions ONLY **

Government Property Profession Career Framework (Link)

 This role sits within the following:

Job Family – Strategic Asset Management
Core Role – Property Data Management
Level – Practitioner

Key accountabilities

Support the Lead Asset Surveyor and Investment Planning Lead (LCW/Surveying) in the delivery of the Asset Management Strategy for the Estates property portfolio.
Maintains knowledge and understanding of all building fabric and M&E assets and asset condition, through interaction operational estates functions and surveys and site visits.
Shadow third party surveyors conducting asset collection surveys across the estate to ensure defined protocols for surveying are being followed.
Review and validate third party asset validation reports and provide technical feedback including submitting asset change requests where applicable.
Provide technical assurance on maintenance Work Order system, reviewing proposals for maintenance / upgrading works and providing technical advice where applicable.
Provide Quality Assurance reviews of survey data.
Provide technical review of Forward Maintenance Register.
Review contractors proposals for compliance with DWP Design Standards.
Collaborates with colleagues in the Asset Management team to identify poor performing assets, repeat failures and obsolete assets for review/inclusion in the LCW planning process.
Maintains asset condition data and LCW maintenance register ‘Demand Plan’ by undertaking periodic condition surveys across a geographical area of responsibility containing circa 100+ sites.
Undertakes prioritisation of LCW Demand in accordance with predetermined criticality, performance and condition criteria.
Contributes to the development of the LCW pipeline plan, understanding limitations of budget, portfolio strategy, and delivery capacity.
Develop project scopes and total budget costs for inclusion in the LCW planning process.
Supports the DWP Projects Delivery Team in the delivery of the LCW programme, with internal ‘Client’ responsibility for delivery of LCW projects within geographical region.
Fosters a ‘one team’ culture of quality and continuous improvement across the extended organisation to include the Integrator and supplier partners, on a day to day as well as strategic basis.
Supports the management of assets and development of asset strategies, within a large portfolio, in support of achieving defined Sustainability and Net Zero Carbon objective.
Supporting DWP occupation by performing surveying duties as required.
Supports and deputises for the Lead Surveyor and Investment Planning Lead as required.
Person specification

Essential Skills, Knowledge & Experience

Significant experience of asset condition surveying within a large commercial property portfolio.
Extensive and detailed technical knowledge of building pathology and asset lifecycle management within diverse range of portfolios (Corporate, multi occupied, public facing)
Has surveyed and planned lifecycle work programs on large property portfolios.
Up to date knowledge of the legislation, best practice and industry standards in relation to providing a safe, sustainable and compliant Estate.
In depth knowledge of building asset types, their significance on legal compliance and improvements needed to support the Department’s commitment to Net Zero Carbon and Greening Government Commitments.
Understanding of end-to-end commercial construction project delivery process.
Commercial awareness and astuteness connected with contractual obligations and interpretation with supply chain partners.
Extensive experience of defining project scopes, estimating project costs, asset surveying and the use of CIBSE asset condition classifications.
Ability to analyse significant amounts of data produced by computer aided facilities management systems supporting a large portfolio and identify opportunities or risk for the department.
Strong project management skills and persuasive in identifying key areas of work required.
Experienced of working with multiple stakeholders across a multi-site estate.
Ability to travel frequently to perform site visits and surveying duties across geographical region, including overnight stays where appropriate.

Qualifications/professional memberships

Desirable

Degree qualified with a core competency in either Building Surveying or Building Services and will be expected to have a good knowledge of the complimentary asset management requirements of each discipline.
MRICS, CIBSE or similar or working towards certification

full UK motor car driving licence

DWP have a broad benefits package built around your work-life balance which includes:

Working patterns to support work/life balance such as job sharing, term-time working, flexi-time and compressed hours.
Generous annual leave – at least 23 days on entry, increasing up to 30 days over time (pro–rata for part time employees), plus 9 days public and privilege leave.
Support for financial wellbeing, including interest-free season ticket loans for travel, a cycle to work scheme and an employee discount scheme.

Funded learning and development to support progress in your role and career. This includes industry recognised qualifications and accreditations, coaching, mentoring and talent development programmes.

Selection process details
This vacancy is using Success Profiles (opens in a new window), and will assess your Behaviours, Strengths and Experience.

STAGE 1 - APPLICATION & SIFT

As part of the application process you will be asked to provide a Personal Statement of no more than 1000 words against the essential criteria as outlined above. You will also be asked to provide a short CV.

Your CV should be fairly short and just evidence very brief details of your work history and Qualifications.

While your CV is not formally scored it will be used to validate the evidence of your Personal Statement.

Please do not submit a speculative application where you do not meet at least 50% of the essential criteria as these applications will be unsuccessful. Do not include Behaviour examples within your application as these will not be assessed in the sift and will only be used at interview stage.

Further details around what this will entail are listed on the application form.

There will be an initial sift of applications based on the Personal Statement only, so please ensure you evidence how you meet the Essential Skills, Knowledge & Experience requirement contained in the vacancy in this section. This will form a short list for interview.

STAGE 2 - INTERVIEW

All candidates who are successful at the sift stage will undertake a single virtual video interview.

There, you will be assessed against the experiences listed in the essential criteria.

You will also be asked additional questions to validate your knowledge which will be measured against the essential criteria as specified in the vacancy. Your will also be asked some Behaviour & Strength questions.

Currently the sift is scheduled to take place w/c 9th November 2026 and interview dates w/c 23rd November 2026 . Interviews are scheduled to take place virtually and dates are subject to change.

Further Information

Important Information – Visa Sponsorship

For these vacancies, we strongly recommend that applicants consult with an immigration specialist or qualified advisor to assess their eligibility for Visa Sponsorship before deciding to apply. Please note that while we consider sponsorship requests in accordance with current DWP guidance and Home Office policy, sponsorship cannot be guaranteed.

Hybrid Working

This role may be suitable for hybrid working, which is where an employee works part of the week in their DWP office and part of the week from home. This is a voluntary, non-contractual arrangement and your office will be your contractual place of work.

If a hybrid working arrangement is suitable for the role and for you, you will normally be required to spend a minimum of 60% of your contracted working hours from your DWP office.

Integrity, plagiarism and Civil Service Principles

The Civil Service values honesty and integrity and expects all candidates to abide by these principles.

Job description

Senior Probation Officer Returner Scheme

This is a rolling campaign; applicants cannot reapply within a six-month period.

This scheme is open to former, qualified senior probation officers who have left the Civil Service within the last five years.

If you are a former qualified senior probation officer who has left the Civil Service less than 5 years ago, and have completed your probationary period and training, we would like you to consider returning to the Probation Service and joining your former colleagues, to keep the public safe and rehabilitate people on probation. 

Should you meet the eligibility criteria, and your application is accepted by the Probation Service, we can offer you a fast-track return to the service with no requirement to undertake a lengthy application form, interview and repeat any entry level training or assessment process.

When considering applications, we take into account a range of relevant factors such as business need, location availability and any previous employment history.

We will contact you to discuss your potential work base location, subject to passing pre-employment checks.

Please note: Former civil servants do not have the right to return. It is at the discretion of the Probation Service whether to reinstate former civil servants. This Returners Scheme utilises Exception 5 of the Recruitment Principles, which provides a mechanism for former civil servants to return, without necessarily going through fair and open competition again.

Further information can be found here: Home - Civil Service Commission (independent.gov.uk)

If you have left the service more than 5 years ago, please visit Current vacancies – Prison and Probation Jobs for all our current vacancies.

If you are not yet ready to re-join at this time, you can still be part of our Probation Alumni Network to be kept up date on the latest developments for probation returners. Click here to register to the Probation Alumni Network.

NB: The Probation Alumni Network is for Probation and Senior Probation Officer roles.

Eligibility:

Job summary

What you’ll do…

As the largest land manager in the country, Forestry England oversees a vast and diverse network of more than 1,500 forests and woods, spanning over 250,000 hectares. We often celebrate our landscapes for their natural beauty and ecological significance, yet they also harbour some of England’s most extraordinary historical sites, monuments, and stories. Beneath the leafy canopies and towering trees lies a rich tapestry of human history, preserved and intertwined with the very roots of the land.

As Heritage Mapping and Data Officer, you will support the collection, analysis, management, and ethical use of historic environment data across the biodiversity program. You will work directly with historic environment advisors well as other national and area teams, and external partners to ensure project data is appropriately collated, processed and managed.

You will establish and follow data standards, frameworks, and workflows, supporting the effective use of spatial, environmental, and heritage datasets. The role includes data governance, quality assurance, and compliance, contributing to reporting and evaluation, and identifying opportunities to improve data integration, insight, and long-term value, including through innovation and future funding opportunities.

Please see the job description below for more information and details about what we need from you.

Where you’ll work…

The postholder will be part of the Environment & Nature Recovery Team in National Operations, managed by the Lead Historic Environment Advisor, but can be based out of any of our regional offices, with hybrid working also possible.

Job description
Key responsibilities & accountabilities 
 
• Lead in the development of a new historic environment data management approach. 
• Support the mapping of archaeological sites and monuments identified with Lidar and arial imagery. 
• Yearly request Historic Environment Records data for the Nation’s Forests. 
• Manage and maintain national heritage datasets, ensuring accuracy, consistency, and alignment with 
organisational standards. Collaborate with district teams to resolve anomalies, and lead the integration of 
new data sources, including new surveys and Historic Environment Records, into internal systems. 
• Support the cleaning and conversion of survey data. 
• Assist with reporting. 
• Champion the use of evidence in decision-making, drawing on best practice. 
• Lead the integration of emerging technologies such as AI into team policy and practice, to help make 
better evidence-based decisions. 
• Identify stories and narratives with the data you work with that can be used to engage the public. 
• Lead the development and guidance of historic environment data within internal GIS systems. 
And any other tasks, reasonably requested by your line manager.
Person specification

Skills, knowledge & experience 

Essential professional and technical experience 

• Strong understanding of archaeological monitoring techniques. 
• A strong team player. 
• Good knowledge of spatial data and GIS. 
• Experience working with external partners. 
• Experience in heritage data management, remote sensing mapping and survey recording for historic 
environment purposes. 
• Ability to use a range of GIS and database software packages, including esri. 
• Excellent problem-solving and communication skills, with the ability to work collaboratively across teams. 
 
Desirable professional and technical experience 

• Understanding of landscape archaeology 
• understanding of technical forestry, land management and countryside recreation. 
• experience working in a historic environment or similar outdoor settings. 
• Experience working on landscape scale heritage mapping projects 
• Knowledge of ARCHES data management system

Job summary

Do you have substantial senior leadership experience with a track record of leading corporate Governance, Planning and Performance?

Are you able to translate organisational strategy into coherent business plans?

If so, this is an exciting opportunity to join the Food Standards Agency (FSA) as our Deputy Director of Governance, Planning and Performance, and we’d love to hear from you!

The FSA is a non-ministerial department of over 1600 people. We play a critical role in protecting public health and consumers’ wider interests in food across England, Wales and Northern Ireland. Our vision is an important one - to drive change, delivering “food you can trust” and working towards a healthier and more sustainable food system.

Job description

This is a new senior leadership role at the heart of the Food Standards Agency, offering the opportunity to strengthen how the organisation makes decisions, delivers its priorities and demonstrates accountability. As Deputy Director of Governance, Planning and Performance, you will bring together governance, planning, performance, risk, and audit, into a coherent organisational approach.

Working across the Agency, you will provide trusted advice to the Chief Executive, Chair, Board and the Executive Management Team (EMT). Through visible and inclusive leadership of a multidisciplinary division, you will help create the structures, insight and accountability needed to support the Agency’s mission of food you can trust.

You will oversee corporate reporting, risk management, business planning, Private Office and senior Committee Secretariat services. You will lead the production and review of the Agency’s annual and multi-year plans, working with finance, people and strategy colleagues to ensure that priorities are ambitious, deliverable and supported by effective performance measures.

You will provide senior oversight of assurance and performance information, delivering high-quality challenge and data-led insight to senior boards. You will resolve complex delivery issues through collaboration and influence, build productive relationships across the wider Civil Service and promote continuous improvement. You will also line manage senior functional leaders, develop organisational capability and ensure workloads and resources are managed effectively.

This is a Faith/Belief specific advert for a Pagan faith and belief advisor Only
Delegates will be required to do a 10 minute presentation at Interview Stage

Job Title     HMPPS Faith and Belief Adviser 
Directorate     Central Operational Services 
Band     8 
 
Overview of the job      

The job holder will be a senior representative of their faith or belief system who will report to the Chaplain General and Head of Faith Services. They will provide prison and probation related advice for their respective faith or belief system as well as advice and guidance on the rehabilitation and resettlement of offenders on release into the community and those serving community sentences.  

This is a non-operational role with line management responsibilities 

Summary      

To provide considered and informed faith and belief system related advice within a prison context for their respective tradition whether this is for staff or the men, women and children in custody. 
 
With Probation Service colleagues provide advice on the successful reintegration of offenders into the community following their release from custody, of those under Probation Service supervision to lead law-abiding lives and thereby reduce future victims of crime. 
 
The post holder will be responsible for ensuring the faith and belief systems’ needs for their respective tradition are met, for providing support to the chaplains of their tradition and for relations with their respective faith or belief system organisations. 
 
Developing and implementing a strategy for the recruitment and retention of the respective chaplains in conjunction with HMPPS Chaplaincy and Faith Services (CFS) and MoJ People Group. 
 
To collaborate with and support CFS in the delivery of chaplaincy services. 

Responsibilities, Activities and Duties      

The job holder will be required to carry out the following responsibilities, activities and duties: 
 
• Provide prison related advice and on the rehabilitation and resettlement of offenders on release into the community and potentially longer term support, those under Probation 
Supervision for their respective faith or belief system, working with CFS on the delivery of Prison Service Instruction 05/2016 Faith and Pastoral Care for Prisoners (and successor documents), related policy guidance while mindful of financial and human resources and to contribute to related Departmental and Ministerial priorities. 
•    Supporting Chaplains, CFS, Prison Group Directors (PGDs), Governors/Directors and other stakeholders, ensuring advice is provided in a timely and appropriate manner. 
•    Be proactive in the recruitment of Chaplains from the post holder’s faith or belief system through maintaining links with their respective organisation/ structures and following up interest from prospective applicants. 
•    Advise establishments on matters relating to recruitment, advising HMPPS on their respective faith and belief systems and the recruitment of their respective Chaplains.  
•    Endorse or facilitate the endorsement of their respective Chaplains. 
•    Line management responsibility for their respective Chaplains who work across multiple sites in conjunction with the establishments the Chaplains serve. 
•    As far as possible, and in conjunction with local support systems, enable pastoral care and professional support for Chaplains. 
•    With the prior agreement of the Chaplain General, work with Chaplains of their faith and belief system from other sectors, e.g. health, armed forces, higher education, on matters of common interest. 
•    Liaising with the Chaplain General and other Faith and Belief Advisers in their development of tools to enable theological engagement and reflection by Chaplains from across the faith traditions represented within prison chaplaincy and to explore how these may enable dialogue between prisoners of different faith and belief systems. 
•    Be a member of the Chaplaincy Faith and Belief Advisory Committee and work collaboratively with other members, sharing information, experience and with colleagues and where appropriate senior management. 
 
The duties/responsibilities listed above describe the post as it is at present and is not intended to be exhaustive. The job holder is expected to accept reasonable alterations and additional tasks of a similar level that may be necessary. Significant adjustments may require re-examination under the Job Evaluation Scheme and shall be discussed in the first instance with the job holder. 
 
An ability to fulfil all spoken aspects of the role with confidence through the medium of English or (where specified in Wales) Welsh.

The Role

Please note this role requires you to pass Security Check clearance. Please click on the link for details.

We’re recruiting for Senior Developers here at Justice Digital, Data and Science to be part of our warm and collaborative HMPPS team.

This role aligns against Senior Developer from the Government Digital and Data Framework

You’ll be confident working with other developers on our tech stack and comfortable learning new technologies and systems. We use a variety of different technologies and will work with you to place you in a team that matches your skills, interests and aspirations wherever possible.

As a Senior Developer, you could be working on projects such as:

Improving how prison visits are scheduled and managed.
Building digital services that help Probation staff support rehabilitation and prepare cases for court.
Designing services that manage identity data safely and accurately across prisons and probation.
Modernising legacy systems used by frontline staff, making them easier to use, maintain and improve.
Building APIs and shared services that allow information to move safely between different parts of the justice system.
Automating manual processes so staff can spend less time on administration and more time supporting people in prison and on probation.

You will work in multidisciplinary teams with user researchers, product managers, designers, delivery managers, technical architects and content specialists who share a vision for improving government through smarter use of technology.

Our Tech Stack

We use a range of modern technologies, and we’re looking for developers with strong experience in one or more of them, as well as an enthusiasm for learning new languages, tools and frameworks.

Our services are commonly built using Kotlin and Node.js. We use GitHub Actions for CI/CD, tools including Application Insights, Grafana and Sentry for application monitoring and observability, and Docker and Kubernetes to package and run our services. Much of our infrastructure runs on AWS, supported by the Ministry of Justice Cloud Platform.

For web interfaces, we use the GOV.UK Design System and MOJ Design System and place a strong emphasis on accessible, user-centred services.

For front-end development, we value a strong understanding of the underlying web technologies. We favour well-maintained, open-source tools and aim to produce semantic HTML, performant CSS, and maintainable, unobtrusive JavaScript or TypeScript. Accessibility is a core part of how we design, build and assess our services.

You don’t need to have used exactly the same technologies as us. We’re happy to help you learn our stack, and we’re more interested in strong engineering fundamentals and your ability to pick up new technologies. For more detail on our tech stack, look at the MoJ Technical Radar.

You can explore the Ministry of Justice GitHub organisation to see examples of the services we build and maintain.

We work in agile, multidisciplinary teams and follow the principles of the Manifesto for Agile Software Development.

Our developers are provided with MacBook Pros for their day-to-day work.

Our Community

You’ll be joining a large and supportive engineering community across the Ministry of Justice, with developers working on services used throughout prisons, probation and the wider justice system.

As a Senior Developer, you’ll help coach and mentor other developers, share your knowledge, and contribute to communities of practice across MoJ. We encourage developers to get involved beyond their immediate team through technical discussions, talks, meet-ups, open-source projects and shared engineering initiatives.

We take supportive and effective line management seriously. We’ll value the experience and skills you bring, while helping you develop further through coaching, learning opportunities and exposure to different teams and technologies.

As your career develops, there are opportunities to move between teams, take on different technical challenges and progress into roles with greater technical or leadership responsibility.

To get a feel for how we work, take a look at the Ministry of Justice Developer Portal or the Justice Digital blog.

You’ll receive a range of excellent benefits when you join our department, including:

A generous employer pension contribution of 28.97% through the Civil Service Pension Scheme.
25 days of annual leave, (increasing to 30 days once you have reached 5 years of service), plus 8 bank holidays and a privilege day for the King’s birthday.
Flexible working arrangements including hybrid working, working part time or compressed hours. Designed to support a positive work–life balance.
Employees are allocated 10% of their working time for personal and professional development.
A £1k per person learning budget is in place to support all our people, with access to best-in-class conferences and seminars, accreditation with professional bodies, fully funded vocational programmes and e-learning platforms.
Compassionate maternity, adoption, and shared parental leave policies, with up to 26 weeks leave at full pay, 13 weeks with partial pay, and 13 weeks further leave. And maternity support/paternity leave at full pay for 2 weeks, too!

You can find more details of the Benefits we offer here. To help picture your life at MoJ Justice Digital, Data and Science please take a look at our blog.

Key Responsibilities:

As a Senior Software Developer at the MoJ, you’ll combine hands-on technical work with supporting and developing the people around you.

Technical responsibilities

Designing, building and maintaining secure APIs, services and systems
Working collaboratively on existing codebases, helping to understand and improve them over time
Improving the resilience, reliability and maintainability of our software

Supporting people and teams

Supporting the development of others through line management, coaching and mentoring
Working closely with Lead Developers and colleagues to create supportive, effective teams
Sharing knowledge and creating opportunities for others to learn and grow
Helping to build and sustain a diverse, inclusive and welcoming development community, where different perspectives are valued

If this sounds like work you’d enjoy and you’re interested in joining a supportive development community, we’d love to hear from you.

About the job
